questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements with reference to the evolution of geography as a subject are incorrect?

answerOptions.text: The term Geography was first coined by a Greek scholar Eratosthenes.
The subject matter of discipline has been taken from Natural sciences.
Geography can be considered as the study of Areal Differentiation over Earth.
Geography cannot be used to describe phenomenon on the Earth with a cause and effect relationship.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) is incorrect with reference to the
evolution of geography as a subject because geography
can be used to describe phenomenon on the Earth with
a cause and effect relationship.
Geographers do not only study the variations in the
phenomena over the Earth’s surface (space) but also
study the associations with the other factors which
cause these variations.

questions.question:
(Chap
1, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 1994)

Which of the following pairs is/are matched correctly? 
1. Neo Determinism – Griffith Taylor
2. Determinism – E Huntington
3. Possibilism – Vidal De La Blache
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the pairs are correctly matched as Griffith
Taylor gave the concept of Neo Determinism also
known as ‘Stop and Go Determinism’.
Determinism can be defined as naturalisation of
humans. E Huntington was one of the pioneers of this
approach.
Vidal De La Blache was a pioneer of possibilism along
with Lucian Febre. Possibilism means humanisation
of nature.

“Human geography is concerned with the study of changing relationship between unresting man and unstable Earth.” Who gave this statement about human geography?

answerOptions.rationale:
The statement about human geography was given
by Ellen Semple.
According to Ellen Semple “Human geography is the

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

The state of universe before the occurrence of the ‘Big Bang’ can correctly described by which of the following terms?

answerOptions.rationale:
The term ‘Singularity’ correctly describes the state
of universe before the occurrence of the ‘Big Bang’.
According to the ‘Big Bang’ theory (expanding universe
hypothesis) in the beginning, all matter forming the
universe existed in one place in the form of a ‘tiny ball’
(singular atom) with an unimaginably small volume,
infinite temperature and infinite density. This existence
was termed as singularity. At the Big Bang, the ‘tiny
ball’ exploded violently, this led to a huge expansion of
the universe.

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:

because the most popular argument about the origin of

this argument, he provided evidence that the universe is
expanding and galaxies are moving a part with the
passage of time.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement is/are not correct about the state of early universe?

answerOptions.text: The distribution of matter and energy was not even.
Differences in the density led to differences in gravitational forces.
Galaxies started forming by the accumulation of a large cloud of hydrogen gas.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct about the
state of early universe. The distribution of matter and
energy was not even in the early universe. This initial
density differences gave rise to differences in
gravitational forces and it caused the matter to get
drawn together.
Hence, galaxies started forming by the accumulation of
a large cloud of hydrogen gas.
A galaxy contains a large number of stars. Galaxies
spread over vast distances are measured in thousands of
light years. The diameters of individual galaxies range
from 80,000-1,50,000 light years.

years ago.
Codes
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3
(c) 1, 3 and 4 (d) 1, 2, 3 and 4

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which among the following statements can be
considered as definitely true about the planets in Solar System?
1. The asteroids are revolving around the Sun between the orbits of terrestrial planets and Jovian planets.
2. The terrestrial planets in the Solar System are much smaller than the Jovian planets.
3. The atmosphere of Jovian planets is made up of oxygen and argon.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are considered as definitely
true about the planets in Solar System because out of
the eight planets, Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are
called as the inner planets as they lie between the Sun
and the belt of asteroids.
The other four planets are called the outer planets.
Alternatively, the first four are called terrestrial,
meaning earth-like as they are made up of rock and
metals, and have relatively high densities.
The rest four are called Jovian or gas giant planets.
Jovian means Jupiter-like, most of them are much
larger than the terrestrial planets.
Statement (3) is false because the atmosphere of Jovian
planets is made up of helium and hydrogen.

Which of the following factors have contributed to the formation of terrestrial rocky planets?
1. Closeness to the parent star
2. Solar winds
3. Higher gravity

Protoplanets are small celestial objects that are the size

Planetoid is another term for asteroids. It is also known

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following statements are correct about the Earth in its primitive form?
1. It was a cloud of dust and gases in its initial stages.
2. All the gases were concentrated in the core of Earth.
3. Life was present on the land in initial stages.
4. It took 4,600 million years in formation of Earth.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (4) are correct about the Earth in
its primitive form because the Sun is surrounded by solar
nebula (a giant cloud) containing mostly, hydrogen and
helium along with dust. It took around 4,600 million years
for the evolution of life on the surface of the planet Earth.
Planet Earth initially was a barren, rocky and hot object
with a thin atmosphere of hydrogen and helium. Hence,
life was not present on the land in initial stages.
Statements (2) and (3) are incorrect as the Earth was mostly
in a volatile state during its primordial stage. Due to
gradual increase in density, the temperature inside the
Earth increased. As a result, the material inside the Earth
started getting separated depending on their densities.
There are no traces of life to be present on the land in
initial stages.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The stages of formation of the Earth are given in the options given below. Arrange the stages in a correct sequence and choose the correct answer using the codes given below.
1. Formation of ridges and basins
2. Swirling ball of dust and clouds
3. Formation of crust of the Earth
4. Floating of gases to form atmosphere
5. Formation of oceans
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Option (b) is the correct sequence. At the
beginning, Earth was a giant ball of dust and cloud
known as Nebula.
After that, through the process of accretion, the planet
Earth started to form. This process allowed heavier
materials (like iron) to sink towards the centre of the
Earth and the lighter ones to move towards the surface.
The crust started to form along with ridges and basins.
In the next stage, the Earth’s atmosphere started to
form with floating gases and at last after 500 million
years from the formation of the Earth, the oceans
started to form.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which among the following is the earliest theory to describe the formation of Earth?

answerOptions.rationale:
Earliest theory to describe the formation of Earth
is known as Nebular Hypothesis. A large number of
hypotheses were put forth by different philosophers
and scientists regarding the origin of the Earth. One of
the earlier and popular arguments was given by
German philosopher Immanuel Kant.
Mathematician Laplace revised it in 1796 and named as
Nebular Hypothesis. Both Big Bang and Expanding
Universe Hypothesis are related to the origin of
universe and Steady State Hypothesis state that the
density of matter in the expanding universe remains
unchanged over time because of the continuous creation
of matter.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

According to the early theories of Earth formation, the accretion of, which of the following materials led to the formation of planet Earth?

answerOptions.rationale:
According to the early theories of Earth formation,
the accretion of hydrogen and helium gases led to the
formation of planet Earth. They initially formed the
Earth’s surface. The early atmosphere with hydrogen
and helium is supposed to have been stripped off as a
result of intense solar wind. This happened not only in
Earth, but also in all the terrestrial planets, which were
supposed to have lost their primordial atmosphere
through the impact of solar winds.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Earth’s revolution around the sun?
1. The Earth’s movement around the Sun in its orbit is called revolution.
2. The Earth’s revolution is responsible for occurrence of leap year on Earth.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding Earth’s revolution around the sun.
The Earth’s movement around the Sun in its orbit is
called revolution. It takes 365 1/4 days (one year) to
revolve around the Sun. We consider it a year, as
consisting of 365 days only and ignore six hours for the
sake of convenience. Six hours saved every year are
added to make one day (24 hours) over a span of four
years.
This surplus day is added to the month of February.
Thus, every fourth year, February is of 29 days instead
of 28 days. Such a year with 366 days is called a leap
year. Thus, the Earth’s revolution is responsible for
occurrence of leap year on Earth.

2. The Earth rotates from West to East.
3. Revolution of Earth on its tilted axis causes formation of seasons.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about the revolution
of Earth. The Earth takes 365¼ days (one year) to
revolve around the Sun in an elliptical orbit.
The Earth rotates on its own axis and it rotates in the
Eastward direction and in a counter-clockwise motion.
So, the direction of the Earth’s rotation is considered
from West to East.
The revolution of Earth on its tilted axis causes
formation of seasons because change of seasons is the
result of changing in the position of the Earth around
the Sun.

Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4.
21st June, the Southern Hemisphere experiences On the
winter season and it is summer in the Northern
hemisphere. At that point of time, the position of the
Earth on 21st June is called the Summer Solstice.
On 22nd December, the Tropic of Capricorn receives
direct rays of the Sun as the South Pole tilted towards it.
As the Sun’s rays fall vertically at the Tropic of
Capricorn, a larger portion of the Southern Hemisphere
gets light. This position of the Earth is called the Winter
Solstice.
On 23rd September, direct rays of the Sun fall on the
equator. This is called an equinox. At this time, it is
autumn season in the Northern Hemisphere and spring
season in the Southern Hemisphere. It is called as
Autumn Equinox.
21st March is opposite case on 21st March, when it is
spring in the Northern Hemisphere and autumn in the
Southern Hemisphere. It is also known as Spring
Equinox.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

On which of the following days, the length of day and night on the North Pole and South Pole will be exactly same?

answerOptions.rationale:
On 21st March, the length of day and night on the
North Pole and South Pole will be exactly same. During
the spring and autumn equinoxes, i.e., on 21st March
and 23rd September, the Sun is exactly overhead the
Equator and the North and South Poles lie at an equal
distance from the Sun. This is the reason, days and
nights are of equal length throughout the world on
these two days.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VI, New NCERT)

The rotation of Earth in its elliptical orbit causes seasons on Earth. Seasons differ in both the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere. Which of the following statements about the seasons in Southern and Northern Hemispheres is/are correct?
1. In the month of September, the Southern Hemisphere has spring season.
2. In the month of June, the Northern Hemisphere has summer season.
3. In the month of December, the Southern Hemisphere has winter season.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct about the
seasons in Southern and Northern Hemisphere.
As on 21st March and 23rd September, direct rays of the
Sun fall on the equator. At this position, neither of the
poles is tilted towards the Sun; so, the whole Earth
experiences equal days and equal nights. On 23rd
September, it is autumn season in the Northern
Hemisphere and spring season in the Southern
Hemisphere.
Also in Northern Hemisphere, the longest day and the
shortest night take places on 21st June. Hence, we can
conclude that in the month of June, the Northern
Hemisphere has summer season.
Statement (3) is incorrect as in the month of December,
the Southern Hemisphere has summer season while the
Northern Hemisphere has winter season.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect about the Summer Solstice?

answerOptions.text: The North Pole of Earth has 24 hours daylight.
The South Pole has 24 hours night.
The Northern Hemisphere has autumn season.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect about the summer
solstice because on 21st June, the Northern
Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun. The rays of
the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer. As a
result, these areas receive more heat. The areas near
the poles receive less heat as the rays of the Sun are
slanting.
Since, a large portion of the Northern Hemisphere is
getting light from the Sun, it is summer in the north

answerOptions.text: The Southern Hemisphere has winter season.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VI, New NCERT)

The Winter Solstice occurs on 22nd December. During Winter Solstice, which of the following phenomenon can be observed in the Southern Hemisphere?
1. The length of days will be longer in the Southern Hemisphere.
2. Southern Hemisphere experiences winter season.
3. The South Pole has 24 hours day for 6 months.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Phenomena mentioned in Statements (1) and (3)
can be observed in the Southern Hemisphere.
During Winter Solstice, the length of days will be
longer in the Southern Hemisphere and the South Pole
has 24 hours day for 6 months. This is because on 22nd
December, the Tropic of Capricorn receives direct rays
of the Sun as the South Pole tilts towards it.
Therefore, it is summer in the Southern Hemisphere
with longer days and shorter nights. This position of the
Earth is called the Winter Solstice.
Phenomenon mentioned in statement (2) cannot be
observed as during this time Southern Hemisphere
experiences summer season and Northern Hemisphere
experiences winter season.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

During certain period of the year, the rays of the Sun are falling directly over the Tropic of Cancer (23 1/2° N). Which of the following is most likely to occur during this period?

answerOptions.text: Northern Hemisphere will have longer days and shorter nights.
There will be 24 hour day on the North Pole.
The length of days and nights will be equal at all places.

answerOptions.rationale:
During the period mentioned in question,
Northern Hemisphere will have longer days and
shorter nights. Also there will be 24 hour day on the
North Pole because on 21st June when the rays of the
Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer, Northern
Hemisphere receive more heat. Since, a large portion
of the Northern Hemisphere is getting light from the
Sun, it is summer in the regions North of the equator
with longer days and shorter nights.
Statement (c) is incorrect because during this time, days
are longer in Northern Hemisphere and nights are
shorter but in Southern Hemisphere all these conditions
are reversed. Thus, the length of days and nights are
equal at all places when the rays of the Sun are falling
directly over the Tropic of Cancer.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following statements are incorrect about the rotation of Earth on its tilted axis?
1. The Earth’s rotation on its tilted axis is responsible for causing seasons on Earth.
2. If the Earth stops rotating, all the places will have equal days and equal nights.
3. Earth’s rotates at an axial tilt of 23 1/2° from the plane of Earth’s orbit.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All of the statements are incorrect about the
rotation of Earth on its tilted axis. The revolution of
Earth around the Sun is responsible for causing seasons
on Earth.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements can be
considered as certainly true about the Moon?

answerOptions.text: The diameter of Moon is one-fifth of the Earth.
A person on Earth will always see the same side of the Moon.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) can be considered as certainly true
about the moon because Earth has only one satellite,
i.e., the Moon. Its diameter is only one-quarter to that
of the Earth.
It appears so big because it is nearer to our planet than
other celestial bodies. It is about 3,84,400 km away from
us. It revolves around the Earth and rotates about its
own axis in about the same time, due to, which only one
side of the Moon is visible to us. Water and soil are not
present on the Moon. Hence, the Moon does not have
favourable conditions for life.

answerOptions.text: The revolution period of Moon is more than the rotation period.
Water and soil are present in abundant quantities on Moon.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the Moon. 
1. The Moon revolves around the Earth in a fixed path.
2. The Moon appears bright due to reflected light of the Sun.
3. The surface of Moon is characterised by unevenness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about the moon
because it revolves around the Earth and rotates about
its own axis in about the same time.
The Moon does not have its own light; it gets its light
from the Sun so, the Moon appears bright due to
reflected light of the Sun. The surface of Moon is
characterised by unevenness as it has mountains, plains
and depressions on its surface. These cast shadows on
the Moon’s surface.

questions.question:

Which one of the following longitudes alongwith the Prime Meridian forms a great circle on the globe?

answerOptions.rationale:
180° longitudes alongwith the Prime Meridian
forms a great circle on the globe. The Prime Meridian
is the zero degree line of longitude that passes near
London.
It forms a great circle at globe at 180°. The Prime
Meridian was accepted as zero degrees longitude at an
International Conference in 1884.

Zero degree latitude and zero degree longitude lies in the

Areas lying between the Arctic Circle and the North

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the meridians of longitude on Earth.
1. All the meridians of longitude are of same length.
2. Prime Meridian is marked by 0° longitude.
3. All the meridians are full circles.
4. Distance between longitudes becomes zero at the poles.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct about the
meridians of longitude on Earth. The line of reference
running from the North Pole to the South Pole are
called the meridians of longitude.
Unlike parallels of latitude, all meridians are of equal
length. The Prime Meridian is the imaginary line used to
indicate 0° longitude that passes through Greenwich. It is
also known as Greenwich Meridian because it passes
through the place called Greenwich in London.
The distances between them are measured in ‘degrees
of longitude’. Each degree is further divided into
minutes, and minutes into seconds.
Statement (3) is incorrect as all the meridians are semi
circles while all the latitudes are full circle.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements about the longitudes on Earth is correct?

answerOptions.text: The distance between longitudes is constant from equator to poles.
All the longitudes are parallel to each other.
All the longitudes converge at poles.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct about the longitudes on
Earth as the meridians or longitudes are semicircles
and the distance between them decreases steadily pole
wards until it becomes zero at the poles, where all the
meridians meet.

answerOptions.text: Longitudes divide the Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

1 hour ahead of Greenwich (London) time, which means

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the longitudes and latitudes.
1. All the longitudes are parallel to the equator.
2. All the latitudes converge at the poles.
3. Distance between longitudes decreases from equator to the poles.
4. All the longitudes are of same length.
Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (3) and (4) are correct about the
longitudes and latitudes as longitudes are semicircles
and the distance between them decreases steadily pole
wards until it becomes zero at the poles, where all the
meridians meet. All the longitudes are of same length.
Each line of longitude equals to half of the
circumference of the Earth because each extends from
the North Pole to South Pole.
Statements (1) and (2) are incorrect because all the
latitudes are parallel to the equator and all the longitudes
converge at the poles.
53. Which of the following statements about the
longitudes and latitudes is/ are correct?

latitude and longitude of a place must be known.
2. Distance between meridians is measured in
‘degrees of longitudes’.
3. Each degree of longitude is divided into minutes
and seconds.
Codes
(a) Only 1 (b) 2 and 3 (c) Only 2 (d) All of these
Ans.
j (d)

longitudes and latitudes. To find the location of a place
on Earth, both the latitude and longitude of a place
must be known. This latitudes and longitudes help us to
fix the position of a place. The distance between them is
measured in ‘degrees of longitude’. Each degree is
further divided into minutes, and minutes into seconds.

questions.question:

answerOptions.text: The Earth has been divided into 24 time zones.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect about the time zones on
Earth because the Earth rotates 360° in about 24
hours, which means 15° an hour or 1° in four minutes.
Thus, each time zone covers 15° of longitude.

answerOptions.text: Local time of a place depends upon its longitudinal value.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements about the parallel of latitudes are correct?
1. The length of parallels decreases as away from the equator.
2. The Tropic of Cancer is the largest parallel of latitude.
3. Latitudinal value of a place is used to determine the local time.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
None of the statements is correct about the
parallel of latitudes. The parallels of latitudes are
always parallel to the equator, so the length of parallels
does not decrease as away from the equator. The
equator is the largest parallel of latitude. Longitudinal
value of a place is used to determine the local time.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion
The continental crust of Earth is less denser and more thicker than the oceanic crust. Reason (R) The continental crust is made up of basaltic rocks. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
answerOptions.rationale:
The Assertion (A) is true but the Reason (R) is
false. The continental crust of Earth is less denser and
more thicker than the oceanic crust. Oceanic crust has
density of about 2.9-3 grams/ cubic centimetre, whereas
the density of the continental crust is about 2.7
grams/cubic centimetre.
On the other hand, continental crust is thicker than the
oceanic crust as the mean thickness of oceanic crust is
5 km, whereas the continental is around 30 km.
Also, the continental crust is not made up of basaltic
rocks. It is mostly composed of different types of
granites.
5. The Mohorovich discontinuity separates, which of
the following layers of interior Earth?
(a) Mantle and inner core
(Chap 2, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)
(b) Outer core and mantle
(c) Crust and mantle
(d) Oceanic crust and continental crust
j Ans. (c)
Exp. The Mohorovich discontinuity or Moho
discontinuity separates the crust and mantle. There
are five discontinuities inside the Earth, which are as
follows
Conrad Discontinuity It is transition zone between SiAl
and SiMa.
Mohorovich Discontinuity It is transition zone between
the crust and the mantle.
Repiti Discontinuity It is transition zone between outer
mantle and inner mantle.

answerOptions.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old/New NCERT)

Temperature and density inside the Earth is highest in the core and yet the inner core is in solid state. Which of following is most appropriate explanation of this phenomenon?

answerOptions.text: Radioactive decay of rocks in inner core.
Increasing velocity of P waves inside inner core.
Increasing pressure inside inner core due to overlying rock layers.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is the most appropriate explanation
of the phenomenon mentioned in the question.
Temperature and density inside the Earth is highest in
the core and yet the inner core is in solid state. The
outer core is a liquid because the high temperatures
melt the iron-nickel alloy at the outer core but very
high pressure from the weight of rocks lying above the
inner core makes it solid.

answerOptions.text: Presence of igneous rocks in inner core.

questions.question:

Which of the following statements is/are correct about pressure and density inside the Earth?

2. The central core of Earth has the highest density among all the layers.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect about pressure and
density inside the Earth as the temperature from the
surface to the depth of the Earth is not constant. The
inner core have the highest temperature and density
among all the layers.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Layer of Earth) (% of volume) A. Crust 1. 15 % B. Mantle 2. 1 % C. Core 3. 84 %
Codes A B C A B C

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-3, C-1.
The crust forms only 1% of the volume of the Earth and
is a very thin hard top layer of the Earth.
84% of the volume of the Earth is formed by mantle,
which is divided into two parts i.e., upper mantle and
lower mantle.
Core accounts for 15% of the Earth’s volume, which is
the innermost layer of the Earth. It is also divided into
two parts i.e., Outer core and Inner core.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following sources are used by scientists to study the interior of Earth?
1. Samples of Earth’s core
2. Gold Mines

4. Meteors
5. Gravity Anomalies

answerOptions.rationale:
Gold mines, volcanic magma, meteors, gravity
anomalies, are used by scientists to study the interior of
Earth.
Gold Mines Through the mining activity, it is known that
temperature and pressure increase with the increasing
distance from the surface towards the interior in deeper
depths.
Volcanic Magma During volcanic eruption, the molten
material (magma) is thrown onto the surface of the Earth.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect about the distribution of material inside the Earth?

answerOptions.text: There is even distribution of mass material inside the Earth.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect about the distribution
of material inside the Earth because scientists have
estimated that the values of temperature, pressure and
the distribution of mass is uneven at different depths
inside the Earth. Magnetic surveys provide
information about the distribution of magnetic
materials in the crust and thus, provide information
about the distribution of materials in this part.

answerOptions.text: The crust of Earth consists of magnetic materials.
Gravity Anomaly gives a clear picture of distribution of mass inside Earth.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the earthquake shadow zone. (CGPSC Pre 2020)
1. The shadow zone of one earthquake is totally different from the shadow zone of another earthquake.
2. Seismometres record both ‘P’ and ‘S’ waves at any distance out of 105° from earthquake’s epicentre.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect about the earthquake
shadow zone. Seismometres record both ‘P’ and ‘S’
waves at any distance within 105° from earthquake’s
epicentre. Earthquake waves get recorded in
seismographs. However, there exist some specific areas
where the waves are not recorded, such a zone is
called the ‘Shadow Zone’. The study of different events
reveals that for each earthquake, there exists an
altogether different shadow zone.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the endogenic movements of Earth?

answerOptions.text: These forces are produced only by movement of lithospheric plates.
Tectonic and volcanic activities are a form of endogenic movements.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is correct about the endogenic
movements of Earth because tectonic and volcanic
activities are a form of endogenic movements of Earth.
Endogenic forces are those forces, which originate in
the interior of the Earth and cause changes on the
surface of the Earth. Earthquakes and volcanic
eruptions are examples of Endogenic movements.

answerOptions.text: Weathering and erosion of Earth’s surface is caused by Endogenic movements.
The energy required for endogenic movements is generated on the Earth’s surface.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following features on Earth are formed by tectonic movements?
1. Volcanic mountains 2. Faults
3. Folds 4. Trenches

answerOptions.rationale:
All the features given in the question are formed
by tectonic movements. These movements are
movement of the plates, which results in the building
up of stresses within the plates and the continental
rocks. These movements of plates can make three
different boundaries these are convergent, divergent
and transform. In these plate boundaries, different
types of Earth features are formed like folding,
trenches, faulting and volcanic activity.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement is/are correct about the earthquake measuring scales?
1. The Richter scale measures the magnitude of Earthquake waves.
2. The Mercalli scale measures the damage of the Earthquake over a region.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct about
the earthquake measuring scales.
The earthquake events are scaled either according to
the magnitude or intensity of the shock. The magnitude
scale is known as the Richter scale. The magnitude
relates to the energy released during the quake. The
magnitude is expressed in absolute numbers i.e., 0-10.
The intensity scale is named after Mercalli, an Italian
seismologist. The intensity scale takes into account the
visible damage caused by the event. The range of
intensity scale exist between 1-12.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about orogenic movements?

answerOptions.text: Orogenic movements are large scale vertical movements of Earth.
Orogenic movements create folds on the surface.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is correct about orogenic
movement. It leads to the upliftment of continental
plates because of the horizontal movement of Earth and
the formation of mountain ranges through folding of
crust.
It takes place due to the convergence of tectonic plates
in the Earth’s crust. This movement is not responsible
for formation of volcanic vent as the liquefied rock in
the magma chamber, which create great pressure on the
crust and over time it fractures the Earth’s crust,
creating a volcanic vent.

answerOptions.text: Orogenic movements are responsible for formation of volcanic vents.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect about the shield volcanoes on the Earth?
1. The shield volcanoes are the largest volcanoes on Earth.
2. These volcanoes are mainly made up of fluid basalt.
3. These volcanoes are characterised by highly explosive eruptions.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect about the shield
volcanoes on the Earth as the shield volcanoes become
explosive if somehow water gets into the vent;
otherwise, they are characterised by low-explosivity.
Statements (1) and (2) are correct as the shield
volcanoes are the largest of all the volcanoes on the
Earth. The Hawaiian volcanoes are their most famous
examples. These volcanoes are mostly made up of fluid
basalt, a type of lava that is very fluid when erupted. For
this reason, these volcanoes are not steep.
The upcoming lava moves in the form of a fountain and
throws out the cone at the top of the vent and develops
into cinder cone.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion
Composite volcanoes are formed of many layers of volcanic materials. Reason (R) Composite volcanoes are most explosive and tend to collapse on themselves. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
answerOptions.rationale:
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Composite volcanoes are characterised by eruptions of
cooler and more viscous lavas than basalt. These
volcanoes often result in explosive eruptions. Along
with lava, large quantities of pyroclastic material and
ashes find their way to the ground. This material
accumulates in the vicinity of the vent openings leading
to formation of layers and this makes the mounts appear
as composite volcanoes. Apart from that Caldera
volcanoes are most explosive and tend to collapse on
themselves.

answerOptions.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following forces is/are responsible for driving the exogenic movements of Earth?
1. Temperature and precipitation
2. Gravitational force
3. Seismic movements
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Temperature, precipitation and gravitational
force are responsible for driving the exogenic
movements of Earth.
The exogenic processes derive their energy from
atmosphere determined by the ultimate energy from the
Sun and also the gradients created by tectonic factors.
Gravitational force acts upon all Earth materials having
a sloping surface and tend to produce movement of
matter in down slope direction. Temperature and
precipitation are the two important climatic elements
that control various processes while Seismic movement
is a part of endogenic movement.

questions.question:

2. Slope and altitude of a place

Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Factors like density, distribution of vegetation,
slope and altitude of a place, type and structure of rocks
etc affect the exogenic movement in a region. The
precipitation and temperature exert indirect influence
on exogenic geomorphic processes elaborate.

questions.question:

Water pressures controlled by wetting and drying
cycles.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Alfred Wegener, a German Meteorologist put forward a comprehensive Continental Drift Theory in 1912.
2. According to Wegener, the Pangaea broke away from Panthalassa 200 million years ago.
3. Panthalassa was a supercontinent floating over Pangaea, the mega ocean.
4. The Pangaea split into Laurasia and Gondwana.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct.
Alfred Wegener, a German Meteorologist put forward
a comprehensive Continental Drift Theory in 1912.
According to him, all the continents formed a single
continental mass and mega ocean surrounded the
same. ‘The supercontinent was named Pangaea, which
meant all Earth’. The mega-ocean was called
Panthalassa, meaning ‘all water’. He argued that,
around 200 million years ago, the super continent,
Pangaea, began to split. Pangaea first broke into two
large continental masses as Laurasia and Gondwana
land forming the Northern and Southern components
respectively. Subsequently, Laurasia and Gondwana
land continued to break into various smaller continents
that exist today.
Statement (3) is incorrect as Pangaea (not Panthalassa)
was a supercontinent floating over the mega ocean
Panthalassa.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. After the World War II, oceanic floor relief was mapped using modern techniques.
2. Mid-oceanic ridges with volcanic eruptions were found after the mapping of oceanic floor.
3. Paleomagnetic studies of rocks of the oceanic floor revealed that continental rocks were younger than oceanic rocks.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct. Expeditions to
map the oceanic floor in the Post World War II period
provided a detailed picture of the ocean relief and
indicated the existence of submerged mountain ranges
as well as deep trenches, mostly located closer to the
continental margins. The mid-oceanic ridges were
found to be most active in terms of volcanic eruptions.
Statement (3) is incorrect as the dating of the rocks from
the oceanic crust revealed the fact that they are much
younger than the continental rocks.

questions.question:

answerOptions.text: There are six major tectonic plates on Earth.

Major tectonic plates include both continents as well as oceans.
answerOptions.rationale:

plates on Earth. A plate may be referred to as the

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The concept of Plate tectonics was given by Mckenzie, Parker and Morgan in 1967.
2. Lithospheric plates includes the crust and top mantle.
3. The concept of sea floor spreading was developed by Alfred Wegener.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct as in 1967,
McKenzie and Parker and also Morgan, independently
collected the available ideas and came out with an
concept termed plate tectonics. A tectonic plate (also
called lithospheric plate) is a massive,
irregularly-shaped slab of solid rock, generally
composed of both continental and oceanic lithosphere.
Plates move horizontally over the asthenosphere as
rigid units. The lithospheric plate includes both the
crust and top mantle layers.
Statement (3) is incorrect as the sea floor spreading
theory was developed by H. Hess.

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following rocks are intrusive igneous rock formations?
1. Laccoliths 2. Batholiths
3. Dykes 4. Caldera
5. Flood Basalt
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Laccoliths, batholiths and dykes are intrusive
igneous rock formations. The lava that cools within the
crustal portions assumes different forms. These forms
are called intrusive forms. For example, Lopolith,
Phacolith and Sills. Caldera and flood basalt are the
examples of volcanic landforms.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Rock) (Metamorphosed form) A. Granite 1. Schist B. Clay 2. Gneiss C. Limestone 3. Quartzite D. Sandstone 4. Marble
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C- 4, D-3.
Igneous and sedimentary rocks can change into
metamorphic rocks under great heat and pressure.
Schist is the metamorphic form of sedimentary rock
clay. Schist is a type of rock formed of layers of different
minerals, that breaks naturally into thin flat pieces.
Gneiss is a coarse to medium grained banded
metamorphic rock formed from igneous or sedimentary
rocks during regional metamorphism.
Quartzite is the metamorphic form of sedimentary rock
sandstone.
Marble is the metamorphic form of sedimentary rock
limestone.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about metamorphism.
1. Metamorphism occurs when crustal rocks come in contact with molten magma at high temperatures.
2. There are no chemical changes in original rocks in dynamic metamorphism.
3. Re-crystallisation of rocks due to high temperature and tectonic shearing is known as regional metamorphism.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about
metamorphism. It occurs when rocks are forced down
to lower levels by tectonic processes or when molten
magma rising through the crust comes in contact with
the crustal rocks or the underlying rocks are subjected
to great amounts of pressure by overlying rocks.
Mechanical disruption and re-organisation of the
original minerals within rocks due to breaking and
crushing without any appreciable chemical changes is
called dynamic metamorphism. In regional
metamorphism, rocks undergo re-crystallisation due to
deformation caused by tectonic shearing together with
high temperature or pressure or both.

answerOptions.rationale:

because block mountains are created when large areas
are broken and displaced vertically. The Rhine valley
and the Vosges mountains are examples of block
mountains.
Statements (2) and (3) are incorrect as the uplifted

called graben. Block mountains have flat peaks not

questions.question:

Consider the following features of a plateau.
1. They have a flat top like a table.
2. Plateaus are rich in minerals like gold and diamond.
3. Tibetan plateau is the highest plateau in the World.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about a plateau
because a plateau is an elevated flat land. It is a
flat-topped table land standing above the surrounding
area. Plateaus are very useful because they are rich in
mineral deposits. As a result, many of the mining areas
in the world are located in the plateau areas.
The Tibet plateau is the highest plateau in the world
with a height of 4,000 to 6,000 metres above the mean
sea level.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about fold mountains?
1. They are formed under the influence of compression tectonic forces.
2. Deep gorges and pyramidal peaks are formed in Fold mountains.
3. Igneous, sedimentary and metamorphosed rocks are found in mountain regions.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct. Fold mountains
are formed where two or more of Earth’s tectonic plates
are pushed together. They are formed through a process
called orogeny. Fold mountains are responsible for
formation of deep gorges and pyramidal peaks.
Himalayas (Asia), Aravali (Asia), Alps in Europe and
Andes in South America are some of the examples of
fold mountains.
Statement (3) is incorrect as the presence of fossils
suggests that the sedimentary rocks of these folded
mountains were formed after accumulation and
consolidation of silts and sediments in a marine
environment. Hence, only the sedimentary rocks are
found in the fold mountains.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about plains.
1. Structural plains are usually found near the sea coast.
2. Erosional plains are formed by the process of deposition of river sediments.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct about plains as the
structural plains are mainly formed by the upliftment
of a part of the sea floor or continental shelf. They are
located on the borders of almost all the major
continents. The structural plains may also be formed
by the subsidence of areas.
Statement (2) is incorrect as erosional plains are formed
by the continuous and longtime erosion of uplands. The
surface of such plains is hardly smooth and hence, they
are also called as Peneplains, which means almost
plain. Hence, it is not formed because the deposition of
sediments.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is a depositional feature formed by river water?
1. Meander 2. River Delta
3. Natural Levee 4. U-shaped valley
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Meander, delta and natural levee are the
depositional feature formed by river water. The process
of erosion and deposition of river create different
landforms on the surface of the Earth. When the river
enters into plain it become slow and begins to deposit
its load. At this point different types of depositional
landforms can be formed by the river. These are alluvial
fan, delta, meander, point bar natural levee and flood
plains.
U-shaped valley is formed by the erosional work of
glaciers, not by river water.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the stages of landform development in rivers?

answerOptions.text: The path of a river is steepest in the valley stage.
Volume of water in a river is highest in the mountain course.
The lower course of river is characterised by gentle slope and deposition.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct about the stages of
landform development in rivers. The course of a river
form its source to its mouth is normally divide into
three sections, namely upper, middle and lower.
In the lower course of a river the valley floor has
extremely gentle slope. Hence, the river is unable to
transport all the sediments in its channel and starts to
deposits its loads.

questions.question:

because the river when enters the plain it twists and
turns forming large bends known as Meanders.

deposition along the concave bank and undercutting
along the convex bank.

shows up as a steep scarp and the convex bank presents
a long, gentle profile.

trenches called valley sinks or Uvalas form.

mangroves, if any, to absorb the destructive force of
storm and Tsunami waves.

questions.question:

Deflation It includes lifting and removal of dust and

night.

Which of the following statements about solar insolation received over the Earth’s surface is correct?

answerOptions.text: Amount of solar insolation received in a region is directly dependent upon the angle of Sun’s rays.

answerOptions.rationale:

In lower latitudes, the Sun’s rays are vertical in summer

questions.question:

Which among the following statements about solar insolation and heating of Earth is/are incorrect?

4. Earth receives insolation at a rate of two calories 2 per m per minute at the atmospheric top.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect about solar insolation
and heating of Earth because atmosphere of Earth is
heated more by the terrestrial radiation than by solar
insolation.

the solar insolation received in the outer atmosphere is
received by the Earth’s surface as direct radiation. Of
which, 34% of the energy is transmitted as direct
radiation and 16% in the form of diffuse day light.
The Earth heats up after receiving the Sun’s radiation
and starts releasing energy again which is called long
wave terrestrial radiation. This long wave terrestrial
radiation is absorbed by atmospheric gases and heats the
atmosphere. On an average, the Earth receives
2 calories per m 2 per minute at the top of its
atmosphere.

answerOptions.rationale:
Convergence of contrasting winds is the important

the sub polar region around latitudes 60° to 65° North
and South of the equator, the rotation of the Earth
pushes up the bulk of the air towards the equator or
polar region, creating a low-pressure belt in this region.

2. Sub polar low pressure belt

answerOptions.rationale:

pressure belt are dynamically formed pressure belts.
The sub-tropical high pressure belt is a dynamically
induced high pressure area. The air rising from the
equator and the low air pressure of the sub-polar
descends on these latitudes. Due to which, the volume
of the air decreases and the air pressure becomes high.
The sub-tropical high pressure belt originates due to the
rotation of the Earth and the sinking and settling of
winds. Thus, it is mainly dynamically driven.
Equatorial low pressure belt and the polar high pressure
belt is thermally formed.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following factors affects wind movement on the Earth?
1. Coriolis force 2. Surface friction
3. Atmospheric pressure
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Coriolis force, surface friction and atmospheric
pressure affect wind movement on the Earth.
The rotation of the Earth about its axis affects the
direction of the wind. The invisible force that appears
to deflect the wind is the Coriolis force. It deflects the
wind to the right direction in the Northern hemisphere
and to the left in the Southern hemisphere. Surface
friction is greatest at the surface and affects the speed
of the wind.
Over the sea surface, the friction is minimal. The
velocity and direction of the wind are the net result of
the atmospheric pressure. Greater pressure gradient
increases wind speed while the low pressure gradient
reduces the wind speed.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements about wind movement on the Earth is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Geostrophic winds blow parallel to the isobars.
The speed of wind movement is influenced by friction of the surface.
Pressure gradient force is more when isobars are close to each other.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements about wind movement on the
Earth are correct. When isobars are straight and there
is no friction, the pressure gradient force is balanced by
the Coriolis force and the resultant wind blows parallel
to the isobar. This wind is known as the geostrophic
wind. Friction of the surface is greatest at the surface
and its influence generally extends up to an elevation of
1 - 3 km. Over the sea surface, the friction is minimal.
Surface friction affects the speed of the wind
movement. The pressure gradient is strong where the
isobars are close to each other and is weak where the
isobars are apart.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Trade winds converge at the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone to form a high pressure area.
2. Convergence, rise and sinking of trade winds occur in the Hadley cell.
3. Convergence of trade winds at the equator causes heavy rainfall.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct because Hadley
cells are the low-latitude overturning circulations that
have air rising at the equator and air sinking at roughly
30° latitude. The easterlies from either side of the
equator converge in Hadley cells.
Due to the convergence of the trade winds at the
equator, the air becomes lighter and rises up and
the air starts getting saturated after reaching the
required height. This causes heavy rainfall in the
equator region.
Statement (1) is incorrect because trade winds converge
at the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) to form
a low pressure area.

questions.question:

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Westerlies are stronger and more regular in the Southern hemisphere than in the Northern hemisphere.
Westerlies converge at the equatorial region with the trade winds.
Westerlies cause frontal rain in mid latitude regions.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct because the
westerly winds in the Southern hemisphere are
stronger and more regular because they face minimal
land interference due to lack of land as compared to the
Northern hemisphere. Westerly winds play an
important role in carrying warm, equatorial waters
and winds to the West coasts of the continents,
causing rainfall along the western coasts of the
continents.
Statement (b) is incorrect because Westerlies do
not converge at the equatorial region with the trade
winds.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Arrange the following atmospheric cells in the correct sequence from equator to poles.

answerOptions.text: Polar cell, Hadley cell, Ferrell cell
Hadley cell, Ferrell cell, Polar cell
answerOptions.rationale:
The correct sequence of atmospheric cells from
equator to poles is Hadley cell, Farrell cell and Polar
cell.
The easterlies from either side of the equator converge
in the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). Such
circulations from the surface upwards and vice-versa are
called cells. Such a cell in the tropics is called
Hadley cell.
In the middle latitudes, the circulation is that of sinking
cold air that comes from the poles and the rising warm
air that blows from the sub-tropical high. At the surface,
these winds are called Westerlies and the cell is known
as the Ferrell cell.
At polar latitudes, the cold dense air subsides near the
poles and blows towards middle latitudes as the polar
Easterlies. This cell is called the Polar cell.

answerOptions.text: Hadley cell, Polar cell, Ferrell cell
Ferrell cell, Hadley cell, Polar cell

Cyclone is formed due to convergence of cold and
warm airmasses. In an extra tropical cyclone, the central
air pressure is lower than that of the surrounding
environment, and the flow of circulation is
counterclockwise in the Northern hemisphere.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The area covered by an extra tropical cyclone is significantly more than a tropical cyclone.
2. Extratropical cyclones can only be formed over continental surfaces.
3. These cyclones move from West to East under the influence of westerly winds.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct because the
diameter of an extra tropical cyclone can range from
about 1040 to 1920 km. The average diameter of a
tropical cyclone can be up to 640 km.
Hence, the area covered by an extra tropical cyclone is
more than a tropical cyclone. Extra-tropical cyclones
after their origin move from West to East with westerly
winds.
Statement (2) is incorrect because extratropical cyclones
can formed over continental or ocean surface.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following conditions is not necessary for the formation of a tropical cyclone?
1. Sea surface with temperature over 27°C
2. Coriolis force
3. Warm airmass
4. Pre-existing low pressure
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Warm airmass is not necessary for the formation
of a tropical cyclone because tropical cyclones originate
and intensify over warm tropical oceans. Warm airmass
is not necessary for the formation of a tropical cyclone.
The conditions favourable for the formation and
intensification of tropical storms are: large sea surface
with temperature higher than 27° C; presence of the
coriolis force; small variations in the vertical wind
speed; a pre-existing weak low-pressure area or
low-level-cyclonic circulation and upper divergence
above the sea level system.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct?
1. Tropical cyclones can originate over sea as well as land surface.
2. Wind velocity of tropical cyclones is much higher than extra tropical cyclones.
3. Tropical cyclones move from East to West.
4. Tropical cyclones can recurve beyond 20°N latitude and become more destructive.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2), (3) and (4) are correct because
average wind speed in tropical cyclone is more than
about 100 km per hour, but in extratropical cyclone, the
average wind speed is about 32 km per hour in summer
and about 48 km per hour in winter. Tropical cyclones
move from East to West with the trade winds after their
origin. In the 20°N latitude with continuous supply of
moisture from the sea, the tropical cyclone is further
strengthened. The cyclones, which cross 20° North
latitude generally, recurve and they are more
destructive.
Statement (1) is incorrect because tropical cyclones can
originate over sea surface.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about tropical cyclones.
1. The eye of a tropical cyclone is characterised by ascent of strong winds.
2. Cumulonimbus clouds cause heavy rainfall in tropical cyclones.
3. The intensity of tropical cyclones increase as they make a landfall over the continents.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct about tropical cyclones
because Cumulonimbus clouds are associated with
extreme weather in tropical cyclones. Such as heavy
torrential downpours, hail storms, lightning and even
tornadoes.
Statements (1) and (3) are incorrect because the eye of a
tropical cyclone is characterised is a region of calm with
subsiding air. The intensity of tropical cyclones
decreases as they make a landfall over the continents.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Tropical Cyclone Name) (Region) A. Cyclone 1. Australia B. Willy-Willy 2. Indian Ocean C. Hurricane 3. South China Sea D. Typhoon 4. Atlantic Ocean
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.
Cyclone Tropical cyclone is a rapid rotating storm
system characterised by a long-pressure centre, a closed
low level strong winds and heavy rain. In Indian Ocean,
tropical cyclones are also called severe cyclonic storms.
Willy-willy It is a famons tropical cyclone in Western
Australia. This tropical cyclone causes heavy rainfall.
Hurricane It is a strong tropical cyclone that occurs in
the Atlantic Ocean or North-Eastern Pacific Ocean.
Typhoon It occurs in North-Western Pacific Ocean. It is
a most dangerous natural calamity in that region.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect about tornadoes?
1. Tornadoes generally occur in the tropical and equatorial regions.
2. Water spouts are the tornadoes formed over sea surface.
3. Tornadoes occur for a short period as compared to cyclones.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect about tornadoes because
tornadoes generally occur in the middle latitude
between 20° and 60° N and S.
A tornado is a furiously rotating column of air that
extends down to the Earth from the base of a
thunderstorm.
55. Which of the following characteristics can be
attributed to thunderstorms?
(Chap 10, Class-XI, New NCERT)
1. Cumulonimbus clouds with lightning
2. Intense updraft and rising of air
3. Heavy precipitation 4. Widespread area
Codes
(a) 1, 2 and 3 (b) 2, 3 and 4
(c) 1, 3 and 4 (d) 1, 2 and 4
Ans. (a)

Exp. Characteristics given in options (1), (2) and (3) can
be attributed to thunderstorms because these are
caused by intense convection on moist hot days.
A thunderstorm is a well-grown cumulonimbus cloud
producing thunder and lightning. When the clouds
extend to heights where sub-zero temperature prevails,
hails are formed and they come down as hailstorm. A
thunderstorm is characterised by intense updraft of
rising warm air, which causes the clouds to grow bigger
and rise to greater height.
This causes precipitation. Later, downdraft brings
down to Earth the cool air and the rain. Thunderstorms
are of short duration, occurring over a small area but
are violent.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the given statements is incorrect?

answerOptions.text: The amount of water vapour in the atmosphere varies from place to place.
The amount of water vapour determines the capacity of precipitation over a region.
Amount of water vapour determines the rate of humidity in a region.
Water vapour is added to atmosphere by only oceanic surfaces.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) is incorrect because water vapour is
water in gaseous form. It can be formed either through
a process of evaporation or sublimation. Water vapour
is added to atmosphere by oceanic surface, land
surface, lake surface and river surface, etc.
Water vapour is basically the gaseous phase of the
water. The amount of water vapour in the atmosphere
varies from place to place.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the cycle of precipitation on the Earth?

answerOptions.text: Moisture is transported on Earth from one region to another through convection.
Cycle of precipitation over land takes more time to complete than cycle over the oceans.
Both evaporation and transpiration contribute moisture to the atmosphere.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about the cycle of
precipitation on the Earth because convection largely
occurs in the atmosphere, oceans, and mantle of
planets. The movement of fluid during convection may
be invisibly slow, or it may become clearer and faster,
as in a storm. Due to convection, the moisture on the
Earth is transferred from one place to another. Ocean
water warms and cools quickly and land cools and
warms late. That is why, the cycle of precipitation over
land takes longer to complete than cycle over the
oceans. Sea areas, land, rivers and lakes contribute
moisture to the atmosphere by evaporation. Plants also
increase the moisture in the atmosphere through
transpiration.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Water vapour contributes to only a minute proportion of Atmospheric composition but it plays a very important role in atmospheric and weather phenomenon on Earth. Which of the following statements indicates significance of water vapour?
1. It regulates the rate of heat loss from Earth.
2. It decides the amount of rainfall in a region.
3. It leads to formation of storms in a region.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements indicate significance of
water vapour because water vapour plays a very
important role in the occurrence of atmospheric and
weather phenomenon on Earth. Water vapour controls
the rate of Earth’s temperature by preventing surface
energy from entering the atmosphere.
Water vapour determines the amount of rainfall in an
area. Where there is more water vapour, there is more
condensation and there is more rainfall in that area.
When water vapour condenses back into liquid water, it
releases energy into the atmosphere that can originate
storms.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Weight of water vapour in a given volume of air determines absolute humidity.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct because relative
humidity is the water vapour content of the air relative
to its content at saturation.
Saturated air, for example, has a relative humidity of
100%. When the relative humidity is 100%, the air
becomes saturated and the water vapour turns into
water and causes precipitation at the dew point.
Statement (3) is incorrect because saturated air has
potential to absorb less amounts of moisture.

answerOptions.text: Warm air can hold less moisture as compared to cold air.
Increase in temperature of atmosphere increases the relative humidity.
All of the above Ans. j

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct because relative
humidity is the water vapour content of the air relative
to its content at saturation.
Saturated air, for example, has a relative humidity of
100%. When the relative humidity is 100%, the air
becomes saturated and the water vapour turns into
water and causes precipitation at the dew point.
Statement (3) is incorrect because saturated air has
potential to absorb less amounts of moisture.

answerOptions.text: is correct because the weight of water vapour in a given volume of air is called absolute humidity. Absolute humidity is the total amount of water vapour present in the air. It is usually expressed as grams of water vapour per cubic metre of air. Statements

humidity is the water vapour content of the air relative

Saturated air, for example, has a relative humidity of

Statement (3) is incorrect because saturated air has

The relative humidity of a saturated air is 100%. 2. Water vapour starts changing into water and causes precipitation at the dew point. 3. Saturated air has potential to absorb large amounts of moisture. Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct because relative
humidity is the water vapour content of the air relative
to its content at saturation.
Saturated air, for example, has a relative humidity of
100%. When the relative humidity is 100%, the air

Statement (3) is incorrect because saturated air has

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Fog and mist are formed from air masses that are very close to the surface of Earth.
2. Mists occur frequently over mountain regions.
3. Fog has more moisture than mist.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct because when the
temperature of an airmass containing a large quantity of
water vapour falls all of a sudden, condensation takes
place within itself on fine dust particles.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following pairs is matched correctly? List I (Forms of List II Condensation) (Description)

answerOptions.text: Dew Deposition of water droplets over cooler surfaces
Frost Formation of minute ice crystals
Advection Fog Meeting of moist air mass and cooler surface

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given pairs are correctly matched.
Dew When the moisture is deposited in the form of
water droplets on cooler surfaces of solid objects such
as grass blades and plant leaves, it is known as dew.
Frost When condensation takes place below freezing
point 0°C, the excess moisture is deposited in the form
of minute ice crystals instead of water droplets called
frost.
Advection Fog formed by condensation of warm air
when it moves horizontally over a cold surface, are
known as advection fog. These fogs are thick. It is
formed in the mixing areas of warm and cold water in
the oceans.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, 3, Class-XI, VII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the formation of clouds in the Earth’s atmosphere?

answerOptions.text: Clouds are formed by adiabatic cooling of air below dew point.
Clouds consist of mass of water vapour and tiny ice crystals.
Clouds are formed at higher altitudes than fog and mist.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about the formation
of clouds in the Earth’s atmosphere. As air rises in
atmosphere, it cools and expands, reducing the
pressure. Clouds are formed when the air cools below
the dew point, and the air cannot hold as much water
vapour. Cloud is a mass of minute water droplets or
tiny crystals of ice formed by the condensation of the
water vapour in free air at considerable elevations.
When the air rises, it starts cooling due to the
condensation of water vapour in the free air at a high
altitude. Clouds are formed due to the arrival of air at
higher altitudes whereas fog and mist are formed near
the surface.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Identify the type of cloud from the information given below. These clouds are formed at 8-12 km above the Earth’s surface. They are thin and have feathery appearance. They always appear white in colour.

answerOptions.rationale:
The information given in the question is about
Cirrus clouds. These are short, detached and hair-like
clouds found at high altitudes (8 – 12 km). They are thin
and detached clouds having a feathery appearance.
They are always white in colour.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following type of clouds have a flat base, high vertical development and cauliflower shape?

(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Precipitation occurs when water vapour is condensed in free air.
Precipitation can be either liquid or solid.
Precipitation only occurs when dew point is below the freezing point.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (b) are correct because when
the air moves upwards, the air cools down due to the
decrease in atmospheric pressure and the relative
humidity of the air increases and the air becomes
saturated.
The air rises again and condensation begins. After
condensation, it becomes cloudy and then it rains.
Precipitation can be in liquid or solid form. The
precipitation in the form of water is called rainfall and
precipitation takes place in the form of fine flakes of
snow and is called snowfall.
Statement (c) is incorrect because precipitation occurs
when dew point is below or above the freezing point.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following pairs is matched correctly?
1. Precipitation below freezing point - Snowfall
2. Frozen raindrops and refrozen water- Sleet
3. Rounded solid pieces of ice - Hailstone
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Pairs (2) and (3) are correctly matched because
sleet is frozen raindrops and refrozen melted
snow-water. When a layer of air with the temperature
above freezing point overlies a subfreezing layer near
the ground, precipitation takes place in the form of
sleet.
Hail is formed when drops of water freeze together in
the cold upper regions of thunderstorm clouds. These
chunks of rounded solid pieces of ice are called
hailstones.
Pair (1) is incorrect because precipitation below freezing
point is called sleet. It is basically frozen raindrops and
occur when the layer of freezing air along the surface
is thicker.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.text: Coastal regions of the world receive lesser rainfall than the interior of Continents.
Equatorial regions receive lesser rainfall than the polar regions.
Eastern margins of temperate regions receive more rainfall than the western margins.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are incorrect because the
coastal areas of the world receive greater amounts of
rainfall than the interior of the continents.
Equatorial regions receive greater rainfall than the
polar regions. In general, as we proceed from the
equator towards the poles, rainfall goes on decreasing
steadily.
In temperate regions between 45° N and 65° S Equator,
due to the Westerlies, the rainfall is first received on
the Western margins of the continents and it goes on
decreasing towards the East.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, 14, Class-XI, New/old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2010)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and the correct code. Assertion
The environment of the equatorial regions is conductive for plants but not for humans. Reason (R) The average annual temperature difference is very low in equatorial regions. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
answerOptions.rationale:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but
Reason (R) is not correct explanation of Assertion (A).
The region between 5° to 10° latitude on North and
South of the equator is known as equatorial region. In
this region, there is constant high temperature and heavy
rainfall occur throughout the year. The climate is not
conductive for humans but conductive for vegetation.

answerOptions.text: A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following regions is/are characterised by Dry ‘B’ climate according to Koeppen’s climatic classification?

answerOptions.rationale:
Steppe grasslands is the region which is
characterised by Dry ‘B’ climate according to
Koeppen’s climatic classification. ‘B’ type Dry climates
are divided into steppe or semi-arid climate (BS) and
desert climate (BW).
‘B’ type dry climate is not found in Northern Australia,
Eastern China and Southern Chile.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Marine West Coastal Climate?
1. Marine Western coastal climate is located polewards of Mediterranean climate.
2. This type of climate is characterised by presence of seasonal rainfall.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct about Marine West Coastal
Climate because this type of climate is found polewards
from the Mediterranean climate on the West coast of the
continents.
The main areas are; North-Western Europe, West coast
of North America, North of California, Southern Chile,
South-Eastern Australia and New Zealand.
Statement (2) is incorrect because in Marine West coast
climate, precipitation occurs throughout the year.
Precipitation varies greatly from 50-250 cm.
