questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Koeppen’s List II Climate Symbol) (Climate) A. BWh 1. Mediterranean Climate B. Cs 2. Sub-tropical Desert Climate C. EF 3. Tropical Monsoon Climate D. Am 4. Polar Icecaps
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.
Sub-tropical desert (BWh) located in the transition zone
between humid and dry climates.
Mediterranean climate (Cs) occurs around Mediterranean
sea, along the West coast of continents in sub-tropical
latitudes between 30° - 40° latitudes.
The polar ice cap climate (EF) occurs over interior
Greenland and Antarctica.
Tropical monsoon climate (Am) is found over the Indian
sub-continent, North-Eastern part of South America and
Northern Australia.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to periodic winds blowing in Africa?

answerOptions.text: Harmattan is a hot and dry wind blowing in summers in Nigeria.
Khamsin is a hot wind blowing in Egypt during summers.
Sirocco blows in the equatorial regions of Africa during winters.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) and (b) are correct with reference to
periodic winds blowing in Africa because Harmattan is
a hot and dry wind originate from the Sahara desert
and blow towards the Guinea coast or Nigeria coast of
Africa in summers. This wind is also known as doctor
winds in the Guinea coast area of Western Africa.
Khamsin winds are warm, dry, dusty contain sand

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Strong and cold stormy winds blowing in Canada in the winter season are known as

answerOptions.rationale:
Blizzard is the strong and cold stormy wind that
blows in Canada in the winter season. It is violent and
powdery polar wind. Blizzard winds are prevalent in
the North and South polar regions, Canada, USA,
Siberia, etc. in winter season. Snow and ice particles
caused by blizzard wind reduce atmospheric visibility
to almost zero.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct?

answerOptions.text: Only 80% of the Earth’s water is found in the oceans.
Only 1% of water on the Earth is freshwater.
2% of total water on the Earth is stored in the ice caps.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct because of the total water
on Earth, 2% is in ice caps/glaciers while 97.2% is in
oceans and inland seas. Ice and glaciers are part of the
water cycle.
An ice cap is a glacier with a large perennial
accumulation of crystalline ice, snow, sediment and
water that originates on land and moves down slopes
under the influence of its own weight and gravity.

answerOptions.text: Most of the freshwater on Earth is stored in the oceans.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct?

answerOptions.text: Oceanic water is circulated in the water cycle by the process of evaporation.
Groundwater is not affected by the process of evaporation.
Most of the surface water on the Earth is stored in ice caps and glaciers.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct because in
marine areas where evaporation is high, the water level
decreases. Due to this, the oceanic current flows from
high water level to low water level.
Evaporation decreases rapidly with depth of
groundwater. That’s why groundwater is not affected by
the process of evaporation.
More than 68% of the freshwater on the Earth is found
in glaciers and only over 30% is found in groundwater.
Only about 0.3% of our freshwater is found in the
surface waters of lakes, rivers and marshes.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect?

answerOptions.text: The water cycle over oceans is longer as compared to that over the land.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect because the water cycle
is longer over land than over the ocean, because it takes
longer time for evaporation and precipitation to occur
on land, whereas in the ocean, precipitation and
evaporation occur at a faster rate.

answerOptions.text: Total quantity of water available on the Earth always remains constant.
Evaporation of water over the oceans is compensated by surface runoff.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the continental shelf ?

answerOptions.text: It has an average gradient of 1° or less.
It is the shallowest part of the ocean having shallow seas and gulfs.
The depth and width of continental shelf is constant over all the oceans.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (b) are correct regarding the
continental shelf. The continental shelf is a gently
sloping oceanic extension of the continental plate.
The continental shelf of all the oceans together covers
7.5% of the total area of the oceans. The continental
slope is 1° or less. The shelf usually ends at a very steep
slope, which is called a shelf break. These extended
margins of each continent are occupied by relatively
shallow seas and gulfs.
Statement (c) is incorrect because the depth and width
of continental shelf is not constant over the entire ocean.
The depth and width of the continental shelf is
influenced by terrestrial relief.
Where there are high mountains, the depth of the
continental shelf is more and less in width.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the relief features found over the oceanic surface.
1. Mid oceanic ridges can be rise even above the oceanic surface.
2. Sea mounts are features of volcanic origin, which do not rise above the oceanic surface.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct about
the relief features found over the oceanic surface.
A mid ocean ridge is a seafloor mountain system which
is formed by plate tectonics. A mid oceanic ridge is
composed of two chains of mountains separated by a
large depression. The mountain ranges can have peaks
as high as 3000 m and some even reach above the
ocean’s surface.
A seamount is a large geologic landform that rises from
the ocean floor but that does not reach to the water’s
surface. Seamounts are typically formed from extinct
volcanoes that rise abruptly and are usually found rising
from the seafloor to 1,000-4,000 m in height.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect about the Indian Ocean?

answerOptions.text: Indian Ocean opens up to the Arctic Ocean in the North.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect regarding the Indian
Ocean, because it is bounded by Asia to the North,
Africa to the West and Australia to the East. To the
South, it is bounded by the Southern Ocean or
Antarctica. The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the
world’s oceanic divisions, covering 19.8% of the water
on Earth’s surface.

answerOptions.text: The floor of Indian Ocean is more regular as compared to Pacific Ocean.
The Lakshadweep Chagos ridge divides the Indian Ocean into two basins.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the profile of Indian Ocean?

answerOptions.text: Most of the Islands of the Ocean are located in the Eastern parts.
The central ridge of the Indian ocean is divided into several small ridges.
The Madagascar ridge divides Arabian Sea into two parts.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Trench) (Located in) A. Mindanao Trench 1. Atlantic Ocean B. Sunda Trench 2. Pacific Ocean C. Romanche Trench 3. Indian Ocean
Codes A B C

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-3, C-1.
Mindanao Trench (Philippine Trench) It is a submarine
trench in the East of the Philippines. The trench is
located in the Philippine Sea of the Western-North
Pacific Ocean.
Sunda Trench It is formerly known as the Java Trench,
is an oceanic trench located in the Indian Ocean near
Sumatra.
Romanche Trench It is the third deepest trench in the
Atlantic Ocean after the Puerto Rico Trench and the
South Sandwich Trench.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements correctly defines a thermocline?

answerOptions.text: The boundary where oceanic waters freeze completely.
The boundary where there is a rapid decline in ocean temperature.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) correctly define a thermocline.
A thermocline is the transition layer between warmer
mixed water at the ocean’s surface and cooler deep
water below it. This second layer lies below the first
layer and is characterised by rapid decrease in
temperature with increasing depth. The thermocline is
500 -1,000 m thick.

answerOptions.text: The boundary where temperature of oceanic water increases.
The boundary where oceanic water becomes denser.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about salinity of oceans?

answerOptions.text: Oceanic salinity in open seas is greater than in inland seas.
In Arctic region, there is seasonal fluctuation in the salinity.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is correct about salinity of oceans
because in the Arctic region, the salinity is low in the
summer due to the melting of snow and the arrival of
river water also reduces the salinity in summer. But in
winter, due to the freezing of snow, the salinity increases
slightly. In hot and dry regions, where evaporation is
high, the salinity sometimes reaches to 70%.
Statements (a) and (c) are not correct because ocean
salinity in inland seas is higher than in open ocean.
Salinity in coastal areas is same as salinity in oceans.
Sometimes, it is more than oceans while sometimes it
is less.

answerOptions.text: Salinity in coastal regions is almost similar to salinity in oceans.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following factors will change the salinity of a water body?
1. Freshwater inflow
2. Increase in temperature
3. Decline in density
4. Wind movement
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given factors have the property to change
the salinity of water body. Salinity is the term used to
define the total content of dissolved salts in sea water.
Factors affecting ocean salinity are, the salinity of water
in the surface layer of oceans depend mainly on
evaporation and precipitation.
Surface salinity is greatly influenced in coastal regions
by the freshwater flow from rivers, and in Polar regions
by the processes of freezing and thawing of ice.
Wind, also influences salinity of an area by transferring
water to other areas. The ocean currents contribute to
the salinity variations. Salinity, temperature and density
of water are interrelated. Hence, any change in the
temperature or density influences the salinity of an area.

Sea waves originate due to the movement of winds.
Velocity and duration of winds affects the formation of waves.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct. Sea waves are
oscillatory motion that results in the rise and fall of the
surface of the water. Waves are a type of horizontal
movement of ocean water.
Ocean waves are actually energy. This energy for the

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Type of Sea Waves) (Description) A. Catastrophic Waves 1. Waves with not much movement, stationary waves B. Storm Waves 2. Sudden waves caused due to tectonic movements C. Seiches 3. Waves caused due to difference in density of layers of water D. Internal Waves 4. Waves caused due to strong wind action
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2 B-4 C-1 D-3.
Catastrophic sea wave It is a sudden wave usually
caused by a submarine earthquake, an underwater or
coastal landslide, or a volcanic eruption.
Storm wave It is primarily caused by strong winds in a
hurricane or tropical storm. The high winds associated
with tropical and extra tropical storms can cause
extreme waves and storm surges. Waves and storm
surges are responsible for severe flooding and property
damage.
Seiche It is a standing wave in an enclosed body of
water. Seiche related phenomena have been observed
on lakes, reservoirs, bays, harbours and seas.
Internal wave It is a type of gravitational wave that
occurs on interior surfaces within ocean water. These
surfaces represent rapidly changing water density levels
with increasing depth, and the waves associated with it
are called internal waves.

Rise of water in ocean during a storm.
Periodic rise and fall of ocean water two times in a day.

The rhythmic or periodic rise and fall of ocean water

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct about the

very important, especially harbours near rivers and

prevent ships and boats from entering into the harbour.
High tides help in navigation.
They raise the water level close to the shores. This helps
the ships to arrive at the harbour more easily.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 1999)

Which among the following statements about tide is/are correct?
1. The highest tides are known as Spring tides.
2. The lowest tides are known as Neap tides.
3. Spring tides occur when Moon is in first quarter.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct because the
positions of both the Sun and the Moon with respect to
the Earth have a direct effect on the height of the tides.
When the Sun, Moon and Earth are in a straight line,
the height of the tide is high. These types of tides are
also called spring tides or high tides. They occur twice
a month, one during the full Moon period and the other
during the new moon.
There is a gap of seven days between spring tide and
neap tide. At this time, the Sun and the Moon are at
right angles to each other and the forces of the Sun and
the Moon oppose each other. The attraction of the
Moon is less than the repulsive force of the Sun’s
gravitational pull like spring tides; these tides also come
twice a month.
Statement (3) is incorrect because spring tide occurs
when the Moon is either new or full and closest to Earth.

2. There is a gap of 21 days between a spring tide and a neap tide.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct about spring tides because
spring tides occur twice a month, one during the full

Spring tides are the highest tides, they are formed
when the Earth, Sun and Moon are lined up in a row.
Statement (2) is incorrect because there is a gap of 7
days between a spring tide and a neap tide.

3. Force of attraction of Moon is much greater than force of attraction of Sun.
Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct because the
closest part of the Earth in front of the Moon is most
affected by the Moon’s attraction, which is responsible
for causing tides.
Even though the Sun is much more massive and
therefore has a stronger gravity than the Moon, the Moon
is closer to the Earth so the Moon’s gravitational gradient
is stronger than that of the Sun.
Statement (2) is incorrect because Sun has lower
attraction power than Moon in context of Earth.
Sun’s tide generating force is about half of the Moon
because Sun is 390 times further from the Earth than is
the Moon.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct about tidal bulge
because the part of the Earth that is closest to the
Moon produces tidal waves due to the force of gravity.
The other side of the Earth, which is farthest from the
Moon, is generated by the centrifugal force. This is due
to the origin of the tidal bulge. On the surface of the
earth, the horizontal tide generating forces are more
important than the vertical forces in generating the
tidal bulges.
Statement (3) is incorrect because the tidal bulges on
wide continental shelves have greater height. When tidal
bulges hit the mid-oceanic islands they become low.

Equatorial countercurrent is a phenomenon near the

Which of the following ocean currents is associated with Indian Ocean?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Agulhas current is
associated with Indian Ocean. It is a warm current
which generates in such a way that branch of South
Equatorial Indian Oceanic current flows towards South
through the South-East coast of Mozambique and is
known as Mozambique current which flows 30° South
and meets with the branch of South Equatorial current
flowing along the East of Madagascar. Therefore, the
combined current of these two branches of currents is
known as Agulhas Current.
51. What of the following explains the Eastward flow
of the equatorial counter current?
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT) (IAS Pre 2015)
(a) The Earth rotation on its axis
(b) Convergence of the two equatorial currents
(c) Difference in salinity of water
(d) Occurrence of the belt of calm near the equator
Ans. (a)

Exp. Statement (a) correctly explains the Eastward flow
of the equatorial counter current. There are two
equatorial currents flowing from East to West–the
North equatorial current and the South equatorial
current. In between these two currents, an equatorial
counter current flows in the opposite direction from
West to East. Therefore, the Earth’s rotation on its axis
is responsible for the Eastward flow of equatorial
counter current.

Which of the following statements is correct about the coral deposits in the oceans?

answerOptions.text: Largest Coral deposits occur in the tropical regions.
Corals are made up of calcium carbonate obtained by the coral polyps.
Corals develop in regions having clear salt water.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct about the
coral deposits in the oceans because coral reefs are the
colonies of tiny living creatures that are found in
tropical oceans. Largest coral deposits occur in the
tropical regions like Great Barriers Reefs in Eastern
Australia.
Coral deposits are underwater structures that are
formed of coral polyps that are held together by calcium
carbonate. Coral reefs grow best in warm water.
Corals prefer clear and shallow water, where lots of
sunlight filters through to their symbiotic algae.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect about oceanic deposits on the bed of the oceans?

answerOptions.text: Oceanic deposits formed by materials derived from the Land are known as Terrigenous deposits.
Deposits in the ocean can be derived from materials obtained only from the surface.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect about oceanic deposits
on the bed of the oceans because oceanic deposits are
the unconsolidated sediments (Inorganic or Organic)
derived from various sources deposited on the oceanic
floor. Oceanic deposits which are mainly found on the
continental shelf are called Terrigenous deposits and
Pelagic deposits are comprised of both organic and
inorganic sediments and generally found in the deep
oceans in the continental slope, continental rise,
trenches and abyssal plains.

answerOptions.text: Deposits formed by shells of marine animals and plants are known as Pelagic Deposits.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about soil formation?

answerOptions.text: Weathered material of rocks is the most important input for soil formation.
Humus is formed in the soil by dead remains of plants and animals.
Bacteria, lichens and mosses are responsible for the formation of soil.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct about soil
formation.
Soil formation depends first on weathering. Due to
weathering, basic inputs are obtained for the formation
of soil. Humus is the dark organic matter that forms in
soil when dead plant and animal matter break down
further, specifically through the action of anaerobic
organisms.
Humus is formed in the soil by dead remains of plants
and animals, which is most important for soil formation.
In soil, weathered material or transported deposits are
colonised by bacteria and other inferior plant bodies like
mosses and lichens. Decomposition of organic matter
and accumulation of substances is done by bacteria.
That’s why bacteria, lichens and mosses are responsible
for the formation of soil.

3. Climate and temperature affect the rate of chemical, physical and biological reactions in the soil.

formation. Parent materials influence soil formation
through their mineralogical composition, their texture

Time is the important controlling factor in soil
formation. The length of time the soil forming processes
operate, determines maturation of soils and profile
development. A soil becomes mature and thick when all
soil-forming processes act for a sufficiently long time
developing a profile.
Climate and temperature affects the rate of
chemical, physical and biological reactions in the soil.
With the increase in soil temperature, the rate of
decomposition of organic matter or humus formation by
chemical reactions and decomposing organisms
increases.

Padocal soil.
Pedocal soil is a class of soil which forms in semi-arid

and mineral salts are high in pedocal soil. Pedocal soil

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about chernozem soil.
1. Chernozem soil is characterised by very low levels of humus content.
2. These soils have high moisture retention capacity.
3. The soil fertility of chernozem is very high.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct about
chernozem soil.
The clay of the chernozem soil has an ability to expand
and contract. When the soil comes in contact with
water, the clay present in the soil absorbs the water and
the moisture content available. Therefore, chernozem
soil has a great capacity to hold moisture.
Chernozem soil contains a very high quantities of
humus, ammonia and phosphoric acids. Chernozem soil
is very fertile and can produce high agricultural yields
with its high moisture storage capacity.
Statement (1) is incorrect because chernozem soil
contains a very high percentage of humus.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Major biomes of the world are formed due to the variations in climatic conditions.
The boundaries between two biomes are transitional regions.
One biome mostly contains uniform conditions in terms of soil, vegetation and climate.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct.
The revolution of our planet around the Sun and the tilt
of axis cause annual variations in the intensity and
duration of temperature, resulting in distinct seasons.
These variations together with annual variation in
precipitation account for the formation of major biomes
such as desert, rain forest and tundra.
An ecotone is a zone of junction or a transitional area
between two biomes. In other words, it is the zone
where two communities meet and integrate.
One biome mostly contains uniform conditions in terms
of soil, vegetation and climate because, a biome is a
large area characterised by its vegetation, soil, climate,
and wildlife.

questions.question:

Which of the following type of forest vegetations is/are mostly found in the islands of Indonesia?

Consider the following statements about the equatorial biome.
1. The seasonal contrast is maximum in equatorial regions.
2. It is characterised by absence of a dry season.
3. There is high level of leaching in the soils of this region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct about the
equatorial biome. The annual rainfall in the equatorial
biome is more than 200 cm and it rains daily, due to
which there is no dry season. The amount of leaching is
high due to the daily rainfall and temperature
exceeding 25°C, and the frequency of rainfall in which
the soil minerals move into the soil, so this soil is not
very fertile.
Statement (1) is incorrect because the seasonal contrast
is very low (not maximum) in equatorial regions.

answerOptions.rationale:
The given statement best describes the climate of
Central Asian Steppe. Nomadic herding is the
controlled movement of livestock. It is a primitive
subsistence activity, in which the herders rely on
animals for food, clothing, shelter and transport.
Savanna doesn’t have extreme climate. In North
American Prairies, there is no nomadic life and Tundra
does not have herders because climate is not suitable for
herding.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following crops is/are generally found in the equatorial rainforests of Central Africa?
1. Ebony 2. Mahogany
3. Rubber 4. Palm
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given crops are found in the equatorial
rainforests of Central Africa. These forests cover most
of the central part of the continent of Africa.
Evergreen forests are found in this region due to
high temperature, high rainfall and high humidity.
Ebony, mahogany, rubber and palm trees are found
here.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following crops is/are grown in the Amazon rainforest region?
1. Coffee and cocoa
2. Tapioca
3. Wheat
4. Cassava
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, coffee, cocoa, tapioca
and cassava are grown in the Amazon rainforest region.
In Amazon forest, the staple food is cassava that grows
under the ground like the potato. Cash crops like
coffee, maize, tapioca and cocoa are also grown.
Wheat is not grown in Amazon rainforest. Wheat is
grown in temperate and subtropical regions like India,
China, USA, Russia, etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The tropical Eastern margins of continents between 10° to 30° N are characterised by tropical deciduous vegetation.
2. There is seasonal reversal of winds in the tropical Eastern continental margins.
3. Tropical eastern continental margins are characterised by the presence of lateritic soils.
Which of the statements given above are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
None of the given statement is incorrect.
Between 10° to 30° North, the tropical Eastern edge of
the continents has a humid and dry season. Due to this,
the forest becomes green during the rainy season and
the plant sheds its leaves in the dry season. That’s why
tropical deciduous vegetation is found along the tropical
eastern edge of the continents between 10° to 30°
North. The seasonal reversal of winds occurs along the
tropical Eastern continental margin. The tropical
Eastern continental marginal is characterised by the
presence of lateral soils.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Tropical Savanna region?

answerOptions.text: This region experiences high range of annual temperature.
It is well developed in Africa around the equatorial region.
National parks and sanctuaries are established inside the Savanna regions.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about Tropical
Savanna region as this region experiences high range of
annual temperature. In Savanna annual temperature is
greater than 18°C. The monthly temperature hovers
between 20° C and 32° C.
It is confined within the tropics and is best developed
in Africa; it is a transitional type of climate found
between the equatorial rainforests and hot deserts.
Large numbers of big animals or other are found in
Savanna region and their numbers are decreasing due
to hunting, for this reason national parks and
sanctuaries are established in Savanna region.
29. Tropical Savanna regions mostly occur in which
of the following regions?
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)
1. Amazon basin 2. Brazilian plateau
3. Orinoco basin
Codes
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3
(c) 1 and 3 (d) All of these
Ans. (b)

Exp. In South America, Savanna regions are found in
the Orinoco basin and the Brazilian plateau or
highlands.
Some of the other regions which include tropical
Savanna are Serengeti plains of Tanzania, the vast
Acacia plains of East Africa and savannas of Venezuela.
In Amazon basin, tropical rainforests (not Savanna
regions) are found.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements are correct about the human habitations in Sahara Desert?
1. Tuareg are settled agricultural communities in the region.
2. Crops such as rice and wheat are grown in the oasis regions in Sahara.
3. Important minerals such as uranium are mined in the Sahara region.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct about the human
habitations in Sahara desert. People live around the oasis
region in the Sahara where water is available, and they
grow date palms. Crops such as wheat, rice, barley and
beans are also grown in the Sahara oasis. Uranium is
abundant in the Sahara and has historically been
important in Niger. The main minerals found in the
Sahara desert are iron, phosphorus, manganese and
uranium.
Statement (1) is incorrect because Tuareg are nomadic
agricultural communities in the Sahara Desert region.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about the characteristics of Mediterranean region?
1. Warm and dry summers and cool and moist winters
2. Occurrence of cyclones in winter season
3. Fruits and grape cultivation
4. Presence of coniferous trees
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about the
characteristics of Mediterranean region.
Mediterranean region has hot, dry summers and cool,
wet winters.
In the Mediterranean region, in winter, the convergence
of cold air from the North and warm air from the South is
the cause of cyclones.
Mediterranean regions are famous for their fruit
cultivation. The trees in this region adapt themselves to
the dry summers with the help of their thick barks and
wax coated leaves which reduce transpiration. Traditional
Mediterranean fruit and nut crops include grapes, olives,
figs and almonds. The Mediterranean vegetation is
dominated by evergreen shrubs and presence of
coniferous trees.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following regions is characterised by mid-latitude desert vegetation?
1. Tibetan Plateau 2. Sahara Desert
3. Patagonia Plateau 4. Savanna Region
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Tibetan Plateau and Patagonia plateau are
characterised by mid-latitude desert. These
mid-latitude desert basins lay hundreds of miles from
the sea, and are sheltered by the high mountains all
around them. The mid-latitude desert is an excessively
dry region with an arid climate.
Sahara Desert and Savanna Region are low latitude arid
desert.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2021)

The vegetation of Savanna consists of grassland with scattered small trees. The forest development in such areas is generally kept in check by one or more or a combination of some conditions. 
Which of the following are such conditions?
1. Borrowing animals and termites
2. Fire
3. Grazing herbivores
4. Seasonal rainfall
5. Soil properties
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Fire, Grazing herbivores and seasonal rainfall are
correct conditions for Savanna vegetation.
Fire or Lightning is a natural ignition source and
Savanna vegetation that is flammable during the dry
winter period. Thus, it is prone to fire during the
dormant season of the year.
Grazing herbivores play a major role in maintaining
Savanna landscapes. Smaller herbivores graze on lower
seedling and saplings, preventing them to growing into
larger things, while larger herbivores like elephants fell
down trees, stop them growing as much and prevent
them from dominating.
Savannas grow in tropical regions 8° to 20° from the
Equator. Conditions are warm to hot in all seasons but
significant rainfall occurs for only a few months each

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect about the Ladakh cold desert region?

answerOptions.text: There is a great difference between day and night temperature in Ladakh during summers.
It is characterised by growth of Poplars and Willow.
Most of the cultivation of wheat and barley take place in the winter season.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect about the Ladakh cold
desert region because wheat and barley are the
traditional crops of Ladakh region and remain the
staple food of the people. Wheat and barley crops are
grown in the summer season. Here, grain is grown for
the dual purpose of food and fodder.

answerOptions.text: Agriculture is complemented by animal husbandry with rearing of sheep, goat and Yak.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Temperate Grasslands) (Region) A. Velds 1. Argentina B. Downs 2. South Africa C. Pampas 3. Central Asia D. Steppes 4. Australia
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-1, D- 3.
The temperate grasslands of South Africa are called the
Veld grasslands. It is a flat open land, with grass and no
trees.
Downs are temperate, grasslands in Australia located to
the West of South-East Queensland. It is mostly treeless
grasslands; covered with black agricultural soil.
Pampas are temperate grasslands found in Argentina in
South America. They are flat, fertile plains, covered with
grass.
Steppe are temperate grasslands found in Eastern
Europe and Central Asia. They are characterised by dry
and grassy plain.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following characteristics are associated with mid-latitude grassland regions?
1. In USA and Canada, this region is characterised by extensive mechanised agriculture.
2. The wheat and maize grown in USA and Canada region is mostly consumed in domestic markets.
3. In Australia and New Zealand, this region has commercialised pastoral industry.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Characteristics given in statements (1) and (3) are
associated with mid-latitude grassland regions.
Prairies are ecosystems considered part of the
temperate grasslands which is found in USA and
Canada. Extensive mechanised commercial grain
farming is practiced in Prairie grassland. In Australia
and New Zealand, the region has commercialised
Pastoral industry due to fair and suitable climatic
conditions and better mechanisation.
Statement (2) is not a characteristic associated with
mid-latitude grassland region as the wheat and maize
grown in USA and Canada region is mostly exported in
international market.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is/are characteristics of commercial pastoral agriculture practised in the mid-latitude grasslands region?

answerOptions.text: Use of large scale machines in processing and packaging.
Exports of meat and dairy products to international markets.
Use of manual labour in the industry.

answerOptions.rationale:
Characteristics of commercial pastoral agriculture
given in statement (a) and (b) are practised in the
mid-latitude grasslands region.
Extensive mechanised commercial grain farming is
practiced in mid-latitude grasslands. There is a shortage
of labour in these areas and the production of food
grains is excessive, due to which machines are used on a
large scale in processing and packaging in these areas.
Livestock are reared on large farms in these areas, of
which cows and sheep are important. The milk or dairy
product and meat of these animals are exported to
international markets.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is/are the characteristics of cool mid-latitude Western margin regions?
1. Westerly winds influence the climate of this region throughout the year.
2. Rainfall is mainly cyclonic and maximum rain occurs in winters.
3. Evergreen vegetation is found in this region.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Characteristics given in statements (1) and (2) are
of cool mid-latitude Western margin regions because
regions of this type are found on the Western margins
of the continents in the permanent zone of Westerlies.
This region is under the influence of westerly winds
throughout the year. The winters are warmer and
annual rainfall is higher than in cool East margin
region. Rainfall is of mainly cyclonic origin and occurs
throughout the year with a maximum in winter.
Statement (3) is not a characteristic of cool mid-latitude
Western margin region because Deciduous forest are
found in this region. Coniferous forests are found on hill
slopes.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about the warm mid-latitude East margin region?

answerOptions.text: During winter season, rainfall occurs through trade winds.
During summer season, rainfall occurs through westerly winds.
The oriental agriculture of China is characterised by intensive commercial farming in this region.
The occidental agriculture of USA specialises in cultivation of corn, tobacco and cotton in this region.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) is correct about the warm
mid-latitude East margin region occidental agriculture
extensive mechanised farming is done in USA.
Commercial crops like cotton and tobacco are
cultivated in occidental farming in USA.
The Warm Mid-latitude East margin region is located
between 30° to 45° North and South of the Equator on
the Eastern margins of the continents in the sub-tropical
belt.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Cool Mid-latitude Eastern margin region is mainly found in which of the following regions?

answerOptions.text: North-Eastern region of USA and Canada

answerOptions.rationale:
Cool mid-latitude Eastern margin region is
mainly found in North-Eastern United States and
adjoining parts of Canada, Korea, and Northern Japan.
This region lies pole ward of the warm East margin
region. The region has warm wet summer and cold dry
winters. It has laurentian type of climate. Annual range
of temperature is high as the summers are hot and
winters are very cold.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is/are the characteristics of Taiga coniferous forest region?
1. Nomadic herding and subsistence agriculture.
2. Short and warm summers and long and cold winters.
3. Lumbering in the winters and fishing in the summers.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Characteristics given in statements (2) and (3) are
of Taiga coniferous forest region.
In Taiga coniferous forest region, the climate is cold and
moist. The region has short warm summer and long cold
winter. Coniferous forests are found here and contain
softwood trees like oak, birch and maple. Lumbering is
the main occupation of the people.
While lumbering is common during winter, fishing is
practised in the short summer season, when the snow
cover melts.
Statement (1) is not the characteristic of this region
because people here do not practice nomadic herding
and subsistence agriculture.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which among the following are types of intensive subsistence agriculture?
1. Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by cultivation. wet paddy
2. Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by paddy. crops other than
3. Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by plantation agriculture.
4. Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by mixed farming.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are types of intensive
subsistence agriculture.
Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by wet
paddy cultivation is characterised by dominance of the
rice crop. Land holdings are very small due to the high
density of population.
Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by crops
other than paddy prevail in those areas where due to the
difference in relief, climate, soil and some of the other
geographical factors, it is not practical to grow paddy.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding extensive commercial grain cultivation?

answerOptions.text: Commercial grain cultivation is practised in the interior parts of semi-arid lands of the mid-latitudes.
The size of the farm is very small, therefore entire operations of cultivation from ploughing to harvesting are mechanised.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect regarding extensive
commercial grain cultivation because the size of the
farm is very large (not small). Therefore, entire
operations of cultivation from ploughing to harvesting
are mechanised.
Extensive commercial grain cultivation type of
agriculture is best developed in Eurasian steppes, the
Canadian and American Prairies, the Pampas of
Argentina, the Velds of South Africa, the Australian
Downs and the Canterbury Plains of New Zealand.

answerOptions.text: Wheat is the principal crop, though other crops like corn, barley, oats and rye are also grown.
There is low yield per acre but high yield per person.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct about pastoral nomadism?

answerOptions.text: It involves settling down of a group of nomads in a specified territory.
Cattle, sheep, goats and camel are reared by the nomadic communities for selling them in the market.
It is practised in the Tundra region of Eurasia and in the Madagascar Island.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct about pastoral nomadism
because pastoral nomadism is associated with three
important regions. The core region extends from the
Atlantic shores of North Africa eastwards across the
Arabian peninsula into Mongolia and Central China.
The second region extends over the Tundra region of
Eurasia. In the Southern Hemisphere, there are small
areas in South-West Africa and on the island of
Madagascar.
Statements (a), (b) and (d) are incorrect because these
shepherds depend on animals for food, clothing, shelter,
equipment and transport. They walk from one place to
another with their animals. The number of pastoral
nomads have decreased in the past few decades.

answerOptions.text: The number of pastoral nomads have increased in the past few decades.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is the most plausible explanation for the declining numbers of pastoral nomads across the world?
1. Emergence of political boundaries
2. Expansion in settled agriculture
3. Competition from industry
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Emergence of political boundaries and Expansion
in settled agriculture are the most plausible explanation
for declining numbers pastoral nomads across the
world. With the emergence of political boundaries, the
movement of pastoral nomads from one place to
another almost stopped, as can be seen in the region of
Tibet. Due to the expansion of agriculture in the areas
of these people, there was a gradual shortage of useful
space for their residence and living. For this reason,
their numbers are decreasing.
11. Which of the following crops is/are most
commonly grown in shifting cultivation?
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Maize (b) Banana
(c) Rice (d) Both ‘a’ and ‘b’
Ans. (d)

Exp. Maize and banana are most commonly grown in
shifting cultivation. This type of agriculture is done in
tropical areas. In this agriculture, only food grains are
grown more because it is livelihood agriculture. The
main crops of this agriculture are maize, cassava,
banana and sweet potato.
Rice is not grown in this agriculture.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Shifting List II Cultivation Name) (Region) A. Ladang 1. Zaire Basin B. Chengin 2. Central America C. Milpa 3. Philippines D. Konuko 4. Venezuela E. Masole 5. Malaysia
Codes A B C D E

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-5, B-3, C-2, D-4, E-1.
Shifting cultivation is known as Ladang in Malaysia,
Chengin in Philippines, Milpa in Central America and
Mexico, Konuko in Venezuela, Roca in Brazil, Masole in
Zaire Basin Central Africa.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is/are the features of sedentary agriculture?

answerOptions.text: Crop rotation to maintain fertility of soil.
Use of animals for obtaining manure for the field.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are the features of
sedentary agriculture. Sedentary agriculture is a
farming method in which the farmer lives in a
particular area of his choice.
The special feature of such agriculture is that the
farmers adopt the method of soil conservation and adopt
a cropping model. Fertiliser of the soil increases
through crop rotation.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is/are correct about intensive subsistence agriculture?
1. Family labour is used for agricultural operations and manual labour.
2. It is practised in regions with large landholdings and moderate density of population.
3. Farm yard manure is mainly used in this type of agriculture.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct about intensive
subsistence agriculture because, in intensive
subsistence agriculture, farmers work with the help of
family labour leading to intensive use of land. Farm
yard manure is used to maintain the fertility of the soil.
In this type of agriculture, the yield per unit area is
high but per labour.
Statement (2) is incorrect because in this type of
agriculture, landholdings are very small due to the high
density of population.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is a feature of plantation agriculture practised in different parts of the world?
1. Single crop specialisation
2. Well-developed transportation system
3. Scientific techniques of cultivation
4. Manual labour
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the features mentioned in the question are of
plantation agriculture practised in different parts of the
world. Plantation agriculture was introduced by the
Europeans in colonies situated in the tropics. Some of
the important plantation crops are tea, coffee, cocoa,
rubber, oil palm, sugarcane and pineapples.
The characteristic features of this type of farming are
large estates or plantations, managerial and technical
support, scientific methods of cultivation, single crop
specialisation, cheap labour and manual labour, and a
good system of transportation which links the estates to
the factories and markets for the export of the products.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Region) List II (Plantation) A. West Africa 1. Sugarcane B. Malaysia 2. Coconut and Sugar C. Philippines 3. Cocoa and Coffee D. Indonesia 4. Rubber Plantations
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1.
Plantation agriculture was introduced by the Europeans
in colonies situated in the tropic.
The French established cocoa and coffee plantations in
West Africa. The British set up large tea gardens in
India and Sri Lanka.
The British set up large rubber plantations in Malaysia.
Sugarcane and banana plantations in West Indies.
Spanish invested heavily in coconut and sugarcane
plantations in the Philippines.
The Dutch once had monopoly over sugarcane
plantation in Indonesia.

questions.question: Extensive agriculture is practised in which of the following regions of Asia? ( Chap 7, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

answerOptions.rationale:
Extensive agriculture (also known as commercial
grain cultivation) is practised in the interior parts of
semi-arid lands of the Central Asia. Wheat is the
principal crop, though other crops like corn, barley,
oats and rye are also grown. The size of the farm is very
large; therefore entire operations of cultivation from
ploughing to harvesting are mechanised.
22. Which of the following statements is/are correct
regarding extensive commercial grain farming?
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Extensive grain farming is practised in regions with
low population density.
(b) Very high production levels, for export markets.
(c) Mechanisation of farms and crop specialisation.
(d) All of the above
Ans. (d)

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following are the crops commonly grown in extensive commercial grain farming?
1. Wheat 2. Corn
3. Barley 4. Lentils
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Wheat, corn and barley are commonly grown in
extensive commercial grain farming. Commercial grain
cultivation is practised in the interior parts of semi-arid
lands of the mid-latitudes. Wheat is the principal crop,
though other crops like corn, barley and oats are also
grown.
Lentils are not grown in extensive commercial grain
farming as they Lentils are not a grain.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements correctly defines mixed farming?

answerOptions.text: Cultivation of crops in alternate rows and columns.
Cultivation of commercial crops with plantation crops.
Cultivation of citrus fruits and grains.
Cultivation of crops and rearing of animals.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) correctly defines mixed farming. It
is a type of farming which involves both the growing of
crops and the raising of livestock.
Mixed farms are moderate in size and usually the crops
associated with it are wheat, barley, maize, fodder and
root crops. Fodder crops are an important component
of mixed farming.
Equal emphasis is laid on crop cultivation and animal
husbandry. Animals like cattle, sheep, pigs and poultry
provide the main income along with crops.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

With reference to mixed farming, consider the following statements.
1. It involves primitive form of tools, techniques and traditional methods of cultivation.
2. Mixed Farming is practised in Europe, Eastern USA, Argentina, South-East Australia, New Zealand.
3. Crop rotation and mixed cropping practises are also used in Mixed farming.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to mixed farming because mixed farming is practised in
Europe, Eastern USA, Argentina, South-East Australia,
New Zealand and South Africa.
In mixed agriculture, crop rotation and intercropping
play an important role in maintaining soil fertility.
Statement (1) is incorrect because mixed farming is
characterised by high capital expenditure on farm
machinery and building, extensive use of chemical
fertilisers and green manure and also by the skill and
expertise of the farmers.
Animal Husbandry

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect about dairy farming practised in New Zealand?

answerOptions.text: Refrigeration and transport has enabled the export of milk products from New Zealand.
Milk products are marketed and sold through co-operatives.
Dairy farms are spread over large areas in New Zealand.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect about dairy farming
Practised in New Zealand because the Taranaki region
of the Northern Island of New Zealand has the highest
density of milch cows of all regions in the World.
The people here have gained proficiency in the milk
business from their experiences. Due to the good
weather here grass grows throughout the year and it
rains throughout the year.
Dairy farmers are not spread over large areas in New
Zealand.

answerOptions.text: Milk is converted into high value products for export to Europe.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct about dairy farming?

answerOptions.text: Dairy farmers grow fodder crops like corn and oats.
Large scale refrigeration and storage infrastructure are needed for dairy farming.
High yielding milch cows are used in dairy farms.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct about dairy
farming. In addition to milk production in dairy
agriculture, it also produces fodder crops, sorghum,
maize, oats and wheat, which are used as fodder. Like
labour, capital is also needed in this industry. The
management and infrastructure of milk refrigeration
and storage require more capital. The high yielding
milch cows in the world are reared in dairy farming.
Dairy is the most advanced and efficient type of rearing
of milch animals. It is highly capital intensive farming.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to dairy farming in the developed regions of the world?
1. It is a highly capital intensive occupation.
2. It involves labour intensive activities.
3. It is practised far away from the urban and industrial centres.
4. It is extensively practised in New Zealand and Tasmania in Australia.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct with
reference to dairy farming. It is highly capital intensive
farming. Dairy farming is highly labour intensive as it
involves rigorous care in feeding and milching. There
is no off season during the year as in the case of crop
raising. It is widely practiced in Tasmania, New
Zealand and Australia because of the high number of
milch cows and the use of mechanisation here. Due to
the good weather, grass grows throughout the year and
it rains throughout the year.
Statement (3) is incorrect because, dairy farming is
practised mainly near urban and industrial centres
which provide neighbourhood market for fresh milk
and dairy products.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion

Commercial Grazing is organised on scientific basis and special emphasis is put upon genetic improvements and disease control. Reason (R) Commercial Grazing is practised in ranches which are divided into different parcels according to their carrying capacity. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
answerOptions.rationale:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but
Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion
(A). Commercial grazing is essentially associated with
Western cultures and is practiced on permanent
ranches.
These ranches cover large areas and are divided into a
number of parcels, which are fenced to regulate the
grazing.
The number of animals in a pasture is kept according to
the carrying capacity of the pasture.
Grazing of animals in ranching is organised on a

emphasis on the use of irrigation, high yielding seeds,
fertilisers, insecticides, greenhouses and artificial
heating in colder regions. This type of agriculture is
well-developed in North-Western Europe,
North-Eastern United States of America and the
Mediterranean regions.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following cooperative farming methods emerged in the former Soviet Union?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Kolkhoz was a special type of agricultural
farm of the Soviet Union, whose theoretical basis is the
communist agricultural management.
Under the First Five Year Plan of the Soviet Union,
Kolkhoz was started in traditional agricultural areas on
the basis of collective ownership. Under this, many
families were collectively given permanent rent-free
ownership of government land.

questions.question:

the entire life span of the crop is between 21° and 37°C.

more than 100 cm.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct regarding
sugarcane production. Sugarcane is a tropical as well as
a subtropical crop that grows well in hot and humid
climate. It requires temperature of 21°C to 27°C and an

second largest producer of sugarcane only after Brazil.

questions.question:

subtropical regions like Egypt, India, China and USA.

Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct with
reference to the Jal Kranti Abhiyan. It was launched by

water in the country.

Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and citizens,

windward side of Western Ghats. Due to heavy rainfall

here. In wetland farming, the rainfall is in excess of soil
moisture requirement of plants during rainy season.

answerOptions.rationale:

producer of rice in the world after China.

contributing about 14.33% of the total rice production
from 12.8% of the rice producing area of the country.

network of canal irrigation and tubewells has made it
possible to grow rice in areas of dry regions of Haryana
and Western Uttar Pradesh in India.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to the
cultivation of wheat in India. Wheat is primarily a crop
of temperate zone. Hence, its cultivation in India is
done during winter i.e. Rabi season. This rabi crop
requires a cool growing season and a bright sunshine at
the time of ripening. It requires 50 to 75 cm of annual
rainfall evenly distributed over the growing season.
Statements (2) and (3) are incorrect because in West
Bengal farmers grow three crops of rice called Aus,
Aman and Boro. India is not is the largest producer of
wheat while China is the largest producer.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-X, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about food security.
1. India’s food security policy has a primary objective to ensure availability of foodgrains to the common people at an affordable price.
2. The focus of the policy is on growth in agriculture production and on fixing the support price for procurement of wheat and rice, to maintain their stocks.
3. Public Distribution System (PDS) is responsible for procuring and stocking foodgrains, whereas distribution is ensured by Food Corporation of India (FCI).
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding food
security. The fundamental goal of India’s food security
strategy is to ensure that foodgrains are available to the
general public at a reasonable cost. It has made it
possible for the destitute to obtain food. The strategy
focuses on increasing agricultural production and
maintaining stock levels by establishing the support
price for wheat and rice procurement.
Statement (3) is incorrect because Food Corporation of
India (FCI) is responsible for procuring and stocking
foodgrains, whereas distribution is ensured by Public
Distribution System (PDS).

nearly 95%, fewest impurities and highest energy
density of all types of coal.

(45% to 70%) and burns with smoky flames. Its colour is
brown. During the burning of lignite coal, long smoky
flames come out. Lignite coal was originated after
bituminous coal, so it has more vegetation content.

has less proportion of vegetal matter. Peat coal has the
lowest carbon content. It is the lowest form of coal.

questions.question:

Arrange the following types of coal in increasing order of their quality in terms of carbon content, with the help of codes given below.
1. Peat 2. Lignite
3. Anthracite 4. Bituminous
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The increasing order of coal of their quality in
terms of carbon content is peat coal, lignite coal,
bituminous coal and anthracite coal.
Anthracite contains 86% to 97% carbon. Anthracite coal
has the highest heating value of all ranks of coal.
Bituminous coal contains 70% to 90% carbon. It has a
lower heating value than anthracite coal.
Lignite coal typically contains 45% to 70% carbon, and it
has a lower heating value than bituminous coal.
Peat coal contains 25% to 35% carbon and it has the
lowest energy content of all coal ranks.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following techniques can be most helpful in conservation of mineral resources on the Earth?
1. Recycling of metallic minerals
2. Efficient utilisation transport infrastructure
3. Shifting to non-conventional energy resources
4. Plantation of trees on barren lands
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Techniques mentioned in statements (1) and (3)
can be most helpful in conservation of mineral
resources on the Earth because mineral resources are
exhaustible resources. Therefore, it is necessary to
protect them.
It is also possible to conserve minerals by re-using
metals. Recycling of some metals can also save their
reserves.
Mineral resources can also be conserving by promoting
the use of non-conventional energy resources like bio
gas, tidal energy, wind or solar power, etc.
Techniques mentioned in statements (2) and (4) will not
be helpful because efficient utilisation transport
infrastructure and plantation of trees on barren lands are
not helpful for conservation of mineral resources.

answerOptions.rationale:

well-being of rural communities in developing
countries, reduce pollution, increase self-sufficiency and
reduce the demand for fuel wood.
