and manufactures fine clothes in bulk.
The cotton industry requires working capital to
overcome price volatility. The cotton industry has to
face very stiff competition with synthetic fibres hence it
has now shown a declining trend in many countries.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct about synthetic fibres industry?

answerOptions.text: The first Rayon factory of the world was started by HB de Chardonnet.
The synthetic textiles obtain their raw materials from chemicals based industries.
Natural fibres are more stronger and versatile than synthetic fibres.

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (a) and (b) are correct about
synthetic fibres industry. The synthetic fibres industry
originated in France. In 1884, a French chemist, H B
de Chardonnet, made synthetic fibres from the
nitro-cellulose process.
Synthetic textiles get their raw material from chemical
based industries. Synthesised polymers are obtained
from coal and petroleum by chemical technology.
Statement (c) is incorrect because natural fibres are less
stronger and versatile then synthetic fibres.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class VIII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements are correct regarding petrochemicals?
1. Chemicals which are obtained from petroleum and natural gas are called petrochemicals.
2. Hydrogen gas is obtained as a petrochemical from natural gas.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding petrochemicals. These are chemicals
obtained from petroleum and natural gas. Hydrogen gas
is obtained as a petrochemical from natural gas. It is
used in manufacture of fertilisers. Petroleum is not only
a source of fuels but also provides raw materials for
manufacture of large number of useful substances.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Petrochemicals Industry ) (Country) A. Philadelphia and Delaware 1. Belgium B. Antwerp 2. USA C. Ras Tanura 3. Canada D. Montreal 4. Saudi Arabia
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2 B-1 C-4 D-3.
Petrochemical Industry is located in Philadelphia and
the Great Lakes region of Delaware and Chicago.
The concentration of the Petrochemical industry in
Europe is closer to those areas where the demand is
high. The Petrochemical industry in Belgium is located
in the Antwerp region.
The Petrochemical industry is located in Ras Tanura in
Saudi Arabia and Mina Al Ahmadi in Kuwait.
The Petrochemical industry in Canada is located in
Montreal. Here oil is brought by pipeline from Portland.
The second Petrochemical industry in Canada is located
in Sarnia.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given techniques is/are used in high technology industry?
1. Robotics and Assembly lines
2. Computer Aided Design
3. Electronic control of manufacturing processes
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given techniques are used in high
technology industry which includes latest generation of

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is/are the features of high technology industry?

answerOptions.text: Blue collar workers are mostly employed in these industries.
Research and development facilities are located in these industries.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is the feature of high technology
industry because high technology industry is the latest
generation of manufacturing activities. It is best
understood as the application of intensive research and
development efforts leading to the manufacture of
products of an advanced scientific and engineering
character.
Statements (a) and (c) are not its feature because white
collar workers are mostly employed in high technology
industry. These are characterised by neatly spaced, low,
modern, dispersed, office-plant-lab buildings rather
than massive assembly structures.

answerOptions.text: These are characterised by massive assembly structures.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement is correct about knowledge industry?

answerOptions.text: There has been a rapid growth in demand for the consumption of knowledge based services in the modern economy.
Knowledge industry is not tied to resources or affected by markets.
Most of the knowledge sector companies operate in the localised markets.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (b) are correct about
knowledge industry because the knowledge economy is
a system of consumption and production based on
intellectual capital. This sector is growing rapidly.
Currently more than half of all workers developed
economies are in knowledge sector and has grown
much more in demand and consumption of information
based services from mutual fund managers tax
consultants, software developers and statistician.
Like some of the tertiary functions, knowledge economy
activities can also be outsourced. They are not tied to
resources, affected by the environment or necessarily
localised by market.
Statement (c) is incorrect because most of the
knowledge sector companies operate in the world
markets.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class XII, New NCERT)

People, materials, and manufactured commodities are physically transported from one area to another through transportation. Which among the following is/are the factors affecting Transport systems? 
1. Demand for transport is influenced by the size of population. The larger the population size, the greater is the demand for transport.
2. Routes depend on location of cities, towns, villages, industrial centres and raw materials, pattern of trade between them, nature of the landscape between them, type of climate, and funds available for overcoming obstacles along the length of the route.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are given above are
the factors affecting transport systems. It is an
organised industry created to satisfy man’s basic need
of mobility. Modern society requires speedy and
efficient transport systems to assist in the production,
distribution and consumption of goods. At every stage
in this complex system, the value of the material is
significantly enhanced by transportation.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following services is an alternative to outsourcing?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Home shoring is an
alternative to outsourcing. Home shoring is an
organisational operational model in which employees
work and perform all official tasks from a home or
external office. New trends in quinary services include
knowledge processing outsourcing and home shoring,
the latter as an alternative to outsourcing.
Industrial Regions

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Industrial Centre ) (Famous for) A. London 1. Glass industry B. Birmingham 2. Heavy machinery C. Charleroi 3. Paper and Pulp Industry D. Sweden 4. Textiles
Codes A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-4 B-2 C-1 D-3.
The UK is the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution.
Due to the favourable climate and location in
London, the textile industry is located around the
River Thames.
Birmingham in the Midland region of Britain is the
center of iron and steel and heavy machinery.
Charleroi is a Belgian city in the Walloon province of
Hainaut.
The Charleroi municipality contains an industrial area
for electrical engineering and the production of iron,
steel, glass and chemicals.
In the Southern part of Sweden from Stockholm to the
Southern shores of Lake Vnen there is a pulp and paper
and wood industry based on forest resources.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Match the given lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Hydel Project) (River) A. Bhakra Nangal Project 1. Krishna B. Hirakud Dam 2. Sutlej C. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam 3. Chambal D. Gandhi Sagar Dam 4. Mahanadi
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.
Bhakra Dam It is a concrete gravity dam and second
tallest dam on the Sutlej river in Bilaspur, Himachal
Pradesh in Northern India.
Hirakud Dam It is built across the Mahanadi River, about
15 kilometres from Sambalpur in the State of Odisha. It
is the longest dam in the world.
Nagarjuna Sagar Dam It is a masonry dam across the
Krishna River at Nagarjuna Sagar which straddles the
border between Nalgonda district in Telangana and
Guntur district in Andhra Pradesh.
The Gandhi Sagar Dam It is one of the four major dams
built on India’s Chambal river. The dam is located in the
Mandsaur, districts of the state of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-X, Old NCERT)

The Gobind Sagar lake is a man-made lake. It forms a reservoir of which of the following multi- purpose projects?

answerOptions.rationale:
Gobind Sagar lake is a man-made reservoir formed
by the Bhakra Nangal Dam. It is situated in Una and
Bilaspur districts of Himachal Pradesh.
The reservoir is on the river Sutlej and is named in
honour of Guru Gobind Singh.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Tehri Hydropower project?
1. Tehri Hydro Development Corporation was set up in 1988 for implementation of this project.
2. It is the highest gravity dam in India and it has been constructed on river Son.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to Tehri
Hydropower project. Tehri Hydro Development
Corporation India Limited is under the ownership of
National Thermal Power Corporation Limited,
Ministry of Power and Government of India. It was
incorporated in July 1988 to develop, operate and
maintain the Tehri Hydro Power Complex and other
Hydro Projects.
Statement (2) is incorrect because it is the tallest dam
in India and it has been constructed on Bhagirathi
River.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-X, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Industries) (Basis of Classification) A. Metallurgical 1. On the basis of ownership industries B. Public and Private 2. On the basis of nature of industries manufactured products C. Agro based industry 3. On the basis of use of products D. Intermediate goods 4. On the basis of nature of raw industry material used
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4 and D-3.
Metallurgical industries are based on the nature of the
manufactured products. Metallurgical industries
generate vast quantities of different types of wastes
such as the flue dust of secondary copper smelting,
which might be attached to construction materials in
workshops.
Public and private industries are based on the basis of
ownership. The private sector comprises businesses,
which are owned, managed and controlled by
individuals. Public sector comprises various business
enterprises owned and managed by the Government.
Agro based industries are based on the basis of nature of
raw material used.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to factors affecting the location of industries.
1. Industries which use weight losing raw materials are located closer to the sources of raw materials.
2. Iron and steel industry mainly uses weight-losing raw materials.
3. Industries which are based on perishable raw materials are located closer to the markets.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to factors affecting the location of industries. Industries
using weight losing raw materials are located in the
regions where raw materials are located. Like pulp
industry, copper smelting and big iron industries are
located near their raw materials. In iron and steel
industries, iron ore and coal both are weight-losing raw
materials. Therefore, an optimum location for iron and
steel industries should be near raw material sources.
Statement (3) is incorrect because industries based on
perishable raw materials are also located close to raw
material sources.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

In India, which of the given industries are most likely to be located closer to the sources of power?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given option, aluminium
manufacturing industry tends to be located near
sources of power because they are power intensive and
require huge quantum of electricity. Power provides
the motive force for machines and therefore, its supply
has to be ensured before the location of any industry.
4. Consider the following statements with reference
to iron and steel industries in India.
(Chap 5, Class-VIII, New NCERT)
1. Bhilai and Rourkela steel plants were started in
India for the purpose of balanced regional
development.
2. Iron and Steel is a basic industry on which most of
the sectors of Indian industries depend.
3. Fireclay, limestone and coking coal are common
raw materials used in this industry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3
(c) 1 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3
Ans. (d)

Exp. All the given statements are correct with
reference to iron and steel industries in India.
The Bhilai Steel Plant was established with Russian
collaboration in Chhattisgarh and started production in
1959. The Rourkela Steel Plant was set up in 1959 in
Odisha in collaboration with Germany.
Bhilai and Rourkela steel plants were started in India
for the purpose of balanced regional development in
tribal region. Iron and steel industry is a basic industry
on which most of the sectors of Indian industries
depend.
The other raw materials besides iron ore and coking
coal, essential for iron and steel industry are limestone,
dolomite, manganese and fireclay.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO)? 
1. It was established on the confluence of Yamuna and Chambal.
2. The Iron ore is obtained from Noamundi and Badam Pahar.
3. It lies very close to Mumbai-Kolkata railway line.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to TISCO. The iron ore for the TISCO plant is obtained
from Noamundi and Badam Pahar and coal is brought
from Joda mines in Odisha. Coking coal comes from
Jharia and West Bokaro coal fields. The Tata Iron and
Steel Company Limited lies very close to the
Mumbai-Kolkata railway line.
Statement (1) is incorrect because TISCO was
established on the confluence of Subarnarekha and
Kharkai river.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Vishvesvaraiya Iron and Steel Works.
1. It is located near Kemmangundi in the Baba Budan Hills.
2. Coal is abundantly available locally near this power plant.
3. Bhadravati river supplies water to this plant.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct with reference
to the Vishvesvaraiya Iron and Steel Works. It was
initially called the Mysore Iron and Steel Works. It is
located close to an iron ore producing area of
Kemmangundi in the Baba Budan hills. The Bhadravati
river supplies water to the plant. This plant produces
specialised steels and alloys.
Statement (2) is incorrect because coal is abundantly not
available locally near this power plant.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Iron and Steel Plant) (State) A. Durgapur Steel Plant 1. Odisha B. Rourkela Steel Plant 2. Chhattisgarh C. Bhilai Steel Plant 3. West Bengal D. Vizag Steel Plant 4. Andhra Pradesh
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.
Durgapur Steel Plant in West Bengal was set up in
collaboration with the government of the United
Kingdom and started production in 1962.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following multipurpose project supplies water to the Rourkela Integrated Steel Plant in Sundargarh?

answerOptions.rationale:
Hirakud Project supplies water to the Rourkela
integrated Steel Plant in Sundargarh. The Rourkela
Steel Plant was set up in 1959 in the Sundargarh
district of Odisha in collaboration with Germany.
The Hirakud project supplies power for the electric
furnaces and water is obtained from the Koel and
Sankh rivers.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2017)

Which of the following Iron and Steel Plant is not in the Vicinity of its raw material?

answerOptions.rationale:
Durgapur Iron and Steel Plant is not close to the
raw material area.
Durgapur Steel Plant is one of the integrated steel
plants of Steel Authority of India Limited, located in
Durgapur, in the Eastern state of West Bengal.
The Iron and Steel Plants are located near the source of
raw materials in India because the Iron and Steel
industry is a heavy and large scale industry.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following iron and steel plant of India is located near the Raniganj and Jharia coal belt and is connected with Kolkata-Delhi railway route?

answerOptions.rationale:
Durgapur Steel Plant lies in Raniganj and Jharia
coal belt in West Bengal. It gets iron ore from
Noamundi. Durgapur Steel Plant lies on the
Kolkata-Delhi railway route.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-X, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2019)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion
Ahmedabad is the largest centre of cotton textile industry in India. Reason (R) Ahmedabad is located in major cotton growing region of India, so it has no problem of raw materials. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
answerOptions.rationale:
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
Mumbai, Maharashtra is the largest centre of cotton
textile industry, which is followed by Ahmedabad.
Ahmedabad being located in India’s major cotton
production area, it does not face any raw material
problem.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Shahpur and Calico cotton mills were established in Ahmedabad in Gujarat.
Ahmedabad is known as the ‘Manchester of India’ due to its textile production.
Power loom sector produces more cotton than the organised handloom sector of India.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct. The
Shahpur Mill and the Calico Mill were established in
Ahmedabad. It soon became the second largest textile
city of India, after Mumbai.
Ahmedabad was therefore often referred to as the
‘Manchester of India’ due to textile production.
Power loom sector produces more cotton in less time
than the organised handloom sector of India.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is not correct
with reference to factors determining setting up of cotton textile industries in various regions?

answerOptions.text: Cotton textile mills have been set up in Kolkata due to its port facilities.
Rapid development of cotton textile industry in Tamil Nadu is attributed to cheap availability of cotton import.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect because the rapid
development of this industry in Tamil Nadu is the result
of the abundant availability of hydro power for the mills.
Lower labour costs at centres like Coimbatore and
Tirunelveli also caused industries to be located away
from cotton-producing areas.

answerOptions.text: Nagpur, Indore, Sholapur and Vadodara are important cotton textile centres in the Central India.
Lower labour costs has led to development of this industry in Ujjain, Bharuch, Agra and Hathras.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to sugar industry of India?
1. The first modern sugar mill was started in India in Bihar in 1903.
2. It uses weight losing raw material and sugarcane has to be crushed within 24 hours of its harvesting.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to sugar industry of India.
Development of the sugar industry on modern lines
dates back to 1903, when a sugar mill was started in
Bihar. Subsequently, sugar mills were started in other
parts of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. It uses weight losing
raw material. Better recovery of sugar is dependent
upon its being crushed within 24 hours of its harvesting.
Thus, sugar factories are located within the cane
producing regions.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to sugar production in India?

answerOptions.text: Andhra Pradesh is the largest sugar producing state in India.
Highest number of sugar mills are located in Gujarat.
Most of the sugar is produced in India in the states of Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct with reference to sugar
production in India. Most of the sugar is produced in
India in the states of Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and
Karnataka. Uttar Pradesh is leading/largest sugar
producer in the country.
Maharashtra is the second largest producer of sugar.
Karnataka is the major producer of sugar in India.
Belagavi, Bellary, Mandya, Shivmoga and Chitradurga
districts are the major producers in Karnataka. The
sugar industry is distributed in the coastal regions.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The petrochemical industry in India constitutes,
which of the following?
1. Polymers
2. Synthetic fibres
3. Elastomers
4. Surfactant intermediates
Codes

answerOptions.text: Exp. The petrochemical group of industries is divided into four sub-groups, polymers, synthetic fibres; elastomers and surfactant intermediates. Petrochemical industries are the major source of organic and inorganic toxic pollutants. 22. Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to polymer and synthetic fibre industry in India?
More than 75% polymer units are found in the small scale sector of India.
Acrylic staple fibre industry is located in Kota and Vadodara in Gujarat.
Production of plastic polymers started in India in 1960s in Mumbai.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are incorrect
with reference to knowledge based industries in India?

answerOptions.text: The IT software and IT enabled services are growing at a robust rate in India and contribute to more than 25% in GDP.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect with reference to
knowledge based industries in India as the IT software
and IT enabled services are growing at a robust rate in
India and contribute to more than 8% in GDP in 2019.
Indian software industry has emerged as one of the
fastest growing sectors in the economy.
Statements (b), (c) and (d) are correct because the Indian
information technology and business process
management industry had over 4 million employed
personnel during financial year 2021. Software
technology industry has surpassed the electronics
manufacturing industry in India. International
recognition has been accorded to IT sector of India.

answerOptions.text: The IT sector provides employment to a large number of people which has almost doubled every year.
Software technology industry has surpassed the electronics manufacturing industry in India.
India’s IT sector has been accorded international recognition.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

India has setup a Software Technology park in,
which of the following cities of India?

answerOptions.rationale:
India has set up software technology parks at the
cities like Kanpur, Mohali, Noida, Hyderabad,
Bengaluru, Jaipur, Navi Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai etc.
Software Technology parks of India are Science and
Technology organisation established by the Indian
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology in
1991 with the objective of encouraging, promoting and
boosting the export of software from India.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which one of the following industries uses limestone as a principal raw material? (CGPSC Pre 2017)

answerOptions.rationale:
Cement industry uses limestone as a principal
raw material. Due to this, cement industry is mainly
located in the areas having an abundance of limestone.
Limestone is used as a building material and to purify
iron in blast furnaces. Beside, manufacturing of
cement, it is also used in the manufacture of glass.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The first cement plant of India was established in Chennai.
2. India’s cement factory is the second largest in the world after China.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct.
The first cement plant was set up in 1904 in
Madras/Chennai. It was set up by a company called
South India Industrial Ltd. India’s cement factory is
the second largest in the world after China.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to fertiliser industry in India?

answerOptions.text: India does not have any reserves of commercially usable potassium.
Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Punjab and Kerala are the important states which produce most of the fertiliser of India.
Fertiliser units can be found in private as well as cooperative sector of India.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct with reference to
fertiliser industry in India. India does not have any
reserves of commercially usable potassium. Potash is
entirely imported as the country does not have any
reserves of commercially usable potash or potassium
compounds in any form.
After the Green Revolution, the industry expanded to
several other parts of the country. Gujarat, Tamil Nadu,
Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Kerala contribute towards
half of the fertiliser production. Fertiliser units can be
found in private as well as cooperative sector of India.
Industrial Regions of India

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is not a major industrial region in India?
1. Hooghly region
2. Kolhapur-South Kannada region
3. Gujarat region
4. Vishakhapatnam-Guntur region
5. Durg-Raipur region
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Kolhapur-South Kannada and Durg-Raipur region
are not major industrial regions in India.
Mumbai-Pune, Hooghly, Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu,
Gujarat, Chhota Nagpur, Vishakhapatnam- Guntur,
Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut and
Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram region are major
industrial regions in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Hooghly industrial region.
1. Kolkata-Howrah forms the core of this industrial region.
2. Development of tea plantations in Assam has led to rapid development of this region.
3. Establishment of jute mill at Rishra in 1855 led to the development of this region in the initial period.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
with reference to Hooghly industrial region. This
region is located along the Hooghly river.
Kolkata-Howrah region is forms the core of the Hooghly
industrial region.
Development of tea plantation in Assam and Northern
hills of West Bengal, contributed to the industrial
development of the region.
The establishment of first jute mill at Rishra in 1855
ushered in the era of modern industrial clustering in
this region.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The industrial centres such as Bansberia, Budge- Budge, Kakinara, Shamnagar, Titagarh, Belur etc., are important industrial centres of which of the following industrial region?

answerOptions.rationale:
The important industrial centres of Hooghly
industrial region are Kolkata, Howrah, Haldia,
Serampur, Rishra, Shibpur, Naihati, Kakinara,
Shamnagar, Titagarh, Sodepur, Budge-Budge, Birla
Nagar, Bansberia, Belgurriah, Triveni, Hooghly, Belur,
etc. Hooghly industrial region is located along the
Hooghly River, this region extends from Bansberia in
the North to Birla Nagar in the South for a distance of
about 100 km.
35. Consider the following statements with reference
to Bengaluru-Chennai Industrial Region.
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)
1. The primary factor for the growth of this industrial
region was the coal obtained from nearby
coalfields.
2. Cotton growing areas are mostly developed
around this region.
3. The development of Pykara Hydroelectric plant in
1932 has provided an impetus to this region.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are
correct?
(a) 1 and 3 (b) 1 and 2
(c) 2 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3
Ans. (c)

Exp. Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to Bengaluru-Chennai Industrial Region because
cotton textile industry was the first to take roots due to
the presence of cotton growing areas in
Bengaluru-Chennai industrial region. Along with
cotton mills, loom industry spread very rapidly.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect with reference to Gujarat industrial region?

answerOptions.text: Development of this region is associated with the development of cotton textile industry.
Petrochemicals industry is well developed around Gujarat industrial region due to the discovery of oil fields.
It has the advantage of both market as well as nearness to raw materials.
The establishment of Nhava Sheva port has aided in the development of Gujarat industrial region.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) is incorrect with reference to
Gujarat Industrial region because the establishment of
Kandla Port has aided in the development of Gujarat
industrial region. Development of this region is also
associated with the location of the cotton textile
industry since 1860s. Located in cotton growing area,
this region has double advantage of the proximity of
raw materials as well as of market.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Chhota Nagpur industrial region.
1. It extends over Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.
2. It is known for the presence of Heavy metallurgical industries.
3. The main source of power in this region is the energy generated from nearby nuclear power plants.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to
Chhota Nagpur industrial region because Chhota
Nagpur industrial region owes its development to the
discovery of coal in the Damodar Valley. To meet the
power requirement, thermal and hydroelectric plants
have been constructed in the Damodar Valley.
The main source of power in this region is the energy
generated from nearby thermal and hydroelectric plants.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the given factors is/are responsible for the development of Rhine valley as an industrial region?
1. Presence of rich uranium resources
2. Well-connected railways network
3. High density of population
4. Presence of well-built canal system
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2), (3) and (4) are the factors
responsible for the development of Rhine valley as an
industrial because the Rhine Valley is known as an
industrial area. The Ruhr coalfield is located in the
lower Rhine valley.
In addition to mineral resources, this region is
connected by railway network, waterways of the Rhine
and canals. This area is the densely populated area of
Europe. There is also a big local market here.
Statement (1) is not a factor responsible for the
development of Rhine valley as an industrial region
because there is no presence of rich uranium resources
in the industrial area of the Rhine valley.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the given factors is/are responsible for development of the New England region as an industrial complex in North America?
1. Development of Hydroelectric power
2. Presence of densely forested region
3. Presence of large reserves of Limestone
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are the factors responsible
for development of the New England region as an
industrial complex in North America. Many factors are
responsible for the industrial development of New
England. Immigrants from Europe first settled in this
area. The density of population here was high. Being a
mountainous area, hydroelectric power was available
from small rivers. New England region is also known as
industrial region.
Statement (3) is not a factor because there is no
presence of large reserves of limestone in the industrial
area of the New England region on North America.

questions.question:

The city of Ivanovo is located on the banks of the Uvod

major textile cities of Russia, producing cotton, and silk
goods and clothing.
The Nizhny Novgorod region is one of the largest
industrial centers of the Russian Federation with a great
potential in machinery.
Vladivostok region is famous for steel industry and
shipbuilding.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (d) is incorrectly matched because the
Kuznetsk Basin, in Russia’s South-Western Siberia, is
one of Russia’s largest coal mining areas. Iron and steel
industries, coal mining industries, machinery industries
etc have been established in this region.
Pairs (a), (b) and (c) are correctly matched because St.

Great Lakes region is located in USA.
Po river valley is located in Italy.

questions.question:

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect about various forms of road (land) transport?

answerOptions.text: Road transport is used for short distance door to door services.
Railways transport is most suitable for bulky materials over longer distances.
Road and railways transport can complement each other for improving the transport efficiency.
None of the above Ans. j

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Channel Tunnel operational in Europe, connects which of the following countries?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Channel Tunnel operational in Europe
connects United Kingdom and France. It is an
underground railway tunnel important in London and
Paris. Channel Tunnel, operated by Euro Tunnel
Group through England, connects London in United
Kingdom with Paris in France.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Trans-Canadian Highway links which of the following cities?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Trans-Canadian Highway links Vancouver in
British Columbia in West coast to St. John’s City in
Newfoundland in East coast.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The cities of Edmonton and Anchorage in North America are connected by which of the following major highways?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Alaskan Highway links Edmonton in Canada
to Anchorage in Alaska.
The Alaskan Highway was constructed during World
War Second to connect the contiguous United States to
Alaska across Canada.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Trans-Continental Stuart Highway runs across which of the following continents?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Trans-continental Stuart Highway runs across
the continent of Australia. It corrects Darwin in north
coast and Melbourne via Tennant Creek and Alice
Springs in Australia. Hence, the Trans-Continental
Stuart Highway runs across in Australia continent.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding National Highway Authority of India.
1. The National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Surface Transport, established in 1995.
2. It acts as an apex body to improve the quality of the roads designated as national Highways.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct about
the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) as it
was operationalised in 1995. It is an autonomous body
under the Ministry of Surface Transport.
It is entrusted with the responsibility of development,
maintenance and operation of National Highways. This
is also the apex body to improve the quality of the roads
designated as National Highway.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect?
1. The first Public railways line was opened in 1825 between Stockton and Darlington.
2. Africa has the most dense railways network in the world.
3. North America has the largest rail network in the world.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect because Europe has one
of the most dense rail networks in the world.
Statements (1) and (3) are correct because the first
public railway line was opened in 1825 between
Stockton and Darlington in Northern England. North
America has one of the most extensive and largest rail
networks accounting for nearly 40 per cent of the world.
9. Which of the following is the most plausible
reason for the declining significance of
trans-continental railways?
(Chap 8, Class-X, Old NCERT)
(a) Degrading infrastructure due to older tracks.
(b) Establishment of closed borders in countries.
(c) Competition from road transport and airways.
(d) All of the above
Ans. (c)

Exp. Competition from road transport and airways is
the most plausible reason for the declining significance
of trans-continental railways.
Road transport is cheaper and faster over short distances
and for door to door services and High-value, light and
perishable goods are best moved by airways.
Statements (a) and (b) are incorrect because, degrading
infrastructure due to older tracks and establishment of
closed borders in country are not plausible reasons for
the declining significance of Trans-Continental railways.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is the longest trans-continental railways in the world?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Trans-Siberian Railways is the longest
trans-Continental railways in the world. It is a network
of railways connecting Western Russia to the Russian
Far East.
It is the most important route in Asia and the longest
9,332 km double tracked and electrified
trans-continental railway in the world. It has helped in
opening up its Asian region to West European markets.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2019)

Which one of the following cities is not located on the Trans-Siberian rail route?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Sochi city is not located
on the Trans-Siberian rail route. Cities located on the
Trans-Siberian rail route from West to East are
St.Petersburg, Moscow, Kazan, Yekaterinburg,
Tyumen, Omsk, Novosibirsk, Krasnoyarsk, Angarak,
Chita, Khabarovsk and Vladivostok.

questions.question:

Which of the following is not one of the region joined lying on the Trans-Canadian railway line?

Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given regions, Novosibirsk and Kazan

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Arrange the given set of regions on the Trans-Siberian rail route in a correct sequence from East to West?
1. St. Petersburg 2. Krasnoyarsk
3. Vladivostok 4. Khabarovsk
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Correct sequence of Trans-Siberian rail route
from East to West is Vladivostok, Khabarovsk,
Krasnoyarsk and St.Petersburg.
Trans-Siberian Railways major rail route of Russia runs
from St. Petersburg in the West to Vladivostok on the
Pacific Coast in the East passing through Moscow, Ufa,
Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, Chita and Khabarovsk.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Kalgoorlie, Port August, Port Pirie and Broken Hill are nodes of which of the following trans-continental railway lines?

answerOptions.rationale:
Kalgoorlie, Port August, Port Pirie and Broken
Hill are nodes of Trans-Australian Railway.
Trans-Australian railway line runs West-East across the
southern part of the continent from Perth on the West
coast, to Sydney on the East coast.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Airport ) List II (Located in) A. Buenos Aires 1. Australia B. Darwin 2. Argentina C. Santiago 3. Chile D. Denver 4. USA
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2 B-1 C-3, D-4.
Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina. Buenos
Aires airport is the biggest airport in Argentina is
located in Ezeiza, 32 km from the centre of Buenos
Aires city.
Darwin International Airport is the busiest airport
serving the Northern Territory in Australia.
Santiago International Airport is located in Pudahuel,
which is 15 km North-West of Downtown Santiago.
This is Chile’s largest aviation facility and busiest
international airport.
Denver is an International Airport located in USA.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following sea routes is considered as the busiest sea route in the world accounting for more than a quarter of world’s foreign trade?

answerOptions.text: Cape of Good Hope Sea Route
answerOptions.rationale:
Cape of Good Hope Sea Route is considered as
the busiest sea route in the world accounting for more
than a quarter of world’s foreign trade. The foreign
trade over Northern Atlantic sea route is greater than
that of the rest of the world combined.
Northern Atlantic sea route links the two industrially
developed regions of the world. i.e., North-Eastern USA
and North-Western Europe.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Which of the following sea routes connects the industrialised countries of Western Europe with West Africa and Southern Africa?

answerOptions.text: Cape of Good Hope Sea Route
answerOptions.rationale:
Cape of Good Hope Sea Trade Route connects the
highly industrialised Western European region with
West Africa, South Africa, South-East Asia and the
commercial agriculture and livestock economies of
Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Panama Canal lies on which of the following sea routes?

answerOptions.rationale:
Panama Canal lies on South Pacific sea route.
The Panama Canal is an artificial 82 km waterway in
Panama that connects Atlantic Ocean in the East to the
Pacific Ocean in the West. It shortens the distance
between New York and San Francisco by 13,000 km
by sea.

answerOptions.text: Cape of Good Hope sea route

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Suez Canal lies on which of the given Sea routes?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Suez Canal lies on Mediterranean Indian
ocean sea Route. It had been constructed in 1869 in
Egypt between Port Said in the North and Port Suez in
the South linking the Mediterranean Sea and the
Indian ocean sea route.
It is a sea-level canal without locks which is about 160
km and 11 to 15 m deep. About 100 ships travel daily
and each ship takes 10-12 hours to cross this canal.

answerOptions.text: Cape of Good Hope sea route

questions.question:
(Chap
8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Panama Canal?

answerOptions.text: It is significant for the economies of the countries in Latin America.
It is a direct link between the Pacific Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean.
It has shortened the distance between Western Europe and Northern America.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (b) are correct about the
Panama Canal because the this canal is located near
Latin American countries, so this canal is important for
the economic interests of Latin countries. Panama
Canal connects the Atlantic Ocean in the East to the
Pacific Ocean in the West. It is a direct link between
the Pacific Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean.
Statement (c) is incorrect because, Panama Canal has
shortened the distance between Western Europe and
West coast of America.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following factors determines the development of inland waterways in a region?
1. Width and depth of the channel of water.
2. Continuity in the flow of water in the river.
3. Competition from Railways and roadways.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given factors determine the development
of inland water ways in a region because the
development of inland waterways is dependent on the
navigability width and depth of the channel of water,
continuity in the water flow of water in the river,
transport technology in use and competition from
railways and roadways. Rivers, canals, lakes and coastal
areas have been important waterways since time
immemorial.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Waterway ) List II (Located in) A. Volga Waterway 1. Russia B. Mississippi Waterway 2. Eastern Europe C. Danube Waterway 3. USA D. Rhine Waterway 3. Germany
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-1 B-3 C-2 D-4.
Volga Waterways are one of the most important
waterways in Russia.
The Volga-Moscow Canal connects it with the Moscow
region and the Volga-Don Canal with the Black Sea.
Mississippi Waterways are one of the most important
waterways in USA.
Danube Waterways are one of the most important
waterways in Eastern Europe. Danube waterways are
important inland waterway serves Eastern Europe.
The Rhine Waterways flows through Germany and
Netherlands. It is navigable for 700 km from Rotterdam.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to North-South-East-West Corridor. (MPPSC Pre 2019)
1. The North-South Corridor will connect Delhi to Kanyakumari with a road length of 4076 km.
2. The East-West Corridor will connect Porbandar to Silchar with a road length of 3,640 km.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct as the North-South-
East-West Corridor is the largest ongoing highway
project in India. The East-West Corridor has been
planned to connect Silchar in Assam with the port
town of Porbandar in Gujarat with 3,640 km of
road length.
Statement (1) is incorrect because North-South Corridor
aims at connecting Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir with
Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu with 4,076 km long road.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Arrange the following types of roads in India in increasing order, according to their proportion of the road length.
1. Major District Roads
2. State Highways
3. National Highways
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct increasing order of roads in India,
according to their proportion of strength is National
Highways, State Highways and Major District Roads.
The main roads which are constructed and maintained
by the Central Government are known as the National
Highways. The National Highways constitute only
about 2% of the total road length.
State Highways are constructed and maintained by
State governments. These roads are connected to the
National Highways. These constitute 4% of total road
length in the country.
District roads are the connecting link between District
Headquarters and the other places of the district. These
roads are maintained by Zila Parishad.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to Border Roads Organisation (BRO)?
1. BRO was established in 1960 with an aim to accelerate economic development and strengthening defence preparedness along Northern border of India.
2. Border Roads Organisation is also responsible for maintenance of strategic roads in the coastal areas of India.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct because the Border Road
Organisation was established in May 1960 for
accelerating economic development and strengthening
defence preparedness through rapid and coordinated
improvement of strategically important roads along the
Northern and North-Eastern boundary of the country.
Statement (2) is incorrect because Border Roads
Organisation is responsible for maintenance of strategic
roads in the border areas (not coastal areas) of India.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect with reference to density of roads in India?

answerOptions.text: Level of economic development and terrain are the determinants of road density in a region.
Road density is high in North-Eastern states as compared to the Southern States of India.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect because due to hilly and
forested areas, high rainfall and annual floods in the
North-Eastern states, the density of roads is less as
compared to the Southern states of India.

answerOptions.text: Road density of Kerala is higher than the average national road density.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following states have high density of road network in India?
1. Bihar 2. Arunachal Pradesh
3. Kerala 4. Goa
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Kerala and Goa have
high density of road network in India because they are
coastal states. Bihar is affected by the annual floods
that’s why, it is difficult task to build a road here. Thus,
the density of roads in Bihar is low. Also the Arunachal
Pradesh is a hilly state, That’s why the construction of
roads is difficult.

questions.question:

because these are 760-km long rail route connecting
Roha in Maharashtra to Mangalore in Karnataka.

Arabian sea coast; with its headquarters at CBD
Belapur in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Railway Zones) (Headquarters) A. Eastern Railways 1. Delhi B. Northern Railways 2. Kolkata C. South Central Railways 3. Hubli D. South Western Railways 4. Secunderabad
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:

The Headquarters of South Central Railway Zone is

Railway Zone is Hubli.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is/are included in inland water transport in India?
1. Creeks 2. Rivers
3. Canals 4. Backwaters
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Inland water transport includes creeks, rivers,
canals and backwaters. India has 14,500 km of
navigable waterways, contributing about 1% to the
country’s transportation. At present, 5,685 km of major
rivers are navigable by mechanised flat bottom vessels.

questions.question:

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect with reference to inland waterways in India?
1. The National Waterways Authority of India is the nodal body for regulation of waterways in India.
2. National Waterways are mainly used for foreign trade with neighbouring countries.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to inland
waterways in India because oceanic routes are mainly
used for foreign trade with neighbouring countries.

questions.question:

with reference to National Waterway I?

Which of the following stretch of navigable canals is included in National Waterways III?

The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur pipeline does not connect, which of the following states?

answerOptions.rationale:
Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur pipeline does not
connect Jharkhand. It is India’s first cross state gas

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

with reference to development of ports in India?

Major ports handle more than 75% of country’s total port traffic.
The Major ports are used to handle only international cargo.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect with reference to
development of ports in India because, today Indian
ports are handling large volumes of domestic, as well
as, overseas trade. Most of the ports are equipped with
modern infrastructure.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Mumbai port is the largest port of India.
2. Kandla port was developed to reduce pressure on Mumbai port.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Mumbai port is a natural harbour and the biggest port
of the country. The port is situated closer to the general
routes from the countries of Middle East,
Mediterranean countries, North Africa, North America
and Europe. Kandla Port is situated at the head of Gulf
of Kuchchh.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following regions does not constitute the hinterland of Mumbai port?

answerOptions.rationale:
Goa does not constitute the hinterland of Mumbai
port. Mumbai port is a natural harbour and the biggest
port of the country. Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra,
Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan constitute
the main hinterlands of Mumbai port.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following ports is used by India for mainly receiving petroleum products and fertilisers?

answerOptions.rationale:
Kandla port is specially designed to receive large
quantities of petroleum and petroleum products and
fertilisers because it is situated at the head of Gulf of
Kuchchh. To reduce the pressure at Kandla port,
offshore terminal at Vadinar has been developed. Kandla
port is also known as Deendayal port.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are not correct?

answerOptions.text: Paradwip Port is situated at the entrance of Zuari river and is used to export iron ore to Japan.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is not correct because Mormugao
Port is situated at the entrance of the Zuari estuary. It is
a natural harbour in Goa. It gained significance after its
remodeling in 1961 to handle iron-ore exports to Japan.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

would increase faster than the food supply.
The preventive checks are better than the physical
checks. For the sustainability of our resources, the
world will have to control the rapid population increase.
Any further rapid population increase would result in a
population crash caused by famine, disease and war.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Sustainability is one of the four pillars of human development. Which of the following statements given below correctly defines sustainability?

answerOptions.text: Equal access of opportunities for everyone.
Improving the access to knowledge for the marginalised sections.
Continuity in the availability of opportunities for present and future generations.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) correctly defines sustainability
because it means continuity in the availability of
opportunities. To have sustainable human
development, each generation must have the same
opportunities. All environmental, financial and human
resources must be used keeping in mind the future.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

With reference to welfare approach of measuring human development, which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: It argues for higher government expenditure on education, health, and social sector.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is correct with reference to welfare
approach of measuring human development as this
approach looks at human beings as beneficiaries or
targets of all development activities. The approach
argues for higher government expenditure on
education, health, social secondary and amenities.
People are not participants in development but only
passive recipients. The government is responsible for
increasing levels of human development by maximising
expenditure on welfare.
Statements (b) and (c) are incorrect because welfare
approach emphasises on the basic needs of all sections.
Welfare approach links human development with social
development.

answerOptions.text: It emphasises on basic needs of certain sections.
It links Human Development to income.

1. Health 2. Child welfare
3. Sanitation 4. Housing
5. Labour 6. Food
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
As per International Labour Organisation’s (ILO’s)
Basic Need approach, six basic needs are health,
education, food, water supply, sanitation, and housing
were identified. The emphasis is given on the provision
of basic needs of defined sections.
Basic needs approach was initially proposed by
International Labour Organisation. It is one of the major
approaches to the measurement of absolute poverty in
developing countries.
It attempts to define the absolute minimum resources
necessary for long term physical well-being, usually in
terms of consumption of goods.

questions.question:

Which of the following indicators are used to measure shortfall in human development in the Human Poverty Index?
1. Number of underweight children
2. Number of people not having access to clean water
3. Lack of technological development
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Indicators mentioned in statements (1) and (2) are
used to measure shortfall in human development in the
Human Poverty Index.
This index basically used to measures the shortfall in
human development. It is a non-income measure. The
probability of not surviving till the age of 40, the adult
illiteracy rate, the number of people who do not have
access to clean water, and the number of small children
who are underweight are all taken into account to show
the shortfall in human development in any region.
Statement (3) is incorrect because lack of technological
development indicators are not used to measure shortfall
in human development in the Human Poverty Index.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements are correct regarding measuring Human Development?
1. The human development index assesses progress in human development. It highlights progress made in crucial areas of human development.
2. Human development Index is not the reliable source to measure because it lacks distribution factor.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding measuring Human Development. The
Human Development Index (HDI) assesses progress in
human development. It highlights progress made in
crucial areas of human development. Yet, it is not the
most reliable measure. This is because it does not say
anything about the distribution.
Human Development Index (HDI) is published by
United Nations Development Programme (UNDP),
every year.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Temporary human settlements are usually built in which of the following regions?

answerOptions.rationale:
Temporary human settlements are usually built
in cold desert regions, Deep forested areas and
Rugged mountain slopes. Settlements which are
occupied for a short time are called temporary
settlements.
The people living in deep forests, hot and cold
deserts and mountains often dwell in such temporary
settlements. They practice hunting, gathering,
shifting cultivation and transhumance.

It is the movement of people towards environmentally sustainable regions.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to patterns of rural settlements?
1. Linear rural settlements are formed along roads and railways.
2. Rectangular patterns of rural settlements are found in wide intermontane valleys.
3. Cruciform settlements are developed around a river.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to patterns of rural settlements because linear pattern
settlements houses are located along a road, railway
line, and river, canal edge of a valley or along a levee.
Rectangular patterns of rural settlements are found in
plain areas or wide intermontane valleys. The roads are
rectangular and cut each other at right angles.
Statement (3) is incorrect because cruciform settlements
develop on the crossroads and houses extend in all the
four directions.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about urban settlements?

answerOptions.text: Trade routes are significant in deciding the growth of urban settlements.
Uniform international criteria are used by all the countries of the world to classify urban settlements.
Majority of the population in urban areas is involved in non-agricultural activities.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct about urban
settlements or centres because these are located close to
an important trade route have experienced rapid
development. Majority of the population in urban areas
is involved in non-agricultural activities. In India, if
more than 75% of the productive population engaged in
non-agricultural activities then it is an urban region.
Statement (b) is incorrect because different international
criteria are used by all the countries of the world to
classify urban settlements. In Italy, a settlement is called
urban, if more than 50 % of its economically productive
population is engaged in non-agricultural pursuits. India
has set this criterion at 75 %.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about large cities.
1. The first city to reach one million plus population in the world was London.
2. New York City was the first mega city of the world.
3. Any city with a population greater than one million is considered as a mega city.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct about large
cities because the city whose population is more than
one million is called million city. London was the first
million city in the world.
London reached the million marks in 1800, followed by
Paris in 1850 and New York in 1860. A mega city is a
general term for cities together with their suburbs with
a population of more than 10 million people.
New York was the first to attain the status of a mega city
by 1950 with a total population of about 12.5 million.
Statement (3) is incorrect because any city with a
population greater than 10 million is considered as a
mega city.

questions.question:

Megalopolis.

1915 and applied to a large area of urban development
that resulted from the merging of originally separate
towns or cities.

of languages. Altia, Balkar, Dolgan are Tribes of Turkey.

questions.question:

Arrange the given mountains in a correct sequence from North to South using the codes given below.

Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct sequence of mountain from North to
South is Yablonovy Mountains, Altai Mountains, Tian
Shan Mountains and Kunlun Mountain.
The Yablonovy mountains is a mountain range in
Siberia. It is in Transbaikal, Russia. The highest peaks
are bare, but most of the range is densely forested with
larch, spruce, and pine.
The Altai mountains are a mountain range in Central
and East Asia, where Russia, China, Mongolia, and
Kazakhstan converge.

The Tian Shan extend 2,500 km East to West across
Central Asia.

chains in Asia, extending for more than 3,000 km. In
the broadest sense, the chain forms the Northern edge
of the Tibetan Plateau South of the Tarim Basin.

features in Asia because the Kunlun mountains is one of

than 3,000 km. In the broadest sense, the chain forms

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about the climate of Asia?

answerOptions.text: Most of the rainfall in Asia is received in the summer season.
There is heavy rainfall in winters in the interior regions of Asia.
Mountain barriers play an important role in influencing the climate pattern in Asia.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct about the
climate of Asia. In summer, most parts of Asia receive
rainfall due to monsoon winds. The climate of Asia is
influenced by many factors. Factors such as the sheer
size of Asia, wide latitudinal extension, large mountain
barriers, etc affect the climate in Asia.
Statement (b) is incorrect because, due to the low
temperature in the winter season, high air pressure is
formed in the interior region of Asia. That is why, there
is no rain in the interior region of Asia during the winter
season.
10. Consider the following statement with reference
to the various types of natural vegetation found
in Asia.
(Chap 6, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)
1. Northern Coast of Asia is marked by Tundra
Vegetation.
2. Pine, fir and spruce are found in Taiga region of
Asia.
3. Temperate grasslands known as steppes are
located on the coastal regions of Asia.
4. Desert vegetation is found mostly in Central Asia.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are
correct?
(a) 1, 2 and 3 (b) 2, 3 and 4
(c) 1, 2 and 4 (d) 1, 3 and 4
Ans.
j (c)
Exp. Statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct with
reference to the various types of natural vegetation
found in Asia.
Due to the lack of temperature in the Northern region
of Asia, this region remains below zero degrees for most
of the time. That is why tundra vegetation is found on
the Northern coast in Asia.
To the South of the tundra is a wide belt of coniferous
forests called Taiga. Soft wood trees like pine, fir and

The island of Sumatra is separated from Malaysia by which of the following strait?

The island of Sumatra is separated from Malaysia

The Islands of Celebes and Borneo are separated by which of the following straits?

The islands of Celebes and Borneo are separated

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following physical features divides Russia into European and Asian parts?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Ural mountain range divides Russia into
European and Asian parts. The Ural mountains range
that runs approximately from North to South through
Western Russia, from the coast of the Arctic Ocean to

questions.question:

3. Ural river 4. Rhine river

West Siberian Plains extends between the Ural
mountains and the Yenisei river in the East. The Irtysh,

plain and fall into the North Pole Ocean.

mountains and flows through Russia and Kazakhstan
into the Caspian Sea. The Rhine river originates from
the Alps mountains and falls in the North Sea in the
West.

questions.question:

White Sea, the Baltic Sea, the Caspian Sea, the Sea of

important port city of Russia.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.

2. A sketch is a map which provides great details for a smaller area on a large scale.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct as one cannot
draw on a map the actual shape and size of different
features and natural features such as buildings, roads,
etc. Hence, they are represented by using certain
letters, shades, colours, pictures and lines. These
symbols provide a lot of information in a limited space.

(MSL) either in metres or feet, and can be drawn at any
desired interval.

without a scale, based on memory and observation, and
represents the main features of an area.

Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct with reference to evolution
of physiographical structure of India. Peninsular
mountains are young, weak and flexible in their
geological structure unlike the rigid and stable
Peninsular block. These mountains are tectonic in origin,
dissected by fast-flowing rivers, which are in their
youthful stage.

period, the Peninsula has been standing like a rigid
block with the exception of some of its Western coast,
which is submerged below the ocean.

delta with an average elevation of 50-150. It is also

region of Bangladesh and West Bengal, India.

West to the Meghna River on the East. The Sunderban
delta got its name from the Sundari tree, which fills well

developing delta.

India. Chhota Nagpur plateau – the North-East part of
Peninsular plateau includes Jharkhand, parts of
Chhattisgarh and West Bengal. Rajmahal hills are the
North-Eastern projection of Chhota Nagpur Plateau. It
is a mineral rich plateau.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Deccan plateau. 
1. The Deccan plateau is separated from the Northern Plains by the Satpuras, Maikal range and Mahadeo hills.
2. The Deccan plateau is highest in the Western part, and slopes towards the Bay of Bengal in the East.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to Deccan plateau. The Deccan Plateau is a
high plateau in Western and Southern India. The
plateau is divided into two parts called Malnad and
Maidan. The Malnad in Kannada means hill country, It
is dissected into deep valleys covered with dense forests.
The Maidan on the other hand is formed of rolling plain
with low granite hills. It is separated from the Gangetic
plain to the North by the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges,
which form its Northern boundary.
The Deccan Plateau is highest in the Western part, and
slopes towards the Bay of Bengal in the East because
the Deccan Plateau is higher in the West and slopes
gently Eastwards.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-IX, New NCERT)

The Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand and Chhota Nagpur plateau are natural extension of which of, the following physical features?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand and Chhota
Nagpur plateau are natural extension of the Central
Highland also called the Madhya Bharat Pathar or
Madhya Bharat Plateau.
It is to the East of the Marwar or Mewar Upland. Most
of plateaus comprise the basin of the Chambal river,
which flows in a rift valley. It is a rolling plateau with
rounded hills composed of sandstone.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about India’s Western coast.
1. The Western coast of India is a submergent coast.
2. It is narrower than the East coast and suitable for development of natural harbours.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding the India’s Western coast. On the basis of the
location and active geomorphological processes, it can
be broadly divided into (i) The Western coastal plains
(ii) The Eastern coastal plains.
The Western coastal plains are an example of
submerged coastal plain.
Because of this submergence, it is a narrow belt and
provides natural conditions for the development of ports
and harbours. Kandla, Mazagaon, Jawaharlal Nehru port
Navha Sheva, Marmagao, Mangalore, Cochin, etc., are
some of the important natural ports located along the
West coast.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to India’s East coast.
1. Eastern coast is broader and gentle sloping than the Western coast.
2. Eastern coast is emergent in the nature unlike Western coast.
3. Rivers in this region form well developed estuaries.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct about India’s
East coast because as compared to the Western coastal
plain, the Eastern coastal plain is broader and it is an
example of an emergent coast. There are well developed
deltas here, formed by the rivers flowing Eastward in to
the Bay of Bengal. These include the deltas of the
Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri.
Because of its emergent nature, it has less number of
ports and harbours. The Continental shelf extends up to
500 km into the sea, which makes it difficult for the
development of good ports and harbours.

answerOptions.rationale:

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following factors is/are not responsible for the formation of natural drainage pattern in a region?

answerOptions.rationale:
Multipurpose projects are not responsible for the
formation of natural drainage pattern in a region as it is
the outcome of the geological time period, nature and
structure of rocks, topography, slope, amount of water
flowing and the periodicity of the flow. Multipurpose
projects are man-made thus, they cannot be responsible
for natural drainage pattern in a region.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to various drainage patterns?

answerOptions.text: Rivers originating from a hill and flowing in all directions forms a radial drainage pattern.
In a trellis drainage pattern, all the tributaries join the main stream at right angles.
A centripetal drainage pattern is formed when all the rivers drain into a lake or depression.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct with
reference to various drainage patterns.
When the river originates from a hill and flow in all
directions, the drainage pattern is known as ‘radial’. for
example, rivers originate from Amarkantak range
follows the radial drainage pattern.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the given pairs is/are matched correctly?

answerOptions.text: Catchment area – An area drained by a river and its tributaries
Drainage basin – Water collected by the river from a specific area
Watershed – A boundary separating two river basins
answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (c) is correctly matched as the boundary line
separating one drainage basin from the other is known
as ‘Watershed’. It is the catchment of small rivulets and
rills and is small in area.
Pair (a) and (b) are not correctly matched because when
a river drains the water collected from a specific area,
then it is called as its ‘catchment area’.
A drainage basin is an area drained by a river and its
tributaries.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following rivers drains into the Bay of Bengal?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both Brahmaputra and Mahanadi rivers drain into
the Bay of Bengal. Brahmaputra river originates in the
Chemayungdung glacier of the Kailash range near
Mansarovar Lake.
Mahanadi river originates near Sihawa in Raipur district
of Chhattisgarh and runs through Odisha to discharge
its water into Bay of Bengal.
Mahi river rises in the Western Vindhya range and
drains into Arabian Sea.

questions.question:

Which of the following is/are the right bank tributaries of Indus?
1. Nubra 2. Zaskar
3. Khurram 4. Shigar

answerOptions.rationale:
Nubra, Khurram and Shigar rivers are the right
bank tributaries of Indus. The other right bank
tributaries of Indus river are Tochi, Gomal, Viboa,
Shyok, Gilgit and Hunza river that originate in
Sulaiman range. Zanskar river is the left bank tributary
of Indus river. The other left Bank tributaries of Indus
river are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

questions.question:

2. Ravi Kullu Hills

answerOptions.rationale:
All of the given pairs are matched correctly.
The Jhelum, an important tributary of the Indus,
originates from a spring at Verinag situated at the foot of
the Pir Panjal in the South-Eastern part of the Kashmir
valley. It flows through Srinagar and the Wular lake
before entering Pakistan through a deep narrow gorge.
The Ravi is the tributary of the Indus, which rises West
of the Rohtang pass in Kullu hills of Himachal Pradesh
and flows through the Chamba Valley of the state.
The Sutlej river in the tributary of the Indus, originates
in the ‘Rakas Tal’ near Mansarovar at an altitude of
4,555 m in Tibet, where it is known as Langchen
Khambab.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to Indus and its tributaries?

answerOptions.text: The Jhelum river joins the Indus river in Pakistan.
The Chenab is the largest tributary of Indus formed by Chandra and Bhaga rivers.
The Beas and Sutlej river meets at Harike in Punjab.

answerOptions.rationale:
All of the given statements are correct with
reference to Indus and its tributaries.
The Jhelum river joins the Indus river in Pakistan. It is
an important tributary of Indus river, rises from a spring
at Verinag situated at the foot of the Pir Panjal in the
South-Eastern part of the valley of Kashmir.
The Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus. It is
formed by two streams, the Chandra and the Bhaga,
which join at Tandi near Keylong in Himachal Pradesh.
Hence, it is known as ‘Chandrabhaga.
The Beas river, tributary of the Indus (originates from
Beas kund near Rohtang Pass) flows through the Kullu
valley. It enters the Punjab Plains where it meets Sutlej
river near Harike.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is /are not correct
with reference to Ganga river system?

answerOptions.text: The Satopanth glacier is the main source of Alaknanda river.
Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag to form Ganga.
The Ganga descends on the plains at Dehradun.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is not correct with reference to
Ganga river system. The Ganga descends on the
plains at Haridwar and not Dehradun. It rises in the
Gangotri Glacier near Gaumukh (Uttarkashi district,
Uttarakhand). Here, it is known as the Bhagirathi. The
Alaknanda has its source in the Satopanth glacier above
Badrinath.

answerOptions.text: The Son is a right bank tributary of Ganga.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following rivers is/are not a tributary of Ganga?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Bhagirathi river is not a
tributary of Ganga. It is one of the two headstreams of
the Ganges and is also considered as the source stream
of the Ganges.
At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda
hereinafter, it is known as the Ganga. The Yamuna (Right
hand tributary) is the longest tributary of the Ganga.
Gomati, the Ghaghara are the left bank tributaries of the
Ganga. The other left bank tributaries of the Ganga are
the Gandak, the Kosi and the Mahananda.

questions.question:

Chambal, Sind and Betwa are the left bank tributaries of Yamuna.
Yamuna is the second longest tributary of Ganga.
Yamuna Basin is larger than the basin of Chambal.

tributary of the river Ganga.
