questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Ganga and its tributaries.
1. The Sarda river originates in Nepal in the Milam Glacier.
2. The Saryu river is also known as Sorrow of Bengal.
3. The Son river originates from Amarkantak Plateau
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct with reference
to Ganga and its tributaries.
The Sarda river or Saryu river originates from the
Milam glacier in the Nepal Himalayas where it is known
as the Goriganga. Along the Indo-Nepal border, it is
called Kali or Chauk, where it joins the Ghaghara.
The Son river is a large South bank tributary of the
Ganga, and it originates in the Amarkantak plateau.
After forming a series of waterfalls, it reaches Arrah,
West of Patna, to join the Ganga.
Statement (2) is incorrect because the Damodar river,
not the Saryu river, is known as ‘Sorrow of Bengal.’
The Brahamaputra

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following glacier is the source of river Brahmaputra?

answerOptions.rationale:
Chemayungdung Glacier of the Kailash range
near the Mansarovar lake is the source of river
Brahmaputra. It emerges as a turbulent and dynamic
river after carving out a deep gorge in the Central
Himalayas near Namcha Barwa. The river emerges
from the foothills under the name of Siang or Dihang.
Flowing South-West, it receives it’s main left bank
tributaries i.e. Dibang or Sikang and Lohit, thereafter it
is known as Brahmaputra. This river is well known for
floods, channel shifting and bank erosion.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Brahmaputra river system?
1. The Brahmaputra river originates in Kailash range near Mansarovar Lake.
2. It is known as Tsangpo in Tibetan region.
3. It enters in India flowing through Assam at Namcha Barwa.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to Brahmaputra river system.
The Brahmaputra river originates in Kailash range near
Mansarovar lake. It traverses Eastward longitudinally
for a distance of nearly 1200 km in a dry and flat region
of the Southern Tibet, where it is known as the
‘Tsangpo’ which means ‘the purifier’.
Statement (3) is not correct because it enters in India,
through Arunachal Pradesh. Following Southwards, it
receives its main left bank tributaries, viz Dibang or
Sikang and Lohit, thereafter it is known as the
‘Brahmaputra’.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following river is a tributary of Brahmaputra in India?
1. Chindwin 2. Dhansari
3. Teesta 4. Dibang
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Dhansari, Teesta and Dibang are the tributaries of
Brahmaputra river in India. The Brahmaputra receives
a numerous tributaries in its 750 km long journey
through the Assam valley.
Dhamiri in its major left bank tributary. Dibang on
Sikang is also its left bank tributary. The other left bank
tributaries of Brahmaputra river and Lohit,
Burhi-Dihing etc.
Teesta is its right bank tributary. In Bangladesh, Teesta
joins the Brahmaputra on its right bank, from where it is
known as ‘Jamuna’. The other right bank tributaries of
Brahmaputra rivers are Subansiri, Kameng, Manas and
Sankosh.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to flow of Brahmaputra in India?

answerOptions.text: Brahmaputra flows for almost 800 km in the Assam Valley.
It is known as river Jamuna as it enters plains of Assam.
It is responsible for channel shifting and bank erosion in the Assam plains.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct with reference to
flow of Brahmaputra in India. The Brahmaputra receives
numerous tributaries in its 750 km long journey through
the Assam valley. The Brahmaputra enters into
Bangladesh near Dhuleri and flows Southward.
In Bangladesh, the Teesta joins it on its right bank from
where the river is known as the Jamuna. It finally
merges with the river Padma, which falls in the Bay of
Bengal. The Brahmaputra is well-known for floods,
channel shifting and bank erosion. This is due to the fact
that most of its tributaries are large and bring large
quantity of sediments owing to heavy rainfall in its
catchment area.
Statement (b) is incorrect as it known as river Jamuna in
Bangladesh not in Assam.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following mountain range acts as a water divide between the Peninsular drainage of Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea?

answerOptions.rationale:
Western Ghats act as a water divide between the
Peninsular drainage of Bay of Bengal and the Arabian
sea.
The Western Ghats running close to the Western coast
act as the water divide between the major peninsular
rivers, discharging their water into Bay of Bengal and as
small rivulets joining the Arabian sea.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following events were responsible for the formation of Peninsular drainage system in its present form?

answerOptions.text: Subsidence of the western flank of Peninsular and its submergence
Tilting of Peninsular from Northwest to Southeast

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given options are responsible for the
formation of Peninsular drainage system in its present
form.
Subsidence of the Western flank of the Peninsular
leading to its submergence below the sea during the
early tertiary period. Generally, it has disturbed the
symmetrical plan of the river.
Upheaval of the Himalayas when the Northern flank of
the Peninsular block was subjected to the subsidence
and the consequent through faulting.

(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

The Kaveri river basin does not extend to, which of the following states?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Kaveri river basin does not extend to
Maharashtra. The Kaveri originates in Brahmagiri hills

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2009)

Consider the following statement. 
1. There are no east flowing rivers in Kerala.
2. There is no west flowing river in Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Neither statements (1) nor (2) is correct. There are
three east flowing rivers in Kerala i.e. Kabani River,
Bhavani River, and Pambar River. The Tapti, Mahi and
Narmada rivers originate in Madhya Pradesh and flow
from east to West and empty into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following rivers is not a West flowing river?

answerOptions.rationale:
Penner is not a West flowing river as it is
East flowing river. It rises in the Nandi hills in
Chikkaballapur district of Karnataka and traverses to
the State of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh to empty
into Bay of Bengal. It has the catchment area of 55,213
square km.
Shetruniji, Dhadhar and Vaitarna are the West flowing
small rivers. The Shetruniji river rises near Dalkahwa in
Amreli district. The Dhadhar river rises near Ghantar
village in Panchmahal district. The Vaitarna rises in
Trimbak hills in Nasik district.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following rivers is not East flowing river?
1. Bharatpuzha 2. Sharavati
3. Subarnarekha 4. Palar
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Bharatpuzha and Sharavati are not East flowing
rivers. They are West flowing rivers. Bharatpuzha, the
longest river of Kerala, rises near Annamalai hilly. It is
also known as Ponnari. It drains an area of 5,397 km 2 .
The Sharavati river originates in Shimoga district of
2
Karnataka and drains a catchment area of 2,209 km .
The Subarnarekha and the Palar are the East flowing
small rivers in India. The Subarnarekha has the
2
catchment area of 19,296 km and the Palar has the
catchment area of 17,870 km 2 . Baitarani, Brahmani,
Penner etc are some of the important East flowing
rivers.

questions.question:

Consider the following statements with reference to Wular lake.
1. Wular lake has been formed due to tectonic activities.

3. It has one of the largest deposits of rare the Earth minerals in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to Wular lake.
Wular lake has been formed due to tectonic activities. It
is the fresh water lake in the Himalayan region. It is also
the largest fresh water lake in India. The Dal Lake,
Bhimtal, Nainital, Loktak and Barapani are some of the
important fresh water lakes.

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Govind Sagar lake is a

generation of hydel power has led to the formation of
Guru Govind Sagar Lake (Bhakra Nangal Project).

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-IX, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Indian climate?

answerOptions.text: The Indian climate has been described as Monsoon, which is derived from the Arabic word Mausim.
Different states of India exhibit only the same type of climate.
There are variations in the temperature and rainfall of different regions in India in an year.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct with reference to
Indian climate.
The climate of India is described as the ‘Monsoon’ type.
The word ‘Monsoon’ is derived from the Arabic word
‘Mausim’ which literally means season.
Monsoon refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind
direction during a year. There are variations in
temperature and rainfall of different regions in India in a
year. For instance, the temperature touches 50°C in
some parts of Rajasthan in summer. Whereas, it may be
around 20°C in Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir.
Similarly, the rainfall varies from over 400 cm in
Meghalaya to less than 10 cm in Ladakh and Western
Rajasthan. Therefore, different states of India exhibit
different type of climate.
2. Which state of India experiences the maximum
annual variation of rainfall?
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT) (WBPSC Pre 2017)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements with reference to climate of India. ( Chap 4, Class-XI , New NCERT)
1. Upper air circulations and jet streams have no effect on the rainfall and climate of India.
2. As India is surrounded by Sea from three sides, the coastal states of India experience moderate climate.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Only statement (2) is correct with reference to
climate of India. The coastal states of India experience
a moderate climate due to moderating influence of the
sea. That’s why people of Mumbai and Konkan coast
have hardly any idea of extreme temperature and the
seasonal rhythm of weather.
Statement (1) is incorrect because upper air
circulations and jet streams play a significant role on
the rainfall and climate of India.
About 3 km above the surface of Earth, a different
pattern of air circulation is observed in the lower
troposphere.
All of Western and Central Asia remains under the
influence of Westerly winds along the altitude of
9-13 km from West to East. These winds are called
jet streams.

questions.question: Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct codes. ( Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT) Assertion

The cities such as Delhi and Kanpur, located in the interior of India have higher climatic contrast as compared to coastal cities such as Mumbai. Reason (R) Coastal regions of India experience more rainfall than the North-Eastern states such as Meghalaya. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
answerOptions.rationale:
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
The cities such as Delhi and Kanpur, located in the
interior of India have higher climatic contrast as
compared to coastal cities such as Mumbai. It is because
the coastal areas have an equable climate i.e., there is
not much variation in temperature throughout the year.
North-Eastern states such as Meghalaya experience
more rainfall than the coastal regions. In some parts of
Khasi and Jaintia hills, the rainfall exceeds 1000 cm.
Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in the Khasi hills of
Meghalaya receive rainfall over 1080 cm in a year.

answerOptions.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following wind systems, after crossing the equator, deflects to form the South- West Monsoon Winds?

answerOptions.rationale:
South-Eastern Trade Winds after crossing the
Equator deflect to form the South-West Monsoon
Winds. During April and May, when the Sun shines
vertically over the Tropic of Cancer, the large landmass
in the North of Indian Ocean gets intensely heated.
This causes the formation of an intense low pressure in
the North-Western part of subcontinent.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

In the month of July, the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is located above which of the following region of India?

answerOptions.rationale:
In the month of July, the ITCZ is located above
Gangetic plains. Due to heating of the subcontinent,
the ITCZ moves Northwards occupying position
centred 25°N in July.
This location of ITCZ attracts a surface circulation of the
winds, which are South Westerly on the West coast as
well as along the coast of West Bengal and Bangladesh.
They are Easterly or Southeasterly over North Bengal
and Bihar. The influx of these winds brings about a
change in the weather towards rainy season.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following regions is not affected much by the Arabian Sea branch of monsoon? (CGPSC Pre 2016)

(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

The rainfall on the Konkan coast is mainly due to
which of the following wind system in the South-West monsoon season?

answerOptions.text: Bay of Bengal branch of South-West monsoon.
Arabian Sea branch of South-West monsoon.
answerOptions.rationale:
The rainfall on the Konkan coast is mainly due to
Arabian Sea branch of South-West monsoon.
South-West monsoon approaches the landmass in two
branches, (i) Arabian Sea branch and (ii) Bay of Bengal
branch.
The monsoon winds originating over the Arabian Sea is
called Arabian Sea branch of South-West monsoon.
Arabian Sea branch is obstructed by Western Ghats and
the winds climb the slopes of Western Ghats from
900-1200 m. Soon, they become cool and as a result, the
windward side of the Sahyadris and Western coastal
plain (including Konkan coast) receive rainfall.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following regions lie in the rainshadow zone of Western Ghats and remains relatively dry during the monsoon?
1. Mumbai 2. Pune
3. Kozhikode 4. Kolkata
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Pune and Kozhikode lie in the rainshadow zone
of Western Ghats and remain relatively dry during the
monsoon. Some other rainshadow areas in this region
are Mangaluru, Bengaluru etc. Western Ghats is one
of the highest rainfall region in India.
After crossing the Western Ghats, Monsoon winds
descend and get heated up. This reduces humidity in
the winds. As a result, these winds cause little rainfall
East of the Western Ghats. This region of low rainfall is
known as the ‘Rainshadow area.’

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Which of the following is the primary reason behind the scanty rainfall caused in the Gujarat and Rajasthan region in the South-West monsoon season of India?

answerOptions.text: The monsoon winds exhaust all of their moisture before reaching this region.
The moisture in the monsoon winds is exhausted due to the heat present in the region.
The moisture carrying winds generally blow parallel to this region and there is no orographic effect present here.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is the primary reason due to, which
Gujarat and Rajasthan region in the South-West
monsoon season of India experience the scanty rainfall.
Monsoonal rainfall is generally governed by relief or
topography. Following are the reasons for the scanty
rainfall in these regions
(i) The moisture carrying winds generally blow parallel to
this region i.e., Aravallis.
(ii) There is no orographic effect as the moisture laden
winds are not obstructed by any mountain or hills.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the characteristics of rainfall during the South-West monsoon season in India.
1. The spatial distribution of rainfall varies from 12 cm to 250 cm across various regions.
2. More than 75% of rainfall is received in India during this season.
3. Monsoon breaks occur due to cyclonic depressions formed in Bay of Bengal region.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct with
reference to the characteristics of rainfall during the
South-West monsoon season in India. The spatial
distribution of rainfall varies from 12 cm to 250 cm
across the various regions. For example, windward side
of Western Ghats receive a rainfall of over 250 cm.
South-West monsoon plays a pivotal role in the
agrarian economy of India because over three-fourths
(75%) of the total rain in the country is received during
this period.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to retreating monsoon season in India.
1. There is rise in temperature during the retreating monsoon season.
2. This period is characterised by pleasant weather due to the phenomenon of October Heat.
3. Coromandel Coast is greatly affected by cyclones during this season.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to
retreating monsoon season in India as this period is not
characterised by pleasant weather. Coromandel Coast
is greatly affected by the depressions and cyclones,
which originate over the Andaman Sea and results into
heavy rainfall.
The retreating South-West monsoon season is marked
ley clear skies and rise in temperature owing to the
conditions of high temperature and humidity, the
weather becomes rather oppressive. This is commonly
known as ‘October heat’.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect
with reference to cold weather season in India?

answerOptions.text: The Peninsular region of India do not experience any well-defined cold weather season.
Coastal areas experience greatest range of temperature during the Cold weather season.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect with reference to cold
weather season in India.
There is hardly any seasonal change in the distribution
pattern of the temperature in coastal areas because of
moderating influence of the sea and the proximity
equator to Equator. For example, the mean maximum
temperature for January at Thiruvananthapuram is as
high as 31°C and for June, it is 29.5°.

answerOptions.text: Westerly and North-Westerly winds blow over the Gangetic Plains during this season.
Shallow cyclonic depressions cause rainfall in some of the North-Western parts of India in this season.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Western cyclonic disturbances in India?
1. Rainfall due to Western disturbances is highly beneficial for Rabi crops in India.
2. Southern Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu also receive rainfall in winter season due to Cyclonic disturbances originating over Mediterranean Sea.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to Western cyclonic disturbances in India.
In North-Western India, some weak temperate cyclones
from Mediterranean Sea cause rainfall in Punjab,
Haryana, Delhi and Western Uttar Pradesh.
Although, the amount is less but it is highly beneficial for
Rabi crops.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

During the April-June months, the Peninsular region do not experience intense summers as compared to the Northern region because of which of the following reason?

answerOptions.text: There are many hill stations in the Peninsular region.
The Peninsular is surrounded by water from three sides.
answerOptions.rationale:
The Peninsular region is surrounded by water
from three sides. Due to this reason, Peninsular region
do not experience intense summer as compared to
Northern region in April-June.
The hot weather season in South India is mild and not
so intense as found in North India. The Peninsular
situation of South India with the moderating effect of
the oceans keeps the temperature lower than that
prevailing in North India so temperatures remain
between 26°C and 32°C in the Peninsular India.

answerOptions.text: The Peninsula is older than the Northern plains of India.
The Peninsula is made up of basaltic rocks.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The ITCZ shifts at 25° N during this season.
2. Hot winds and dust storms blow in this season in the Northern Plains.
3. Local storms which bring rainfall are common in this season. The statements given above characterise which of the following seasons?

answerOptions.rationale:
The given statements characterise summer
season. The summer months are a period of excessive
heat and falling air pressure in the Northern half of the
country. Due to the heating of the subcontinent, the
ITCZ moves Northwards occupying a position centred
at 25°N in July.
During this season, hot winds and dust storms blow in
the Northern plains. Hot, dry and oppressing winds
blowing in Northern plains during season is locally
known as ‘ loo’.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following regions is/are characterised by low rainfall in India?
1. Deccan plateau 2. Khasi Hills
3. Western Uttar Pradesh 4. Ladakh
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Deccan plateau, Western Uttar Pradesh and
Ladakh regions are characterised by low rainfall in
India. Deccan plateau and Western Uttar Pradesh
come under the areas of low rainfall. These areas
receive rainfall between 50-100 cm. Some other areas
of low rainfall are Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu and
Kashmir, Eastern Rajasthan etc.
Ladakh comes under the areas of inadequate rainfall. It
receives rainfall below 50 cm.
Apart from these, parts of Peninsular area especially in
Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Maharashtra and
Western Rajasthan receive inadequate rainfall.

The winter rains caused by Western disturbance in North-Western plains of India gradually decreases from

answerOptions.rationale:
The winter rains caused by Western disturbance
in North-Western plains of India gradually decreases
from West to East. The extratropical storm originating
in the Mediterranean region that brings sudden winter
rain to the North-Western parts of Indian subcontinent
is called Western disturbance.

reference to laterite soil. The laterite soils develop in
areas with high temperature and high rainfall. These
are the result of intense leaching due to tropical rains.
With rain, lime and silica are leached away and soils
rich in iron oxide and aluminium compound are left
behind.

Consider the following Assertion

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following soil type is used for making bricks for construction of houses?

answerOptions.rationale:
Laterite soil is used for making bricks for
construction of houses. The word laterite comes from
the Latin word later, which means a brick. This is
highly compacted and cemented soil that can easily be
cut into brick-shaped blocks for building.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to arid soils of India.
1. Arid soils are most suitable for making common salt in dry region of India.
2. They are rich in moisture, humus and organic matter.
3. The bottom horizons restrict infiltration of water in these soils due to Kankar formation.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct with reference
to arid soils in India.
Arid soils range from red to brown in colour. They are
generally sandy in structure and saline in nature. Lower
horizons of the Arid soil are occupied by ‘Kankar’ layers
because of the increasing calcium content downwards.
The ‘Kankar’ layer formation in the bottom horizons
restricts the infiltration of water, and as such when
irrigation is made available, the soil moisture is readily
available for a sustainable plant growth.
Statement (2) is incorrect as due to the dry climate, high
temperature and accelerated evaporation, arid soils lack
moisture and humus. Nitrogen is insufficient and the
phosphate content is normal.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following soils are known as Usara soil and contain a large proportion of sodium, magnesium and potassium?

answerOptions.rationale:
Saline soil is also known as Usara soil. Saline soils
contain a larger proportion of sodium, potassium and
magnesium, and thus, they are infertile, and do not
support any vegetative growth.
They have more salts, largely because of dry climate
and poor drainage. They occur in arid and semi-arid
regions and in waterlogged and swampy areas.
16. Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to saline soil?
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)
(a) Saline soils can be made fertile by treating it with
gypsum.
(b) Highly fertile alluvial soils become saline soils in
regions of over irrigation.
(c) Saline soils develop layers of salt on the top layer
due to capillary action.
(d) All of the above
Ans. (d)

Exp. All the given statements are correct with
reference to saline soil. In the areas of intensive
cultivation with excessive use of irrigation, especially
in areas of green revolution, the fertile alluvial soils are
becoming saline.
Excessive irrigation with dry climatic conditions
promotes capillary action, which results in the
deposition of salt on the top layer of the soil. In such
areas, especially in Punjab and Haryana, farmers are
advised to add gypsum to solve the problem of salinity
in the soil.
17. Peaty soils are generally found in which of the
following regions? (Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)
(a) Regions with medium rainfall and low temperature.
(b) Dry regions with high annual range of temperature.
(c) Regions characterised by high humidity and rainfall.
(d) Cold regions with excessively low rainfall.
Ans. (c)

Exp. Peaty soils are generally found in the areas of
heavy rainfall and high humidity, where there is a good
growth of vegetation.
Thus, large quantity of dead organic matter
accumulates in these areas and this gives a rich humus
and organic content to the soil.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding soil erosion in India?
1. Gully erosion is prevalent in India in the Chambal basin.
2. Sheet erosion leads to removal of the top layers of fertile soil.
3. Construction of check dams is helpful in reducing gully erosion.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct regarding the
soil erosion in India.
Gully erosion is common on steep slopes. Gullies
deepen with rainfall, cut the agricultural lands into small
fragments and make them unfit for cultivation. Ravines
are widespread in the Chambal basin. Besides this, they
are also found in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.
Sheet erosion takes place on level lands after a heavy
shower and the soil removal is not easily noticeable.
But it is harmful since, it removes the finer and more
fertile top soil.
Check dams are constructed across the gully bed to stop
channel and lateral erosion. By reducing the original
gradient of the gully channel, check dams diminish the
velocity of water flow and the erosive power of run-off.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following techniques is/are most suitable for reducing degradation of soil?
1. Contour bunding 2. Mixed cropping
3. Gully plugging 4. Agro forestry
5. Shelter plantations
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given techniques are suitable for reducing
degradation of soil. Soil conservation is a methodology
to maintain soil fertility, prevent soil erosion and
exhaustion, and improve the degraded condition of
the soil.
Contour bunding is a soil conservation technique for
marginal, sloping and hilly land where the soil
productivity is very low.
Mixed cropping is a practice of growing two or more
crops in the same piece of land.
Gully plugging is a practice of constructing small,
temporary dam across a drainage to lower the speed of
concentrated flows.
Agro forestry is a land use management system in
which trees or shrubs are grown.
Shelter planation is a practice of planting shelter of
trees to avoid erosion of soil from wind.
Natural Vegetation

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Tropical Evergreen forests found in India?
1. They are found in regions with annual precipitation more than 200 cm.
2. They are widespread in the Malwa Plateau region.
3. Creeper and climber species are found in abundance in these forests.
4. Plantations such as tea, rubber, coffee are generally grown in these regions.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (3) and (4) are correct regarding
tropical evergreen forest. They are found in warm and
humid areas with an annual precipitation of over 200
cm and mean annual temperature above 22° C.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following species is/are generally not found in Evergreen and Semi-evergreen forests of India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Sandalwood is not found in Evergreen and
Semi-evergreen forests of India. It is found in dry
deciduous forests in India. The species found in the
Evergreen and Semi-evergreen forests of India include
rosewood, mahogany, hollock, ebony, etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Tropical Deciduous forests in India.
1. Teak, Sal, Sheesham are found in abundance in the Tropical Moist Deciduous forests.
2. Dry deciduous forests develop in regions having rainfall between 70-100 cm.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to tropical deciduous forests in India.
Tropical Deciduous forests are the most widespread
forests in India. They are also called the monsoon
forests.
They spread over regions which receive rainfall
between 70-200 cm. Teak, sal, sheesham, hurra, mahua,
amla, semul, kusum and sandalwood etc. are the main
species of these forests.
24. Tendu, palas, amaltas, bel, khair, axlewood
species are commonly found in, which of the
following forests of India?
(a) Tropical Thorn forests (Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)
(b) Montane forests
(c) Tropical Dry Deciduous forests
(d) Swamp forests

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Match the given lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Altitude ) List II (Forests) A. Foothills of Himalayas 1. Wet Temperate Forests B. 1000-2000 m 2. Deciduous Forests C. 1500-1750 m 3. Pine Forests D. 2200-3000 m 4. Temperate Grasslands
Codes A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
The Himalayan ranges shows a succession of vegetation
from the tropical to the tundra, which change in with
the altitude.
Deciduous forests are found in the foothills of the
Himalayas. Deciduous forest is succeeded by the wet
temperate type of forests between an altitude of
1,000-2,000 m.
Between 1,500-1,750 m, pine forests are also
well-developed in this zone, with Chir pine as a very
useful commercial tree.
Blue pine and spruce appear at altitudes of 2,225-3,048 m
along with Temperate grasslands.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to various species found in the Himalayan region?

answerOptions.text: Chir pine species is used for obtaining wood for commercial purpose.
Deodar is an endemic species used in construction activities and is common in Western Himalayas.
Chinar and Walnut are used in the Handicrafts industry of Kashmir region.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (a), (b) and (c) are correct
with reference to various species found in Himalayan

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Alpine vegetation found in Himalayas.
1. These forests are found at an altitude of 3000-4000 m in the Himalayas.
2. Tribes such as Gujjars, Bhotiyas and Bakarwals practise transhumance in this region.
3. Rhododendron, juniper and pines are common species of this region.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
with reference to the Alpine vegetation found in
Himalayas. In the higher reaches of Himalaya, there
are Alpine forests and pastures.
Silver firs, junipers, pines, birch and rhododendrons, etc.,
occur between 3,000-4,000 m. However, these pastures
are used extensively for transhumance by tribes like the
Gujjars, the Bakarwals, the Bhotiyas and the Gaddis.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Shola forests, which are temperate forests of Montane region, are most commonly found in,
which of the following regions?

answerOptions.rationale:
Shola forests are most commonly found in
Western Ghats. The Southern mountain forests include
the forests found in three distinct areas of Peninsular
India viz; the Western Ghats, the Vindhyas and the
Nilgiris.
As they are closer to the tropics, and only 1,500 m
above the sea level, vegetation is temperate in the
higher regions, and subtropical on the lower regions of
the Western Ghats, especially in Kerala, Tamil Nadu
and Karnataka. The temperate forests are called Sholas
in the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Mangrove forests in India.
1. This type of vegetation grows well along the coast in salt marshes, tidal creeks and estuaries.
2. The Sundari tree found in mangrove region cannot survive in soils with high salinity.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Only statement (2) is incorrect with reference to
Mangrove forests in India. Mangroves grow along the
coasts in the salt marshes, tidal creeks, mud flats and
estuaries.
Sundari is the dominant mangrove tree species of the
Sundarbans of India and Bangladesh. Hence, we can
conclude that the Sundari tree found in Mangrove
region can survive in soils with high salinity.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Mangrove forests are not found in which of the following regions of India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Mangrove forests are not found in Lakshadweep
Islands. Lakshadweep Islands consists of coral reefs
and palm trees. In India, the mangrove forests
spread over 6,740 km 2 , which is 7% of the world’s
mangrove forests. They are highly developed in the
Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Sundarbans of
West Bengal. Other areas of significance are the
Mahanadi, the Godavari and the Krishna deltas.

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect regarding the State of

33. The highest mangrove cover is found in West

(a) Tamil Nadu (Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Gujarat (1177 sq km) has the second largest

answerOptions.text: Very dense forests constitute 13% of the forest cover of India.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to social forestry.
1. It aims to protect forests and promote afforestation on barren lands of the country.
2. It aims to promote agro forestry in rural areas for both tree plantations and agriculture crops.
3. Community forestry, which aims to plant trees on public lands such as village pastures is not included in social forestry.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to
social forestry because community forestry is a part of
social forestry, it involves the raising of trees on
public or community land such as the village pasture
and temple land, roadside, canal bank, strips along
railway lines, and schools etc. Community forestry
programme aims at providing benefits to the
community as a whole. Community forestry provides
a medium under which the people of landless classes
can associate themselves in tree raising and thus, get
those benefits, which otherwise are restricted for
landowners.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements correctly defines farm forestry?

answerOptions.text: Planting ecologically friendly crops on farms to protect soil moisture.
Protecting soil moisture by covering it with farm residue.
Planting tree belts for commercial purposes on the margins of agriculture fields.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) correctly defines farm forestry.
Farm Forestry is the process of planting tree belts for
commercial purposes on the margins of agriculture
fields.
Forest departments of various states distribute
seedlings of trees free of cost to small and medium
farmers. Several lands such as the margins of
agricultural fields, grasslands and pastures, land
around homes and cow sheds may be used for raising
trees under non-commercial farm forestry.

answerOptions.text: Promoting eco-friendly techniques in exploitation of forest resource.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-X, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Natural Resources ) (Basis of Classification) A. Biotic and Abiotic Resources 1. On the basis of origin B. Potential and Developed 2. On the basis of Resources ownership C. Individual and Community 3. On the basis of status owned Resources of development D. Renewable and 4. On the basis of Non-renewable Resources exhaustibility
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4.
Biotic and Abiotic resources are classified on the basis of
origin. Example of Biotic resources are animals, birds,
plants etc and Abiotic resources are water, air, soil,
sunlight.
Potential and Developed resources are classified on the
basis of status of development. Potential resources are
those resources, which are found in a region, but have
not been utilised. Developed resources are those
resources, which are surveyed and their quality and
quantity have been determined for utilisation.
Individual resources and community owned resources are
resources based on ownership. Individual resources are
also owned privately by individuals. Community owned
resources are resources which are accessible to all the
members of the community privately by individuals.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to various landuse categories in India?

answerOptions.text: Expansion of secondary and tertiary activities would lead to increase in the ‘Land put to Non-agriculture Uses’.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is correct with reference to various
landuse categories in India.
Land under rural and urban settlements and for
infrastructure such roads, canals, industries, shops etc.,
are included in the category of Land put to
Non-agricultural Uses.
Thus, it can be concluded that an expansion in the
secondary and tertiary activities would lead to an
increase in ‘Land put to Non-agricultural Uses’.
Statements (b) and (c) are incorrect because areas
under Permanent pastures and grazing lands are owned
by the village ‘Panchayat’ or the Government. Any land,
which is left fallow for more than 5 years is known as
culturable wasteland.

answerOptions.text: Areas under Permanent pastures and Grazing lands are owned by the Central Government.
Any land which is left fallow for more than 1 year is known as culturable wasteland.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect
with reference to landuse in India?

answerOptions.text: Land pastures and grazing lands shows an increasing trend due to increase in area under Agriculture activities.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect with reference to
landuse in India. Area under Permanent Pastures and
Grazing Lands are owned by the village ‘Panchayat’ or
the Government. Only a small proportion of this land is
privately owned. The land owned by the village
panchayat comes under ‘Common Property Resources’.

answerOptions.text: Agriculture land is generally used for non-agriculture purposes when there is a shift in the economy from Primary to Secondary and Tertiary sectors.
Net area sown in India will show an increasing trend when culturable wasteland will be cultivated.

Cotton and sugarcane being one of the major cash crops
in India are produced intensively, but due to good

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Soil erosion and deforestation over a long period may convert an arable land into a wasteland.
India has largest land under Plain areas as compared to Mountains and plateaus.
The net sown area in India is similar in all the states, excluding the North- Eastern states.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (b) are correct because, in the
long term, soil erosion by rivers, wind and waves and
human deforestation turn arable land into a barren
land. In India, 43% of the total land area is covered
under plains land, and 30% of the area is covered under
mountains.
Statement (c) is incorrect because the total sown area in
India is different in all the states except the
North-Eastern state.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect with reference to water resource in India?

answerOptions.text: India accounts for almost 4% of water resources on Earth.
The total utilisable water resources in India are 1123 cubic km.
Only 60% of surface water in India can be utilised.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect with reference to water
resources in India. There are four major sources of
surface water i.e., rivers, lakes, ponds and tanks. In the
country, there are about 10,360 rivers and their
tributaries longer than 1.6 km each.
However, due to topographical, hydrological and other
constraints, only about 690 cubic km i.e., 32% of the
available surface water can be utilised.

answerOptions.text: Water resources of Ganga, Brahmaputra and Barak river account for 60% of total water resources of the country.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class X, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2021)

With reference to the water on the planet Earth,
consider the following statements. 
1. The amount of water in the rivers and lakes is more than amount of groundwater.
2. The amount of water in polar ice caps and glaciers is more than the amount of groundwater.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct as 69% of freshwater,
resides in glaciers and 30% of is underground. Polar ice
caps and glaciers has more water than groundwater.
Statement (1) is incorrect because the out of total
freshwater, less than 1% is located in lakes, rivers and
swamps. Thus, the amount of water in rivers and lakes is
less than amount of groundwater.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to utilisation of water resources in India?

answerOptions.text: Industries account for the highest share of groundwater utilisation in India.
Agriculture sector accounts for the highest share of surface water utilisation in India.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is correct with reference to
utilisation of water resources in India. Agriculture
sector accounts for most of the surface and groundwater
utilisation, it accounts for 89% of the surface water and
92% of the groundwater utilisation.
Statements (a) and (c) are incorrect because agriculture
sector accounts for most of the surface and groundwater
utilisation. Industrial sector is limited to 2% of the
surface water utilisation. The share of industrial sector is
lower in the surface water utilisation as compared to the
household sector. The share of domestic sector is higher
i.e., 9% in surface water utilisation.
13. Which of the following river basin has the lowest
groundwater resources among others?
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)
(a) Narmada (b) Kaveri
(c) Krishna (d) Mahanadi
Ans. (d)

Exp.
Mahanadi river basin has the lowest groundwater
resources than the Narmada, Kaveri and Krishna rivers.
The Mahanadi river system is the third largest of
Peninsular India after Godavari and Krishna, and the
largest river of Odisha state. It rises from Bastar hills in
the state of Chhattisgarh to the South of Amarkantak.

answerOptions.text: The share of industrial sector is higher in the surface water utilisation as compared to the household sector.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to degradation of groundwater resources in India.
1. Intensive irrigation in Punjab and Haryana has led to increase in salinity of soils in these regions.
2. Groundwater is affected by concentration of fluoride in Maharashtra and Rajasthan.
3. The Groundwater in West Bengal and Bihar is severely affected by Uranium concentration in the groundwater.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct. Western Uttar
Pradesh is increasing salinity in the soil and depletion
of groundwater irrigation. In Punjab, Haryana and
Western Uttar Pradesh, more than 85% of their Net
Sown Area (NSA) is under irrigation.
In fact, over withdrawals in some states, like Rajasthan
and Maharashtra, has increased fluoride concentration
in groundwater. Groundwater is affected by
concentration of fluoride in the states like Rajasthan and
Maharashtra.
Statement (3) is incorrect because the groundwater in
West Bengal and Bihar is severely affected by arsenic
concentration in the groundwater.
Water Conservation

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements correctly defines watershed management?

answerOptions.text: Reuse and recycling of waste water through technological intervention.
Disinfection of sewage water so that it can be used again for non-important purposes.
Efficient management and conservation of all the natural and human resources within a watershed.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) correctly defines watershed
management. It includes conservation, regeneration
and judicious use of natural (like land, water, plants and
animals) and human resources within a watershed.
Watershed management basically refers to efficient
management and conservation of surface and
groundwater resources.

answerOptions.text: Efficient management of only the groundwater resources in a watershed.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following pair is/are matched correctly? Water Conservation Program Region

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (c) is correctly matched because Arvary Pani
Sansad in Alwar, Rajasthan have taken up constructions
of various water-harvesting structures such as
percolation tanks; dug out ponds, check dams etc,
through people’s participation.
Pairs (a) and (b) are incorrect because Haryali is a

Central government, which aims at enabling the rural

Neeru-Meeru (Water and You) programme is related to

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following techniques is/are mainly used in rainwater harvesting?
1. Storage of rainwater in natural ponds and lakes.
2. Construction of underground tanks and tankas for capturing rainwater.
3. Storing rainwater in lands having depleted coal seams.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Techniques mentioned in statements (1) and (2) are
mainly used in rainwater harvesting because traditional
rainwater harvesting in rural areas is done by using
surface storage bodies, like lakes, ponds, irrigation
tanks, etc. Rainwater harvesting is a method to capture
and store rainwater for various uses.
In Rajasthan, rainwater harvesting structures locally
known as Kund or Tanka (a covered underground tank)
are constructed near or in the house or village to store
harvested rainwater. The most common storage devices
for harvesting rainwater are tanks.
Statement (3) is incorrect because rainwater harvesting is
not stored in coal-deficient lands.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-X, New NCERT)

Man-made structures locally known as kuls, guls, khadins etc are constructed for which of the following purpose in various parts of India?

answerOptions.text: Storage of minor forest produce by the tribal people to protect it from wild animals.
Storage of food grains such as wheat and rice in local godowns for using them in times of high inflation.
Capture and storage of rainwater during the monsoon season for the purpose of rainwater harvesting.
answerOptions.rationale:
Man-made structures locally known as kuls, guls,
khadins, etc are constructed for capture storage of
rainwater during the monsoon season for the purpose
of rainwater harvesting. In hill and mountainous
regions, people built diversion channels like the guls
or kuls during the monsoon season for the purpose of
rainwater harvesting in the Western Himalayas.
In arid and semi-arid regions, agricultural fields were
converted into rain fed storage structures that
allowed the water to stand and moisten the soil like the
Khadins in Jaisalmer and ‘Johads’ in other parts of
Rajasthan.

answerOptions.text: Locally developed cold storage for storing recently harvested horticulture produce for a temporary period.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following states has the largest share of its agricultural land under irrigation in India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Punjab has the largest share of its agricultural land
under irrigation in India. About 98.1% of agriculture
land in Punjab is covered under irrigation. About 87.6%
of agriculture land in Haryana is covered under
irrigation. Haryana is the second largest share of its
agricultural land under irrigation in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to livestock in India?

answerOptions.text: The population of Buffalo is 21 % of total livestock population in India.
Yaks constitutes the lowest share of livestock in India.
Uttar Pradesh accounts for the largest share of livestock in the country.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct with reference to
livestock in India. The population of Buffalo is 20.45 %
of total livestock population in India. The other
livestock including mithun, yak, horses, ponies, mule,
donkeys, and camel together contribute around 0.23%
of the total livestock. Yaks constitute the lowest share of
livestock in India. Uttar Pradesh accounts for the
largest share (67.8 million) of livestock in the country.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect with reference to fisheries in India?

answerOptions.text: Largest share of fisheries production is obtained from Inland fishing as compared to deep sea fishing.
Fisheries cannot be practised in Brackish water ecosystems in India.
India accounts for the largest fish production in the world.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are incorrect with reference to
fisheries in India. The largest share of fisheries
production is obtained from deep sea fishing as
compared to inland fishing.
Fisheries can be practised in Brackish, river, ocean and
wetlands water ecosystems in India. China accounts for
the largest fish production in the world.
47. Which of the following factors provide a natural
potential advantage to India in the development
of fisheries?
(Chap 6, Class-X, Old NCERT)
1. Wider continental shelf on the East coast.
2. A huge exclusive economic zone of 2 million sq.
km.
3. Huge discharge of nutrients by the rivers draining
in the Bay of Bengal.
Codes
(a) 2 and 3 (b) Only 2
(c) Only 3 (d) All of these
Ans. (d)

Exp. All the given factors provide a natural potential
advantage to India in the development of fisheries.
The wider continental shelf on the East coast, A huge
exclusive economic zone of 2 million km2 and huge
discharge of nutrients by the rivers draining in the Bay
of Bengal factors provide a natural potential advantage
to India in the development of fisheries.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to mineral belts of India?

answerOptions.text: The South-Western plateau has the largest occurrence of copper in the country.
The Dharwar rocks of North-Western region consists of high grade petroleum.
Mica, bauxite and iron ore mostly occur in the North-Eastern plateau region of India.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct with reference to mineral
belts of India. The North-Eastern Plateau Region belt
covers Chhota Nagpur (Jharkhand), Odisha Plateau,
West Bengal and parts of Chhattisgarh. The North-
Eastern Plateau Region belt has variety of minerals viz.
iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.
Statements (a) and (b) are incorrect because the
North-Western Region has the largest occurrence of
copper in the country. High grade crude petroleum
occurs in sedimentary rocks of the tertiary period.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following is not a ferrous mineral?

answerOptions.rationale:
Tin is not a ferrous mineral. Non-ferrous minerals
are those which do not contain iron in the oxidation.
Tin is a type of non-ferrous minerals. Non-ferrous
metals include aluminium, copper, lead, nickel, tin,
titanium and zinc.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to minerals in India.
1. Himalayan belt of India consists of copper, zinc, cobalt and lead.
2. Most of the building stones such as granite, marble and gypsum are found in Rajasthan.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to minerals in India.
The Himalayan belt is important mineral belt in India,
where copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten are known
to occur. They occur on both the Eastern and Western
parts. The North-Western Region belt extends along
Aravali region in Rajasthan and part of Gujarat.
Rajasthan is rich in building stones i.e. sandstone,
granite, marble. Gypsum and Fuller’s Earth deposits are
also found in Rajasthan.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are incorrect
with reference to iron ore in India?

answerOptions.text: Only the haematite ore of iron occurs in India.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect with reference to iron
ore in India. India is endowed with fairly abundant
resources of iron ore. India has the largest reserve of
iron ore in Asia. The two main types of ore found in
India are Haematite and Magnetite. It has great demand
in international market due to its superior quality.

answerOptions.text: In Odisha, iron ore occurs in a series of hill ranges in Sundergarh, Mayurbhanj and Jhar.
India consists of the largest reserves of iron ore in Asia.
More than 90% of iron ore reserves are found in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Goa.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following is not one of the belts of iron ore deposits in India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Ludhiana-Delhi-Kanpur belt is not considered as
the belts of iron ore deposits in India. Odisha-Jharkhand
belt, Durg-Bastar-Chandarpur belt, Bellary-Chitradurga
Chikkamagaluru-Tumkur belt and Maharashtra-Goa
belt are important iron ore belts in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to iron ore production in India?
1. The largest reserves of iron ore are found in India.
2. Odisha is the largest producer of iron ore in India.
3. Iron ore mines in India lie in close proximity to the coal fields and Iron and steel plants.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to iron ore production in India. Odisha is the largest
producer of iron ore in India. In Odisha, iron ore
occurs in a series of hill ranges in Sundergarh,
Mayurbhanj and Jhar regions.
The important iron ore mines are Gurumahisani,
Sulaipet, Badampahar, Kiruburu and Bonai. The iron
ore mines occur in close proximity to the coal fields in
the North-Eastern plateau region of the country which
adds to their advantage.
Statement (1) is incorrect because the largest reserves
of iron ore are found in Australia.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following iron ores is mined at Bailadila? (CGPSC Pre 2017)

answerOptions.rationale:
Haematite is an iron ore, which is mined at
Bailadila. It is located in Dantewada district of
Chhattisgarh. Haematite is a high quality iron ore
which is mainly found in the states of Chhattisgarh,
Jharkhand, Odisha, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Manganese ore?
1. It forms an important component of raw materials used for smelting of iron ore.
2. Manganese deposits are usually associated with Gondwana deposits.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to
manganese ore. Manganese is an important raw
material for smelting of iron ore and also used for
manufacturing Ferro alloys.
Statement (2) is incorrect because manganese deposits
are found in almost all geological formations. However,
it is mainly associated with Dharwar system.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-X, New NCERT)

Manganese forms an important component in raw materials used in which of the following industries?

answerOptions.rationale:
In synthetic paint and insecticide industries
manganese forms an important component in raw
materials used.
Manganese is mainly used in the manufacturing of steel
and ferro-manganese alloy. Nearly 10 kg of manganese
is required to manufacture one tonne of steel. It is also
used in manufacturing bleaching powder, insecticides
and paints.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to production of bauxite in India.
1. In India, largest deposits of bauxite occurs in the Dharwar rock systems.
2. Jharkhand is the largest producer of bauxite in India.
3. Most of the bauxite is found in the laterite rocks on the plateau or hill ranges of Peninsula.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are incorrect with
reference to bauxite production in India. Bauxite is
found mainly in tertiary deposits and is associated with
laterite rocks occurring extensively either on the
plateau or hill ranges of peninsular India.
Odisha is the largest producer of bauxite. Kalahandi
and Sambalpur regions are the leading producers in
Odisha.
16. Which of the following Indian states are not a
major bauxite deposits site?
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)
(a) Jharkhand (b) Maharashtra
(c) West Bengal (d) Madhya Pradesh
Ans. (c)

Exp.
Major bauxite deposits are not found in West
Bengal. Bauxite is found mainly in tertiary deposits and
is associated with laterite rocks.
Major bauxite deposits are found in Gujarat,
Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given pairs is/are correctly
matched? List I List II (Bauxite reserves) (States)
1. Amarkantak plateau Chhattisgarh
2. Jamnagar Gujarat
3. Katni-Jabalpur Madhya Pradesh
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given pairs are correctly matched.
The Maikalu range of Bilaspur and Surguja regions of
Amarkantak plateau are bauxite rich deposits of
Chhattisgarh. In Madhya Pradesh, the Katni-Jabalpur
region and Maikalu range in Shahdol are famous for its
bauxite deposits.
Gujarat, the second largest producer of bauxite in India
have its bauxite deposits in the district of Jamnagar.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following region do not contain any reserves of copper in India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Kalol region of Gujarat do not contain any
reserves of copper in India. Copper is an indispensable
metal in the electrical industry for making wires and
electric motors.
The copper deposits mainly occur in Singhbhum district
in Jharkhand, Balaghat district in Madhya Pradesh and
Jhunjhunu and Alwar districts in Rajasthan.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

In which district of Chhattisgarh, Bauxite ore is available? (CGPSC Pre 2019)

answerOptions.rationale:
Bauxite ore is available in Kondgaon district of
Chhattisgarh. Bauxite is the ore, which is used in
manufacturing of aluminium. Bauxite is found mainly in
tertiary deposits and is associated with laterite rocks
occurring extensively either on plateau or hill ranges of
Peninsular India.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2004)

Which of the following states is the largest producer of Mica in India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of mica in
India. Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh is famous for
its mica production, Nellore district produces the best
quality mica. Mica is mainly used in the electrical and
electronic industries.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to limestone production in India?

answerOptions.text: Limestone occurs in association with rocks composed of calcium carbonates.
It is used in iron ore smelting and cement industry.
It occurs in the sedimentary rock formations.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct with reference
to limestone production in India. Limestone is found in
association with rocks composed of calcium carbonates
or calcium and magnesium carbonates.
Limestone is the basic raw material for the cement
industry and essential for smelting iron ore in the blast
furnace. It is found in sedimentary rocks of geological
formations.
Conventional Resources

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are incorrect
with reference to coal deposits in India?
1. Bituminous coal forms the largest deposits of coal in India.
2. More than 80% of coal in India is of coking grade,
which can be used in the production of steel.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to coal
deposits in India because more than 80% of coal in India
is of non-coking grade. Coal is mainly used in the
generation of thermal power and smelting of iron ore.
Bituminous coal forms the largest deposits of coal in
India.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2019)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Coalfields) List II (Location) A. 1. Talcher Damodar Valley B. 2. Karanpura Son Valley C. 3. Singrauli Godavari Valley D. 4. Singareni Mahanadi Valley
Codes A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.
Talcher coalfield is the largest repository of power
grade coal in India. It occupies a basin in the
South-Eastern part of Mahanadi valley belt of
Gondwana Basin. It is mainly located in Anguly district
of Odisha.
North Karanpura coalfield is located in Chatra, Ranchi,
Hazaribagh and Chatra district in Jharkhand. Damodar
valley region consists of Gondwana coal.
Singrauli coalfied is spread across the districts of
Singrauli and Sonbhadra in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar
Pradesh. It is mostly located in basin of Son valley (Son
river).
Singareni coalfield is located in the Godavari valley of
Telangana. It is jointly owned by Telangana
government and Union government.

questions.question:

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to uranium exploration in India?
1. Most of the Uranium deposits of India occur in the Dharwar deposits.
2. Uranium mines are located along the Singhbhum copper belt.
3. Uranium can be obtained from the monazite sands
which occur in the coastal regions of India.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to uranium exploration in India. Uranium occurs
naturally in low concentrations in soil, rock and water.
It is a hard, dense, malleable, ductile, silver-white,
radioactive metal. Uranium mineral deposits are occur
in the Dharwar rocks. Geographically, uranium ores are
known to occur in several locations along the
Singhbhum copper belt.
Statement (3) is incorrect as thorium can be obtained
from the monazite sands, which occur in the coastal
regions of India.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to solar power production?
1. Production of Solar power is more efficient than Coal and Nuclear Energy.
2. Kamuthi Solar Power Project is the largest Solar project in India.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to solar power production. Solar thermal
technology has some relative advantages over all other
non-renewable energy sources like coal and nuclear
energy. Solar energy is 7% more effective than coal or
oil based plants and 10% more effective than nuclear
plants. The Kamuthi Solar Power Project is the largest
solar power plant spread over 2,500 acres in Kamuthi
in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following region(s) of India has very high potential for tidal energy production in India?
1. Gulf of Khambat
2. Palk Bay
3. Gulf of Kuchchh
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
In India, the Gulf of Khambhat, Gulf of Kuchchh
in Gujarat on the Western coast, Palk Bay in Southern
India have high potential for tidal energy production in
India. Gangetic delta in Sunderban regions of West
Bengal also provide ideal conditions for utilising tidal
energy.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Geothermal energy is generally produced with the help of which of the following techniques?

answerOptions.text: Trapping the heat energy from the atmosphere.
Producing energy with the help of burning charcoal.
Energy production with the help of magma inside the Earth.
answerOptions.rationale:
Geothermal energy is generally produced with the
help of magma inside the Earth. When the magma from
the interior of Earth, comes out on the surface,
tremendous heat is released. This heat energy can
successfully be tapped and converted to electrical
energy.

answerOptions.text: Energy production by thermal heating of coal.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is not one of the advantages of using bioenergy?

answerOptions.text: Improving economic and social life in rural areas.
Reducing pressure on forests for fuel wood.
Improving groundwater recharge in hilly areas.
answerOptions.rationale:
Improving groundwater recharge in hilly areas is
not one of the advantages of using bioenergy. Bioenergy
refers to energy derived from biological products which
includes agricultural residues, municipal, industrial and
other wastes.

answerOptions.text: Reducing land pollution in rural and urban areas.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to clustered settlements in India?

answerOptions.text: Living area is distinct and separated from the farms.
It forms various patterns such as rectangular, linear radial, etc.
These settlements develop for defence purposes or for conservation of water resources.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct with
reference to clustered settlements in India. The
clustered rural settlement is a compact or closely built
up area of houses. In this type of village, the general
living area is distinct and separated from the
surrounding farms, barns and pastures.
The closely built-up area and its intervening streets
present some recognisable pattern or geometric
shape, such as rectangular, radial, linear, etc. Such
settlements are generally found in fertile alluvial plains
and in the North-Eastern states. These settlements
develop for defence purposes or for conservation of
water resources.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to semi-clustered settlements in India.
1. These settlements are developed due to fragmentation of large compact villages.
2. These settlements are mainly found in Southern India.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Panna, para, palli, nalga and dhani are the terms used for which of the following types of settlements?

answerOptions.rationale:
Panna, para, palli, nalga and dhani are the terms
used for Hamleted Settlements. Hemleted settlements
are settlements, which are fragmented into several
units physically separated from each other bearing a
common name. This segmentation of a large village is
often motivated by social and ethnic factors.
Such villages are more frequently found in the middle
and lower Ganga plain, Chhattisgarh and lower valleys
of the Himalayas.

Delhi, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, Agra
and Nagpur.

Which of the following can be classified as an urban agglomeration?
1. University Campus 2. Railways Colony
3. A Military Cantonment
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
University campus, railway colony and military
cantonment can be classified as an urban
agglomeration. An urban agglomeration may consist of
any one of the following three combinations
A town and its adjoining urban outgrowths.
Two or more contiguous towns with or without their
outgrowths.
A city and one or more adjoining towns with their
outgrowths together forming a contiguous spread.

questions.question:

Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4 and D-3.
Those Towns that are supporting administrative

such as Chandigarh, New Delhi, Bhopal.
Transport Towns are primarily engaged in export and

as Raniganj, Jharia, Digboi, Ankaleshwar, Singrauli, etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-VII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2006)

Environment refers to

answerOptions.text: The natural world of land, water, air, plants and animals that exists around it.
The sum total of conditions, which surround human beings at a given point of time.
The interacting system of physical, biological and cultural elements, which are interlinked.

answerOptions.rationale:
Environment refers to an aggregate of conditions
or surroundings in which living beings (such as
humans, animals and plants live or survive) and
non-living things exists.
Environment is the sum total of conditional, which
surround human beings at a given point of time. It is the
natural world of land, water, air, plants and animals that
exists around it. Also, it refers to the interacting system
of physical, biological and cultural elements, which are
interlinked.

Environment is a basic life support system and provides

make their life better.
