title: Ecology and Ecosystem
subject: Arihant NCERT Quiz - Geography
source_file: Arihant NCERT MCQs India & World Geography

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 1997)

Which among the following statement is incorrect?

answerOptions.text: The working system of environment is governed by Natural laws.
Terrestrial unity is present in the environment elements.
Environment is the reserve of physical resource not the biological resource.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect because environment is
the reserve of physical and biological resources.
Physical reserves are space, land forms, water bodies,
climate, soils, rocks and minerals. They determine the
variable character of human habitat. Biological elements
plants, animals, micro-organism are the biological
resources of our environment.

answerOptions.text: Self-enrichment capacity is inherent in environment.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The environment interact with human life and its economic activities.
2. Species adapt their environment through natural
selection in successive generation.
3. More complex living organisms can communicate through various means.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are
correct. The environment encompasses the interaction
of all living species, climate, weather and natural
resources that affect human survival and economic
activities.
Living organisms under go to grow and reproduce
through natural selection, adapt to their environment in
successive generations. More complex living organisms
can communicate through various means.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect about an ecosystem?

answerOptions.text: It is a system formed by the interaction of all living organisms with their physical and chemical factors.
Transfer of energy and material takes place through the ecosystem.
Ecosystem involves the interdependence among the organisms and dependence on their environment.

answerOptions.rationale:
None of the given statement is incorrect about an
ecosystem. Ecosystem is a system formed by living
beings interacting with each other and their non-living
surroundings in a wide geographical area. Ecosystem
functions include exchange of energy and nutrients in
the food chain. It is important for ecological processes
and regulation of the energy flow, supporting life
systems and providing stability. It involves the
interdependence among the organisms and
dependence on their environment.
2. Which of the following may result in creating
imbalances in the environment and ecosystem?
(Chap 5, Class-VI, Old NCERT)
(a) Silting of river beds and flooding of surrounding
areas.
(b) Rapid increase in the population of a region.
(c) Pollution of water, air and land.
(d) All of the above

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2015)

Which one of the following is the most suitable description of the term ‘ecosystem’?

answerOptions.text: A community of organisms interacting with one another.
That part of the Earth which is inhabited by living organisms.
A community of organisms together with the environment in which they live.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is the most suitable description of
the term ‘ecosystem’.
Ecosystem is defined as the community of organisms
together with the environment in which they live. It is
chain of interactions between organisms and their
environment.

answerOptions.text: The flora and fauna of a geographical area.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following can be considered as a biotic component of the ecosystem?
1. Climate 2. Temperature
3. Phytoplankton 4. Carbon dioxide
5. Primary producers
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) correctly describes the function of
detritus in a food chain. Detritus food chain is the type
of food chain that starts with dead organic materials.
The dead organic substances are decomposed by
microorganisms. The organisms that feed on dead
organic matter or detritus, are known as detritivores or
decomposers. These detritivores are later eaten by
predators.

answerOptions.text: Exp. Phytoplankton and primary producers can be considered as biotic components of ecosystem. The term ‘biotic’ describes a living component of an ecosystem. e.g., plants and animals. Phytoplankton, also known as microalgae, are similar to terrestrial plants as they contain chlorophyll and require sunlight in order to live and grow. Autotrophs or primary producers are organisms that acquire their energy from sunlight and materials from non-living sources. Climate, temperature and carbon dioxide are abiotic components. 5. Which of the following correctly describes the function of detritus in a food chain?
They produce their own food with the help of chlorophyll.
They convert dead organic matter into inorganic substances.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) correctly describes the function of
detritus in a food chain. Detritus food chain is the type
of food chain that starts with dead organic materials.
The dead organic substances are decomposed by
microorganisms. The organisms that feed on dead
organic matter or detritus, are known as detritivores or
decomposers. These detritivores are later eaten by
predators.

answerOptions.text: They provide energy to consumers for their functioning.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding saprophytes?

answerOptions.text: Saprophytes are not a part of graying food chain.
Saprophytes are organisms who feed and live on dead organic material.
They obtain nutrition for their growth through dead organic material.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct regarding
saprophytes.
Saprophytes are part of detritus food chain. They feed
and live on dead organic material. Saprophytes cannot
make their own food. They obtain nutrition for their
growth through dead organic material. Saprophytes
have no leaves, stem or roots, they produce spores and
cannot perform photosynthesis. Mushrooms, molds,
fungi are some of the examples of saprophytes.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

The richest fishing grounds of the world are located in which of the following region in an aquatic ecosystem?

answerOptions.rationale:
The richest fishing grounds of the world are
located in Neritic zone of an aquatic ecosystem. This
zone is the most productive ocean region, as it
supports an abundance of living organisms. The reason
for abundance of fishes in this region is the penetration
of varying amounts of sunlight, which permits
photosynthesis by both planktonic and bottom-dwelling
organisms.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following factors is/are responsible for the efficient growth of terrestrial ecosystems?
1. Rainfall 2. Temperature
3. Sunlight 4. Soil
Codes

(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is/are decomposers in an ecosystem?
1. Zooplankton 2. Bacteria
3. Flagella
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Bacteria and flagella are the decomposers in an
ecosystem. Decomposers are the organisms that are
involved in the process of decomposition of the dead,
both animal as well as plant matter, in the ecosystem.
Major decomposers in the ecosystem include bacteria
and fungi.
Zooplankton are small, aquatic microorganisms which
are present in water bodies.
13. Which of the following statements correctly
defines productivity of an ecosystem?
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)
(a) The rate of formation of new organic matter by the
consumers.
(b) The respiration losses, which have occurred during
production of biomass.
(c) The rate of production of biomass of an autotroph.
(d) None of the above
Ans. (c)

Exp. Statement (c) correctly defines productivity of an
ecosystem. In ecology, productivity is the rate at which
energy is added to the bodies of organisms in the form
of biomass.
It is expressed in units of mass per volume (unit
surface) per unit of time, such as grams per square
metre per day. The productivity of autotrophs, such
as plants, is called primary productivity.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following pairs is/are matched correctly?

answerOptions.text: Xerophyte – Plant that can survive in dry regions
Hydrophyte – Plant surviving in excessive water
Tropophyte – Plant adapting to seasonal variations

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given pairs are correctly matched.
A xerophyte is a plant, which is able to survive in an
environment with low availability of water or moisture
such as deserts etc.
Hydrophyte is a plants that live in water and adjust with
its surroundings. e.g., water lilies and lotus.
Tropophyte is a plant adapted to seasonal variations in
which periods of heavy rainfall alternate with periods of
drought.
16. Consider the following statements about
decomposition.
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)
1. The degradation of detritus into simpler inorganic
substances is known as catabolism.
2. The breakdown of humus into inorganic
substances leads to mineralisation.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are
correct?
(a) Only 1 (b) Only 2
(c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2
Ans. (c)

Exp. Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct about
decomposition. Decomposition is the process of
breaking complex organic matter into simpler inorganic
matter. There are five steps of decomposition. These
are fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification
and mineralisation. Catabolism is the process of
breaking down complex molecules into simpler
molecules. Mineralisation is the process of degradation
of the humus to release inorganic nutrients.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-Xl, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2021)

In the case of which of the following biogeochemical cycles, the weathering of rocks is the main source of release of nutrients to enter the cycle?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given biogeochemical cycles, in case
of phosphorus cycle the weathering of rocks is the main
source of release of nutrients to enter the cycle. The
phosphorus cycle describes the movement of
phosphorus through the lithosphere, hydrosphere and
biosphere. Phosphorus moves in a cycle through rocks,
water, soil and sediments. Over time rain and
weathering cause rocks to release phosphate ions and
other minerals.
Carbon and Nitrogen are Gaseous cycles whereas
sulphur and phosphorus are sedimentary cycles.
Weathering of rocks, erosional runoff and
decomposition of organic materials release nutrients in
the sulphur cycle.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2021)

Consider the following kinds of organisms. 
1. Copepods 2. Cyanobacteria
3. Diatoms 4. Foraminifera
Which of the above are primary producers in the food chains of oceans?

answerOptions.rationale:
Cyanobacteria and Diatoms are the primary
producers in the food chain of oceans.
Cyanobacteria, also called blue-green algae, are
microscopic organisms found naturally in all types of
water. These organisms are primary producers who use
Sunlight to make their own food.
Diatoms are photosynthesising algae. They are primary
producers in oceanic food chain.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following pyramids is always upright and can never be inverted?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given pyramids, the Pyramid of
Energy is always upright and can never be inverted
because energy flow in a food chain is always
unidirectional.
In an ecosystem, food is passed from one trophic
level to the next higher trophic level. This transfer
results in the passage of energy through these
trophic levels and some energy is always lost as heat
in each step to the atmosphere and never goes back to
the Sun.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about ecological pyramids.
1. A trophic level in an ecological pyramid represents a particular species.
2. A given species may occupy one or more trophic level in an ecological pyramid.
3. The pyramid of biomass in a sea is generally inverted.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect about ecological
pyramids because in ecology. A tropic level in an
ecological pyramid represents a group of organisms.
Statements (2) and (3) are correct. The pyramid of
biomass in the sea is inverted because the amount of
biomass is least at the base of the pyramid and the
amount of biomass is maximum at the apex of the
pyramid.
In aquatic ecosystem, the producers are small
organisms with least biomass and the biomass
gradually increase towards the apex of the pyramid.
Thus, the pyramid of biomass of aquatic ecosystems is
inverted in shape.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect with reference to ecological succession?
1. The climax community is innear equilibrium with the environment.
2. Succession results in changes in the composition of various ecosystems.
3. The process of succession and evolution are not parallel with each other.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with respect to
ecological succenion.
The process of succession and evolution are parallel
with respect to time.
Succession is a process which starts in an area where no
living organism are present.
Ecological succession is the process of change in the
species structure of an ecological community over time.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Secondary options is often faster than primary succession.
Primary succession can take place over barren and rocky surface.
Hydrarch succession of plants takes place in wetter areas.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct. In primary
succession, newly exposed or newly formed rock is
colonised by living things for the first time.
In secondary succession, an area that was previously
occupied by living things is disturbed, then re-colonised
following the disturbance.
A hydrarch succession is a form of plant succession that
starts out in shallow water and eventually culminates in
a forest.
24. With reference to food chains in ecosystems,
consider the following statements.
(Chap 15, Class-XI, New NCERT) (IAS Pre 2013)
1. A food chain illustrates the order in which a chain
of organisms feeds upon each other.
2. Food chains are found within the populations of a
species.
3. A food chain illustrates the numbers of each
organism which are eaten by others.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following species is a pioneer species?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, lichen is a pioneer
species. Species that arrive first in a newly created
environment (such as an island rising out of the sea) are
called pioneer species. Fungi and lichen are the most
common pioneer species in primary succession. They
have the ability to break down minerals to form soil and
subsequently develop organic matter.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement most appropriately defines a biosphere?

answerOptions.text: A zone of mixing of all the species on Earth and having life.
A zone of intermixing of living and non-living organisms where human habitations exists.
A bio zone of humans and animals which consists of living organisms.
A zone of contact between land, water and air, where life exists on Earth.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) most appropriately defines a
biosphere. The portion of the universe where all life is
found is called the biosphere. The biosphere is made of
three parts, called the lithosphere (land), atmosphere
(air) and hydrosphere (water).

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XI, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2013)

Which one of the following terms describes not only the physical space occupied by an organism but also its functional role in the community of organisms?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, ecological niche
describes not only the physical space occupied by an
organism but also its functional role in the community
of organisms.
An ecotone is a zone of transition between two
biological communities when the two collide and
merge. Habitat can be defined as the natural
environment of an organism, the type of place in which
it is natural for it to live and grow.

Which among the given statement(s) is/are incorrect about nitrification?

answerOptions.text: Nitrification is a process used for converting the nitrogen available in the atmosphere into usable nitrates.
In the process of nitrification, the second step is oxidation of nitrite to nitrate.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is not a type of biodiversity?

answerOptions.rationale:
Biochemical diversity is not a type of biodiversity.
Biodiversity basically refers to the variability among
living organisms from all sources including terrestrial,
marine and other aquatic ecosystems. This includes
diversity within species, between species and of
ecosystems. There are three types of biodiversity -
genetic diversity, species diversity and ecosystem
diversity. These three levels work together to create the
complexity of life on Earth.

answerOptions.rationale:

taken globally, nationally and locally by organisations of

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the distribution of biodiversity.
1. The biodiversity of tropical regions is more as they had a long evolutionary period of species.
2. Higher solar insolation in the tropical regions has led to higher productivity of the ecosystem.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding distribution of biodiversity.
Tropical environments unlike temperate ones are less
seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable.
Such constant environments promote niche
specialisation and lead to a greater species diversity.
There is more solar energy available in the tropics,
which contributes to higher productivity; this in turn
might contribute indirectly to greater diversity.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/ are correct?

answerOptions.text: A stable community of species has more biodiversity than an unstable community.
Increase in Biodiversity contributes to higher productivity in the ecosystem.
Species richness in an ecosystem leads to higher biodiversity.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct. A stable
community of species has more biodiversity than an
unstable community. David Tilman’s long-term
ecosystem experiments showed increased diversity
contributed to higher productivity. Larger numbers of
species and more even abundances of species lead to
higher species diversity.
7. Consider the following statements with reference

(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)
1. Increase in the biodiversity of a region improves
the cycling of nutrients and energy.
2. Species diversity on Earth is uniformly distributed.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following can be obtained from the biodiversity of a region?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given options can be obtained from the
biodiversity of a region. Biodiversity is known to
provide ecosystem services such as
Pharmaceuticals and medicine are included in

Food and nutrition can be obtain from biodiversity of

questions.question:
(Chap
15, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements correctly defines bioprospecting?

answerOptions.text: Protecting biodiversity for the protection of economic interests.
Exploring molecular, genetic and diversity for making products of economic importance.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) correctly defines bioprospecting.
Bioprospecting is defined as a systematic and organised
search for useful products derived from bio-resources.
It includes plants, microorganisms, animals, etc. that
can be developed further for commercialisation and
overall benefits of the society. For example, the bark of
white willow tree is used to develop aspirin.

answerOptions.text: Preserving the existing biodiversity on Earth for the welfare of mankind.
Protecting and preserving biodiversity for economic and nutritional needs of humans.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following is/are invasive/exotic species which can lead to a decline in biodiversity of a region?
1. Water hyacinth 2. Nile perch
3. Lantana 4. Carrot grass
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Water hyacinth, Nile perch, Lantana and Carrot
grass are the invasive/exotic species that can lead to a
decline in biodiversity of a region.
Invasive species is a living organism, that is not native
to an ecosystem and cassrss hasm.
Invasive weed species like Carrot grass (Parthenium),

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct codes. List I List II (Type of Species) (Name) A. Endangered Species 1. Gangetic Dolphin B. Critically endangered 2. Sangai C. Endemic Species 3. Asiatic Cheetah D. Vulnerable Species 4. Mithun

Which of the following factors has been responsible for the large scale death of vulture species in various regions?

answerOptions.text: Decline in the number of snail, earthworm and rodent species in various regions.
Use of drugs such as diclofenac in livestock.
answerOptions.rationale:

kidney failure, even when given in small doses.
Vulture is exposed to a mortal dose of diclofenac if it

with diclofenac recently.

answerOptions.text: Loss of habitat of vultures due to high rise buildings.
Use of high poles for electricity wires.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to Chiru?

answerOptions.text: Chiru is hunted for shahtoosh in the Tibet region.
It is an endangered species of antelope.
It is used for the purpose of transportation in the high altitude regions.

answerOptions.rationale:

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to biodiversity hotspots.
1. Western Ghats and Himalayas are global biodiversity hotspots in India.
2. India has the largest area under biodiversity hotspot in the world.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Western Ghats and Himalayas are global
biodiversity hotspots in India. India hosts four
biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, the Western
Ghats, the Indo-Burma region and the Sundaland
(includes Nicobar group of islands).
Statement (2) is incorrect because Brazil has the largest
area under biodiversity hotspot in the world.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given countries hosts a Global Biodiversity Hotspot in their territory?
1. Tanzania 2. Australia
3. Indonesia 4. Brazil
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given countries in the question host a
Global Biodiversity Hotspot in their territory. Eastern
Afro-Montane hotspot is in Tanzania. South-Western
Australian region hotspot is in Australia. Western
Sunda is (Indonesia, Malas and Brunei) a global hotspot
region. Brazil’s Cerrado is also a global biodiversity
hotspot region of the world.

questions.question:

The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was adopted in which of the following summits?

answerOptions.text: United Nations Conference on the Environment, 1972
The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development, 1992 (Earth Summit)
answerOptions.rationale:
The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
was adopted on 5th June, 1992 at the 1992 UN
Conference on Environment and Development (Earth
Summit) in Rio de Janeiro and ratified in 1993.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)

The Earth Summit did not propose, which of the following steps for biodiversity conservation?

answerOptions.text: Regulation of international trade in wildlife species.

answerOptions.rationale:
The Earth Summit did not propose ‘introducing
genetically modified species’ as a step for biodiversity
conservation. Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro
in 1992.
Earth Summit 1992 produced the Rio Declaration on
Environment and Development, the Statement of
Forest Principles and Agenda 21. The ‘Earth
Summit’ concluded that the concept of sustainable
development was an attainable goal for all the people of
the world.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-X, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2014)

The most important strategy for the conservation of biodiversity together with traditional human life is the establishment of

answerOptions.rationale:
The most important strategy for the conservation
of biodiversity together with traditional human life is
the establishment of biosphere reserves. The
biosphere reserves help to maintain the biodiversity
and culture of that area. Botanical garden is a
collection of living plants designed chiefly to illustrate
relationships within plant groups. A national park is a
natural park that is used for conservation purposes. It
is created and protected by national governments. A
wildlife sanctuary is an area where animals and birds
can live protected and safe in their natural habitats,
away from poaching or trafficking.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about Project Tiger?
1. Project Tiger was started in 1973 in India by IUCN.
2. Tiger conservation reserves have been established under Project Tiger in many states.
3. It has not improved the population of tigers even after a long period of its implementation.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct with reference to Project
Tiger. Project Tiger is a Tiger Conservation
programme launched in April 1973 by the Government
of India. The various tiger reserves were created in the
country based on the ‘core-buffer’ strategy.
Shivalik-Terai Conservation Unit, North-East
Conservation Unit and Sunderbans Conservation Unit
are some of the tiger conservation reserves. Project
Tiger has been successful in increasing the population
of the tigers. As per 2018 Census report, there are 2967
tigers in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-X, New NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct codes. List I List II (Protected Area) (Located in) A. Bandipur National Park 1. Madhya Pradesh B. Manas Tiger Reserve 2. Assam C. Bandhavgarh National Park 3. Karnataka D. Corbett National Park 3. Uttarakhand
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4.
Bandipur National Park It has the second highest tiger
population in India. It is located in Karnataka.
Manas National Park It is a national park, UNESCO
Natural World Heritage site, a Project Tiger reserve,
an elephant reserve and a biosphere reserve in Assam.
Bandhavgarh National Park It is spread at Vindhya hills
in Madhya Pradesh.
Corbett National Park It is located in Nainital,
Uttarakhand. It is regarded as first national park in
India. It was established in 1936.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to biosphere reserves in India?

answerOptions.text: Sunderbans was the first biosphere reserve to be established in India.
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is located in Manipur.
The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is a marine biosphere reserve located in the Indian Ocean.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct with reference to
biosphere reserves in India. The Gulf of Mannar, the
first marine biosphere reserve is located in the South
and South-East Asia of Indian Ocean. In India, the Gulf
of Mannar region in Tamil Nadu is one of the four
major coral reef areas. The Gulf of Mannar is one of the
biologically richest coastal regions in all of mainland of
India.

answerOptions.text: Biosphere Reserves can be established in India under the Wildlife Protection Act.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given pairs is/are matched correctly?

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (b) is correctly matched as Bharatpur
Bird Sanctuary or Keoladeo Ghana National Park, is
home to the finest birds and faunal species. It is located

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements with reference to global warming is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.text: Increase in greenhouse gases results in erratic changes in the climate.
Global warming results in increase in sea level over a period of time.
Ozone depletion is caused mainly due to global warming.
Carbon dioxide is the largest contributor to global warming among all other gases.

title: Environmental Issues
subject: Arihant NCERT Quiz - Geography
source_file: Arihant NCERT MCQs India & World Geography

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following natural factors is/are responsible for causing climate change?

answerOptions.text: Changes in the Earth’s axial tilt (Milankovitch Cycle)

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given options are natural factors
responsible for causing climate change.
Climate change has been caused by many natural
factors. It includes changes in the sunspot and solar
flares, emissions from volcanoes, variations in Earth’s
orbit and levels of carbon dioxide (CO ). Global climate
2
change has typically occurred very slowly, over
thousands or millions of years.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following can be considered as most probable effects of climate change on humans?
1. Crop failure
2. Severe drought
3. Severe flood
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Crop failure, severe drought and severe flood are
the most probable effects of climate change on humans.
The warmer temperatures associated with climate
change are projected to significantly reduce yields of
the world’s staple food crops. Climate change induced
by increasing greenhouse gases is likely to affect crops
differently from region to region.
Climate change is increasing the levels of water vapour
in the atmosphere and is making water availability less
predictable. This can lead to more intense rain storms
in some areas, while other regions may face more
severe drought conditions, especially during the
summer months.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following international treaty aims to reduce the emissions of harmful greenhouse gases in the environment?

(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to climate change and global warming?
1. The rate of increase in temperature of the Earth has slowed down after 1940.
2. Extreme variability in climate has resulted in devastating droughts in the Sahara region during
1967.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to climate change and global warming.
Global average temperatures got down by about 0.2°C
after 1940 and remained low until 1970, after which
they began to climb rapidly again. Thus, it shows that
the rate of increase in temperature of the Earth has
slowed down after 1940. Climate variability refers
to the climatic parameter of a region varying from its
long-term mean. It has resulted in devastating droughts
in the Sahara region during 1967.
12. In the context of mitigating the impending global
warming due to anthropogenic emissions of
carbon dioxide, which of the following can be
potential sites for carbon sequestration?
(Chap 12, Class-XI, New NCERT) (IAS Pre 2017)
1. Abandoned and uneconomic coal seams.
2. Depleted oil and gas reservoirs.
3. Subterranean deep saline formalities.
Codes
(a) 1 and 2 (b) Only 3
(c) 1 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3
Ans. (d)

Exp. Carbon sequestration is the process of storing
atmospheric carbon dioxide. The potential sites for
carbon sequestration are abandoned and uneconomic
coal seams, depleted oil and gas reserves and
subterranean deep saline formations.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding atmospheric gases?

answerOptions.text: Carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxide gases are mainly emitted from the exhaust of automobiles.
Motor vehicle exhaust emissions are known to contain carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
regarding atmospheric gases. Carbon monoxide and
nitrogen oxide gases are mainly emitted from the
exhaust of automobiles.
Motor vehicle exhaust emissions are known to
contain carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides,
hydrocarbons, suspended particulate matter and a small
amount of sulphur dioxide. It is the major cause of
global warming. Hydrofluorocarbons are man-made
organic compounds, They are frequently used in air
conditioning and refrigerator.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following gases/particles is mainly responsible for causing air pollution?
1. Hydrocarbons 2. PM 2.5
3. Carbon dioxide 4. Nitrogen
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Hydrocarbons and PM 2.5 (Particulate Matters)
are mainly responsible for causing air pollution.
A hydrocarbon is any compound that consists of carbon
and hydrogen atoms. They are organic compounds.
60% of air pollution is caused due to automobiles that
run on hydrocarbon-based fuels.
Fine particulate matter, PM 2.5 is an air pollutant. PM
2.5 are tiny particles in the air that reduce visibility and
cause the air to appear hazy when levels are elevated.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to acid rain?

answerOptions.text: Carbon monoxide in the atmosphere is the main constituent of acid rain.
Acid rain damages the agriculture crops due to the reaction of hydrogen sulphate with water vapour.
Sulphur dioxides and nitric oxides are mixed in rainwater to form acid rain.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is correct with reference to acid
rain. Acid rain results when sulphur dioxide (SO ) and
2
nitrogen oxides (NOx) are emitted into the atmosphere
and transported by wind and air currents. The SO and
2
NOx react with water, oxygen and other chemicals to
form sulphuric and nitric acids.
6. Which of the following is/are the most probable
effects of acid rain on human and natural
ecosystem?
(Chap 11, Class-IX, Old NCERT)
(a) Damage to rainforests
(b) Decline in productivity of fishes
(c) Respiratory diseases
(d) Both ‘a’ and ‘ b’
Ans. (d)

Exp. Among the given options, damage to rainforests
and decline in productivity of fishes are the most
probable effects of acid rain on human and natural
ecosystem. Acid rain can be extremely harmful to
forests. Acid rain also causes aluminium to be released
into the soil, which makes it difficult for trees to take up
water. High concentrations of dissolved aluminium
released from soils often enter streams and lakes
damaging fish gills and impair respiration.

answerOptions.text: Ozone is a primary pollutants which is responsible for formation of acid rain.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (UPSC Pre 2014)

Which of the following are some important pollutants released by steel industry in India? I. Oxides of sulphur
2. Oxides of nitrogen
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Carbon dioxide
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Important pollutants released by steel industry in
India are oxides of sulphur, oxides of nitrogen, carbon
monoxide and carbon dioxide. In steel furnace, coke
reacts with iron ore, releasing iron and generating CO
and CO gases. Due to use of coal, pollutants such as
2
SOx and NOx are released.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Contaminated water, due to water pollution of rivers and lakes, may have which of the following pollutants?

answerOptions.rationale:
Contaminated water, due to pollution of rivers
and lakes, may contain urea, coliform and arsenic.
Urea contributes to the eutrophication of inland and
coastal waters.
Coliform group is a large collection of different kinds of
bacteria. Which have adverse effect on health.
Arsenic contamination of groundwater is a form of
groundwater pollution which is often due to naturally
occurring high concentrations of arsenic in deeper
levels of groundwater.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is an important measure of measuring the levels of pollution in water bodies. Which of the given types of pollutants can be measured by BOD?

answerOptions.rationale:
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) can be used
to measure organic and biodegradable pollution. It is a
measure of the amount of oxygen required to remove
waste organic matter from water in the process of
decomposition by aerobic bacteria. BOD is used, often
in wastewater-treatment plants, as an index of the
degree of organic pollution in water.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to algal bloom?
1. It is caused due to presence of large amount of nutrients in the water .
2. It involves rapid growth of planktonic algae in the water bodies.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to algal bloom.
An algal bloom is the overgrowth of microscopic
algae or algae like bacteria in fresh, salt or brackish
water. Higher concentrations of these nutrients in
water cause increased growth of planktonic algae and
green plants.
Algal blooms are the result of an excess of nutrients
(particularly phosphorus and nitrogen) into water.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements correctly defines biomagnification in an aquatic ecosystem such as lakes and rivers?

answerOptions.text: The natural ageing of a lake due to large amount of nutrient.
Increase in concentration of toxic substances with the increase in trophic levels.
Accumulation of waste water in the oceans.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to water hyacinth?
1. It grows rapidly in water bodies where there is high level of eutrophication.
2. It causes imbalance in the water bodies.
3. It is an aquatic weed, which is commonly referred to as ‘ Terror of Bengal’.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct with
reference to water hyacinth.
It is a free-floating perennial aquatic plant. Water
hyacinth has a strong capacity to absorb nutrients, heavy
metals and organic pollutants. That is why it causes
imbalance in the water bodies.
It is commonly referred to as ‘Terror of Bengal’. This is
because it hampers the growth of fish and other aquatic
organisms by cutting down the supply of sunlight and
dissolved oxygen in the water bodies.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given factors is/are responsible for causing accelerated eutrophication?

answerOptions.text: Increasing use of fertilisers in agriculture fields.
Discharging industrial waste into water bodies.
Use of phosphates for increasing plant growth.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are the responsible
factors for causing accelerated eutrophication. Runoff
of fertilisers from nearby field to the water body causes
algal bloom which leads to eutrophication.
Sewage and industrial effluents increase the
temperature and BOD of the water body, thereby
causing increased biological activity, leading to
algal blooms. Phosphorus pollution comes from
households and industry including phosphorus-based
detergents.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which the following statements is/are correct
with reference to water pollution in lakes?
1. Thermal wastewater flowing out of electricity generation units causes damage to indigenous flora and fauna in a water body.
2. Increase in nutrients into a lake over a long period of time results in the conversion of lake into land.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to water pollution in lakes. Thermal
wastewater eliminates or reduces the number of
organisms sensitive to high temperature.
It may enhance the growth of plants and fishes in
extremely cold areas but, only after causing damage to
the indigenous flora and fauna. Nutrient-rich lakes with
high levels of productivity are called eutrophic.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given methods cannot reduce the pollution of water in certain water bodies?
1. Treatment of land with the help of natural bacteria and fungi.
2. Chlorine treatment and filtering.
3. Using dry compost toilets.
4. Using Portland cement in construction.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Use of Portland cement in construction cannot
reduce the pollution of water in certain water bodies.
Ecological sanitation is a sustainable system for
handling human excreta, using dry composting toilets.
This is a practical, hygienic, efficient and cost-effective
solution to human waste disposal. Appropriate plants,
algae, fungi and bacteria neutralise, absorb and
assimilate the pollutants. Hence, as the water flows
through the marshes, it gets purified naturally.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are incorrect
with reference to noise pollution?
1. Sounds produced from only high intensity sources can cause psychological distress in humans.
2. Noise Pollution can also cause stress, poor concentration and communication difficulties.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect because noise pollution
can be caused from various sources and not only from
high intensity sources. There can be various sources of
noise pollution such as sounds of vehicles, Bursting of
crackers, loudspeakers at high volume, Air traffic noise,
concentration sites and all sources can contribute to
psychological distress
Solid Waste

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Municipal solid waste generated from households does not include which of the following?

answerOptions.rationale:
Municipal solid waste generated from households
does not include radium and molybdenum. Municipal
Solid Waste (MSW) includes all items from homes and
businesses that people no longer have any use for.
These wastes are commonly called trash or garbage and
include items such as food, paper, plastics, textiles,
leather, wood, glass, metals, sanitary waste in septic
tanks and other wastes. Radium and molybdenum are
examples of radioactive waste.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following techniques can be used to reduce the generation of harmful municipal solid waste in a region?
1. Using polythene and plastic packaging.
2. Transporting solid waste to landfills outside the city.
3. Recycling and reuse of solid material generated by households.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
‘Recycling and reuse of solid material generated
by households’ can be used to reduce the generation of
harmful municipal solid waste in a region. Separating,
recovering and reusing components of solid waste that
may still have economic value is called recycling.
The essence of reuse is that it preserves some or all of
the energy and materials that went into making an item.
Landfills are sites designated for dumping rubbish,
garbage or other sorts of solid wastes.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to e-waste generated by households.
1. It is buried in landfills in huge quantities in the developing countries.
2. Recycling of e-waste involves exposure to toxic substances.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to e-waste generated by households.
e-waste buried in landfills in huge quantities in the
developing countries. Also the Recycling of e-waste
involves exposure to toxic substances.
Electronic waste or e-waste describes discarded
electrical or electronic devices. E-waste contains
chemicals that are harmful to people and the
environment. For example mercury, lead, beryllium,
brominated flame retardants and cadmium.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect regarding solid waste management?

answerOptions.text: Untreated municipal waste will lead to release of toxic biogas over a period of time.
Municipal waste can be converted to energy and compost with the help of suitable technologies.
Solid waste in urban areas can be reduced with the help of organic farming.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect because solid waste
management may be defined as the discipline
associated with the control of generation, collection,
storage, transfer and transport, processing and disposal
of solid wastes.
Most cities and towns in India dispose of their waste
by depositing it in low-lying areas outside the city,
without taking adequate precautions.
Land Degradation and
Desertification

answerOptions.text: Municipal waste may lead to diseases such as diarrhoea and malaria.

title: Sustainable Development
subject: Arihant NCERT Quiz - Geography
source_file: Arihant NCERT MCQs India & World Geography

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which of the following can be considered as the main factor(s) responsible for land degradation?

answerOptions.rationale:
Mining waste, municipal waste and salinity of soil
are the main factors responsible for land degradation.
Mining and its subsequent activities have been found to
degrade the land to a significant extent. Overburden
removal from the mining area results in a very
significant loss of rain forest and the rich top soil.
Discharging of untreated Municipal Solid Wastes
(MSWs) onto land is very widespread in developing
countries. The soil salinisation is a major process of land
degradation that decreases soil fertility.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the given programs is/are associated with conservation of land and forest resources?
1. Chipko Movement
2. Joint Forest Management (JFM)
3. Beej Bachao Andolan
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the programs given in the question are
associated with conservation of land and forest
resources.
Chipko Movement was a non-violent social and
ecological movement by rural villagers particularly
women in India in the 1970s. It aimed at protecting
trees and forests slated for government-backed logging.
Joint Forest Management is a concept of developing
relationships between fringe forest groups and forest
department on the basis of mutual trust and jointly
defined roles and responsibilities for forest protection
and development.
Beej Bachao Andolan was a people’s movement to
conserve indigenous seeds and promote traditional
agricultural practices.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct about sustainable development?
1. The concept of sustainable development was introduced by Brundtland Commission Report in
1987.
2. The report ‘Our Common Future’ promoted the concept of sustainable development for the conservation of our resources.
3. Sustainable development advocates the use of resources keeping in mind the needs of future generation.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct about
sustainable development. The modern concept of
sustainable development is derived mostly from the
1987 Brundtland Commission Report of 1987.
Our Common Future, also known as the Brundtland
Report, was published on October 1987 by the United
Nations through the Oxford University Press.
Brundtland Commission defined sustainability as
“meeting the needs of the present without
compromising the ability of future generations to meet
their own needs”.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-X, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct
with reference to ‘Agenda 21’ for sustainable development?

answerOptions.text: It was signed in the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
It aims to combat environmental damage by global cooperation.
It involves local agendas that are to be drawn by local governments.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct with reference to
‘Agenda 21’ for sustainable development. Agenda 21 is
a non-binding action plan of the United Nations with
regard to sustainable development. It was signed in the
Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
The implementation of Agenda 21 was intended to
involve action at international, national, regional and
local levels.
One major objective of the Agenda 21 initiative is that
every local government should draw its own local
Agenda 21. Its aim initially was to achieve global
sustainable development by 2000. Agenda 21 is
referring to the original target of the 21st century.

title: Disaster Management
subject: Arihant NCERT Quiz - Geography
source_file: Arihant NCERT MCQs India & World Geography

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The concept of sustainable development does not include which of the following?

answerOptions.text: Improving standard of living of the people

answerOptions.rationale:
The concept of sustainable development does not
include increasing use of fossil fuels because it will
threaten the survival of future generation as fossil fuels
are non-renewable resources.
Sustainable development means utilising resources
keeping in mind the future generations. For
sustainable development to be achieved, it is
crucial to harmonise three core elements: economic
growth, social inclusion and environmental
protection.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to earthquake zones in India?
1. National Institute of Disaster Management is formed with collaboration of National Geophysical Laboratory and Geological Survey of India.
2. India is divided into five earthquake zones.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
respect to earthquake zones in India. National Institute
of Disaster Management is formed with collaboration of
National Geophysical Laboratory and Geological
Survey of India, Department of Meteorology and
Government of India. India is divided into five
earthquake zones :
(i) Very high damage risk zone
(ii) High damage risk zone
(iii) Moderate damage risk zone
(iv) Low damage risk zone
(v) Very low damage risk zone.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are not correct about Tsunami waves?
1. Tsunami waves are generated by the force produced by Moon on the Earth.
2. Tsunami waves move at a faster rate near the coast than in the deep ocean.
3. Tsunami waves are generally known as shallow water waves.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is not correct about Tsunami waves.
Tsunamis are giant waves caused by earthquakes or
volcanic eruptions under the sea. The speed of a
tsunami depends on the depth of the water it is
travelling through. Therefore, Tsunami waves move at a
faster rate in the deep ocean than near the coast.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Tsunami waves occur mostly in, which of the following zones?

answerOptions.text: Ring of Fire in the Pacific Ocean
answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Tsunami waves
mostly occur in Ring of Fire in the Pacific Ocean.
The Ring of Fire, also referred to as the
Circum-Pacific Belt, is a path along the Pacific Ocean
characterised by active volcanoes and frequent
earthquakes. Its length is approximately 40,000
kilometres.
It is a long horseshoe-shaped seismically active belt of
earthquake epicentres, volcanoes, and tectonic plate
boundaries that fringes the Pacific basin.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are not correct with reference to landslides?

answerOptions.text: Landslides are caused mainly due to localised factors rather than macro factors.
Geology and geomorphic agents play an important role in the occurrence of a landslide in a region.
Due to the localised occurrence of landslides, it has not been possible to make landslide vulnerability zones.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is not correct with reference to
landslides. A landslide is the movement of rock, earth, or
debris down a sloped section of land. Landslide-zone
maps depict areas with a higher probability of
landsliding.
The major landslide prone areas in India include
the Western Ghats and Konkan Hills (Tamil Nadu,
Kerala, Karnataka, Goa and Maharashtra), Eastern Ghats
(Araku region in Andhra Pradesh), North-East Himalayas
(Darjeeling and Sikkim) and North-West Himalayas
(Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir).

answerOptions.text: Forecasting and monitoring landslides is highly costly.

(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Tropical cyclones.
1. Tropical cyclones are usually confined between 5° North and 5° South of the Equator.
2. The vertical extent of tropical cyclone is about 12-15 km.
3. A tropical cyclone lasts for 2-3 weeks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct with reference to tropical
cyclones. Tropical cyclones are intense low-pressure
areas. The vertical extent of tropical cyclone is about
12-15 km.
Absence of strong vertical wind wedge, which disturbs
the vertical transport of latent heat, is a pre-requisite for
development of tropical cyclone.
Statements (1) and (3) are not correct because Tropical
cyclones are confined to 10° North and 30° South of
Equator. A tropical cyclone doesn’t lasts for more than a
week. Temperate cyclones lasts for 2-3 weeks.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct
with reference to Tropical cyclones in India?

answerOptions.text: Tropical cyclones develop in the months of October and November.
Tropical cyclones mainly occur in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.
Cyclonic circulations often result in Storm surge in the coastal areas.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct with reference to
tropical cyclones in India. In case of the Bay of Bengal,
cyclones mostly develop during the months of October
and November.
Owing to its peninsular shape surrounded by the Bay
of Bengal in the East and the Arabian Sea in the West,
the tropical cyclones in India originate in these two
important locations.
Storm surges are oscillations in the period range of a
few minutes to a few days in water levels in a coastal
or inland body of water.
Floods and Droughts

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to flood?

answerOptions.text: Floods are slow in occurrence as compared to other disasters.
Floods do not occur at all in coastal regions of India.
Floods can be predicted easily as they occur during a particular period of time.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct with reference
to flood. Floods are relatively slow in occurrence and
often, occur in well-identified regions and within
expected time in a year.
Statement (b) is not correct as floods occur commonly
when water in the form of surface run-off exceeds
the carrying capacity of the river channels and
streams and flows into the neighbouring low-lying
flood plains.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Bihar and West Bengal are highly flood prone regions of India.
Some parts of Tamil Nadu experience floods during retreating monsoon season.
Flash floods are responsible for flooding in Gujarat, Haryana and Punjab.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct.
Various states of India face heavy loss of lives and
property due to recurrent floods. West Bengal and
Bihar are among the high flood-prone states of India
due to perennial rivers flowing from the Himalayas.
A flood caused by heavy or excessive rainfall in a short
period of time, generally less than 6 hours. Tamil Nadu
experiences flooding during November - January due to
the retreating monsoon. Gujarat, Haryana and Punjab
are also getting inundated in recent decades due to
flash floods.

(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the given statements is/are correct with reference to drought in India?

answerOptions.text: More than 15% of total geographical area of India is drought prone.
Kutch region falls under the extreme drought prone category.
Jharkhand and Odisha are under severe drought prone category.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements are correct with reference to
drought in India. Out of the total geographical area of
India, almost one-sixth (15%) area with 12% of the
population is drought prone. The areas that receive an
annual rainfall up to 60 cm are the most prone.
The annual rainfall in Kutch is about 48 cm which makes
the region under extreme drought prone category.

(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)
(a) UN has declared 1990-2000 as the decade of Natural
Disaster Reduction.
(b) The National Institute of Disaster Management was
established in 1995.
(c) The first World Conference on Disaster
Management was held in Yokohama, Japan.
(d) All of the above
Ans. (d)

Exp. All the given statements are correct. The United
Nations General Assembly designated the 1990s as the
International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction
(IDNDR).
The First World Conference on Natural Disasters in
Yokohama, Japan from 23rd to 27th May, 1994,
adopted the Yokohama Strategy for a Safer world.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: Intensification of human activities results in increasing vulnerabilities to disasters.
The management of disasters is dependent upon socio-environmental conditions of different regions.
Unscientific land use and man-made pollution have increased the intensity of disasters.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct.
Vulnerability is the human dimension of disasters and is
the result of the range of economic, social, cultural,
institutional, political and psychological factors that
shape people’s lives and the environment that they live
in poverty and inequality, climate change and
variability, unplanned and rapid urbanisation and the
lack of disaster risk considerations in land management
and environmental and natural resource management
has all increased the intensity of disasters.

(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to disaster mitigation in India.
1. Geological Survey of India and National Institute of Disaster Management are responsible for carrying out disaster mitigation in India.
2. The Disaster Management Bill was passed by the Government of India in 2005 with an aim to improve the capabilities of India in Disaster Management.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to disaster mitigation in India.
Geological Survey of India (GSI) relate to creation and
updation of national geo-scientific data and mineral
resource assessment, air-borne and marine surveys.
National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) is a
premier institute for training and capacity development
programs for managing natural disasters in India, on a
national as well as regional basis.
Disaster Management Act, 2005 aims for planning and
implementation of disaster plans to prevent or mitigate
people from disaster-affected areas, to respond and
recover from disaster events.
